129: 5. **HAL response mocking** — Must set `MasterCode` on `CategoryDto` (Required.Always in NSwag)
130: 6. **NSubstitute + ILogger** — Cannot mock `LogError()` directly (extension method); must mock `Log()` with verbose signature
131: 7. **CancellationToken mocking** — NSwag methods have optional CancellationToken; must mock BOTH `Method(arg, Arg.Any<CancellationToken>())` AND `Method(arg)` for NSubstitute to match
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: ## Anti-Pattern Inventory (from audit)
136: 
137: ### Blazor Client Tests
138: - ~40 instances of `Received()` on read operations
139: - Logger mocked but never verified in error paths
140: - 38% service coverage (11/29)
141: 
142: ### Application Unit Tests
143: - IMapper mocked everywhere (mapping logic untested)
144: - `Received(1)` on repository calls (brittle)
145: - Only 4.8% handler coverage (10/207)
146: - HybridCache compilation errors (pre-existing)
147: 
148: ### API Integration Tests
149: - No test data seeding (in-memory DB starts empty)
150: - `SharedType.PerAssembly` — no test isolation
151: - No multi-role auth testing (always Admin)
152: - Only status code assertions (no body validation)
153: - 21% controller coverage (9/43)
154: 
155: ### Persistence Integration Tests
156: - Only 2 tests for 1 repository
157: - No Update/Delete/Filter/Paginate tests
158: - Uses `EnsureCreated()` instead of `Migrate()`
159: 
160: ### Domain Unit Tests
161: - 0% coverage — placeholder only
162: 
163: ---
164: 
165: ## Quick Resume
166: 
167: To continue work on this task:
168: 1. Read this file for current state
169: 2. Read `test-strategy-tasks.md` for remaining checklist
170: 3. Read `test-strategy-plan.md` for overall strategy
171: 4. Start with Phase 1 (anti-pattern fixes) — it has the highest ROI with no new code
172: 5. Then Phase 2 (coverage gaps) — prioritize Domain and Blazor services
````

## File: dev/active/test-strategy/test-strategy-plan.md
````markdown
  1: # Enterprise Testing Strategy — ISLAMU Event Platform
  2: 
  3: **Last Updated: 2026-02-09**
  4: 
  5: ## Executive Summary
  6: 
  7: The ISLAMU Event platform has **946 tests across 7 projects** — a solid foundation, but with significant coverage gaps and some anti-patterns that undermine maintainability. This plan establishes an enterprise-grade testing strategy following the principle of **"Test Behavior, Not Implementation"** to achieve 80%+ meaningful coverage across all layers.
  8: 
  9: ### Current State (946 tests, uneven coverage)
 10: 
 11: | Project | Tests | Coverage | Health |
 12: |---------|-------|----------|--------|
 13: | Event.Application.UnitTests | 143 | ~5% handlers (10/207) | ⚠️ Gaps |
 14: | Event.Architecture.Tests | 24 | ~90% rules | ✅ Strong |
 15: | Event.API.IntegrationTests | 357 | ~70% endpoints | ✅ Strong |
 16: | Explore.Blazor.Client.Tests | 230 | 38% services (11/29) | ⚠️ Gaps |
 17: | Explore.Secrets.UnitTests | 190 | ~85% services | ✅ Strong |
 18: | Event.Persistence.IntegrationTests | 2 | ~5% repos | ❌ Critical |
 19: | Event.Domain.UnitTests | 0 | 0% | ❌ Critical |
 20: 
 21: ### Target State (~1400+ tests, 80%+ coverage)
 22: 
 23: | Project | Current | Target | Delta |
 24: |---------|---------|--------|-------|
 25: | Event.Application.UnitTests | 143 | 200+ | +57 |
 26: | Event.Architecture.Tests | 24 | 35+ | +11 |
 27: | Event.API.IntegrationTests | 357 | 400+ | +43 |
 28: | Explore.Blazor.Client.Tests | 230 | 400+ | +170 |
 29: | Explore.Secrets.UnitTests | 190 | 210+ | +20 |
 30: | Event.Persistence.IntegrationTests | 2 | 64+ | +62 |
 31: | Event.Domain.UnitTests | 0 | 80+ | +80 |
 32: 
 33: ---
 34: 
 35: ## Core Philosophy
 36: 
 37: ### Test Behavior, Not Implementation
 38: 
 39: > "If I refactor the internal logic of a method but the output remains the same, the test MUST NOT fail."
 40: 
 41: **Rules:**
 42: 1. **Assert on outcomes** (return values, state changes, observable side-effects) — never on internal call sequences
 43: 2. **Use `Received()` verification ONLY** when the side-effect IS the behavior (e.g., `CreateAsync()` was called, email was sent)
 44: 3. **Use real DTOs and value objects** — only mock volatile external dependencies (DB, HTTP, file system)
 45: 4. **AAA pattern** (Arrange–Act–Assert) with clear visual separation
 46: 5. **Method naming**: `MethodName_StateUnderTesting_ExpectedBehavior`
 47: 
 48: ### What NOT to Test
 49: - Library internals (NSwag client generation, MediatR pipeline, EF Core queries)
 50: - Auto-generated code (`EventApiClient.g.cs`)
 51: - Simple property getters/setters
 52: - Constructor-only classes with no logic
 53: - Framework behavior (ASP.NET routing, DI container)
 54: 
 55: ### What TO Test
 56: - Business logic and decision branches
 57: - Error handling behavior (what happens when X fails?)
 58: - Data transformation (DTO → Entity, HAL → DTO)
 59: - State management (cache invalidation, auth state)
 60: - Integration points (API responses, DB queries with real data)
 61: - Architecture constraints (layer dependencies, naming conventions)
 62: 
 63: ---
 64: 
 65: ## Technology Stack
 66: 
 67: | Tool | Purpose | Status |
 68: |------|---------|--------|
 69: | **TUnit** | Test framework (async-first, source-gen runner) | ✅ In use |
 70: | **NSubstitute** | Mocking framework | ✅ In use |
 71: | **Bogus** | Fake data generation (via ComponentDataBuilder) | ✅ In use |
 72: | **bUnit** | Blazor component testing | ✅ In use (limited) |
 73: | **NetArchTest.Rules** | Architecture fitness tests | ✅ In use |
 74: | **TestContainers** | PostgreSQL integration tests | ✅ In use (Persistence only) |
 75: | **TUnit Assertions** | `await Assert.That(x).IsEqualTo(y)` | ✅ In use |
 76: 
 77: ### Decision: TUnit Assertions vs FluentAssertions
 78: 
 79: **Decision: Keep TUnit assertions.** The entire codebase uses `await Assert.That(...)` consistently. Switching to FluentAssertions would create inconsistency and a migration burden with zero behavioral benefit. TUnit assertions are async-first and sufficient.
 80: 
 81: ---
 82: 
 83: ## Phase 1: Audit & Fix Anti-Patterns (Week 1)
 84: 
 85: **Goal:** Remove implementation-coupled tests that will break on refactoring.
 86: 
 87: ### 1.1 Remove Over-Mocking in Blazor Client Tests
 88: 
 89: **Problem:** ~40+ instances of `Received(1)` verification on read operations across Blazor service tests.
 90: 
 91: **Before (brittle):**
 92: ```csharp
 93: var result = await _service.GetAllEventsAsync();
 94: await Assert.That(result.Count).IsEqualTo(3);
 95: // ANTI-PATTERN: Tests HOW, not WHAT
 96: await _apiClient.Received(1).GetEventsAsync(1, 100, Arg.Any<CancellationToken>());
 97: ```
 98: 
 99: **After (behavioral):**
100: ```csharp
101: var result = await _service.GetAllEventsAsync();
102: await Assert.That(result.Count).IsEqualTo(3);
103: // Only assert the outcome — implementation is free to change
104: ```
105: 
106: **Keep `Received()` ONLY for:**
107: - Write operations: `Received(1).CreateEventAsync(...)` — the side-effect IS the behavior
108: - Retry logic: `Received(3).SyncUserAsync(...)` — verifying retry count IS the behavior
109: - Logging in error paths: `_logger.Received(1).Log(...)` — if logging is a requirement
110: 
111: **Pagination parameter verification — use outcome-based testing instead:**
112: Instead of `Received(1).GetEventsAsync(1, 100, ...)` (couples test to constants), configure the mock to return different results for different inputs and assert on the output:
113: ```csharp
114: // GOOD: Mock returns specific data for correct pagination, assert outcome
115: _apiClient.GetEventsAsync(Arg.Any<int?>(), Arg.Any<int?>(), Arg.Any<CancellationToken>())
116:     .Returns(halResponse);
117: var result = await _service.GetAllEventsAsync();
118: await Assert.That(result.Count).IsEqualTo(3); // Outcome proves it called the right thing
119: ```
120: 
121: **Files to fix:**
122: - `EventServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on read operations
123: - `CategoryServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on GetAll/GetById
124: - `LocationServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on read operations
125: - `AdminServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on read operations, keep on writes
126: - `OrganizationServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on reads
127: - `OrganizationMemberServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on reads
128: - `OrganizationReviewServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on reads
129: - `EventRegistrationServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on reads
130: - `LandingPageServiceTests.cs` — Remove Received() on reads
131: - `UserServiceTests.cs` — Keep Received() on SyncUser (side-effect), remove on reads
132: 
133: **Acceptance:** All 230 existing tests still pass after changes. No `Received()` on read-only API calls.
134: 
135: ### 1.2 Add Error Logging Verification
136: 
137: **Problem:** Logger is mocked in all tests but never verified. Silent failures go undetected.
138: 
139: **Action:** For every test that exercises an error path (`ThrowsAsync`, returns null), verify that `_logger` received appropriate log call:
140: ```csharp
141: _logger.Received(1).Log(
142:     LogLevel.Error,
143:     Arg.Any<EventId>(),
144:     Arg.Any<object>(),
145:     Arg.Any<Exception?>(),
146:     Arg.Any<Func<object, Exception?, string>>()
147: );
148: ```
149: 
150: **Note:** NSubstitute with `ILogger<T>` requires the verbose `Log()` method signature — not `LogError()` directly (it's an extension method).
151: 
152: **Scope:** Only services that inject `ILogger<T>` and call `_logger.LogError()` / `_logger.LogWarning()` in their catch blocks. If a service doesn't log on error paths, don't add logging verification — add it to the service first if logging is desired.
153: 
154: **Acceptance:** Every error-path test in services that log verifies logging occurred.
155: 
156: ### 1.3 Consolidate Redundant Tests
157: 
158: **Problem:** Many services have separate tests for "returns empty when null" and "returns empty when exception" that are effectively identical from a behavioral perspective.
159: 
160: **Action:** Keep both tests but ensure they test genuinely different behavior. If the service behaves identically, combine using `[MethodDataSource]` or a shared helper:
161: ```csharp
162: [Test]
163: public async Task GetAllEventsAsync_ReturnsEmptyList_WhenApiReturnsNull() { ... }
164: 
165: [Test]
166: public async Task GetAllEventsAsync_ReturnsEmptyList_WhenApiThrowsApiException() { ... }
167: ```
168: 
169: **Decision:** Keep separate — each documents a distinct contract even if implementation is same. They serve as regression guards if error handling diverges later.
170: 
171: ---
172: 
173: ## Phase 2: Fill Critical Coverage Gaps (Weeks 2–4)
174: 
175: ### 2.1 Event.Domain.UnitTests — FROM ZERO (Priority: CRITICAL)
176: 
177: **Current state:** Placeholder file only. 0 tests.
178: 
179: **Domain entities to test (in priority order):**
180: 
181: | Entity | Logic Complexity | Tests Needed |
182: |--------|-----------------|--------------|
183: | Event | HIGH — status transitions, validation | 15-20 |
184: | Organization | MEDIUM — membership rules | 8-12 |
185: | EventSession | MEDIUM — speaker/language composition | 8-10 |
186: | User | LOW — mostly data carrier | 5-8 |
187: | Actor | LOW — type validation | 3-5 |
188: | Tenant | LOW — settings, mode | 5-8 |
189: | Location | LOW — coordinate validation | 3-5 |
190: | StorageObject | LOW — file type validation | 3-5 |
191: 
192: **Test patterns for domain entities:**
193: ```csharp
194: public class EventTests
195: {
196:     [Test]
197:     public async Task Create_WithValidData_ShouldSetDefaultValues()
198:     {
199:         var @event = new Event { Title = "Test", ... };
200:         await Assert.That(@event.IsDeleted).IsFalse();
201:         await Assert.That(@event.CreatedAt).IsNotNull();
202:     }
203: 
204:     [Test]
205:     public async Task SoftDelete_ShouldSetIsDeletedTrue()
206:     {
207:         // Test if domain has soft-delete logic
208:     }
209: }
210: ```
211: 
212: **What to test:**
213: - Entity creation with valid/invalid data
214: - Business rule enforcement (if domain has rich logic)
215: - Enum value mappings (EventTypeEnum → EventType lookup)
216: - Audit field behavior (CreatedAt, UpdatedAt)
217: - Soft delete behavior
218: - Navigation property integrity
219: 
220: **What NOT to test:**
221: - EF Core mapping (that's persistence layer)
222: - Simple property getters/setters
223: - Framework-generated equality
224: 
225: **Acceptance:** 80+ tests covering all entities with logic. `dotnet run --project Event.Domain.UnitTests` passes.
226: 
227: ### 2.2 Blazor Client — 18 Untested Services (Priority: HIGH)
228: 
229: **Services grouped by implementation pattern:**
230: 
231: #### Group A: Simple Lookup Services (10 services, ~5 tests each = 50 tests)
232: 
233: These all follow the same pattern: wrap NSwag client call → parse HAL response → return DTO list.
234: 
235: | Service | API Method | Expected Tests |
236: |---------|-----------|----------------|
237: | EventTypeService | GetEventTypesAsync | 5 |
238: | EventStatusService | GetEventStatusesAsync | 5 |
239: | EventFormatService | GetEventFormatsAsync | 5 |
240: | AudienceAgeService | GetAudienceAgesAsync | 5 |
241: | AudienceGenderService | GetAudienceGendersAsync | 5 |
242: | MadhabService | GetMadhabsAsync | 5 |
243: | LanguageService | GetLanguagesAsync | 5 |
244: | ActorService | GetActorsAsync + CRUD | 8 |
245: | TagService | GetTagsAsync + CRUD | 8 |
246: | PublicExperienceService | GetPublicExperiencesAsync | 5 |
247: 
248: **IMPORTANT:** Not all lookup services are identical. Before writing tests, read each service implementation to determine which pattern it follows:
249: 
250: | Pattern | Services | Tests |
251: |---------|----------|-------|
252: | **HAL collection → DTO list** (with null/exception fallback) | Category, Location, Organization (reference pattern) | 5: success, null, exception, getById, getById-notFound |
253: | **Direct ICollection passthrough** (no HAL, no fallback) | Some lookups return `ICollection<T>` directly from NSwag | 3: success, exception, empty collection |
254: | **Simple one-liner passthrough** (no error handling) | EventType, EventStatus, EventFormat etc. | 2: success, exception (verify service doesn't silently swallow) |
255: | **CRUD (GetAll + Create/Update/Delete)** | Actor, Tag | 8: above + create success, create throws, update, delete |
256: 
257: **Per-service workflow:**
258: 1. Read `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/{Service}.cs` — identify which pattern above
259: 2. Read its interface `I{Service}.cs` — identify all methods to test  
260: 3. Create test file at `Explore.Blazor.Client.Tests/Services/{Service}Tests.cs`
261: 4. Follow `EventServiceTests.cs` constructor pattern (mock `IEventApiClient` + `ILogger<T>`)
262: 5. Write only tests that match the service's actual error handling behavior
263: 6. Do NOT write 5 tests for a 3-line passthrough — match test depth to service complexity
264: 
265: **Optimization:** Create a shared test base or helper to reduce boilerplate across these 10 services.
266: 
267: #### Group B: Complex Services (5 services, ~15 tests each = 75 tests)
268: 
269: | Service | Complexity | Key Behaviors |
270: |---------|-----------|---------------|
271: | LookupCacheService | HIGH | Cache invalidation, thread safety (SemaphoreSlim), expiration |
272: | ImageStorageService | HIGH | Pre-signed URL generation, file validation, upload streaming |
273: | MapsService | MEDIUM | Geolocation parsing, coordinate validation |
274: | TenantOnboardingService | MEDIUM | Multi-step onboarding, state management |
275: | InstanceOnboardingService | MEDIUM | Instance setup, configuration validation |
276: 
277: **LookupCacheService tests (highest priority):**
278: 1. `GetLookupData_ReturnsCachedData_WhenCacheIsValid`
279: 2. `GetLookupData_FetchesFromApi_WhenCacheExpired`
280: 3. `GetLookupData_FetchesFromApi_WhenCacheEmpty`
281: 4. `InvalidateCache_ClearsAllCachedData`

293: #### Group C: Infrastructure Services (3 services, ~10 tests each = 30 tests)
294: 
295: | Service | Complexity | Key Behaviors |

301: **Total new Blazor tests: ~155 tests (50 + 75 + 30)**
302: 
303: **Acceptance:** Service coverage rises from 38% (11/29) to 100% (29/29). All 400+ tests pass.
304: 
305: ### 2.3 Event.Persistence.IntegrationTests — Expand (Priority: HIGH)
306: 
307: **Current state:** 2 tests for EventRepository only.
308: 
309: **Repositories to test:**
310: 
311: | Repository | Tests Needed | Key Operations |
312: |-----------|-------------|----------------|
313: | EventRepository | +10 | Update, Delete, Filter, Paginate, Include |
314: | OrganizationRepository | 12 | Full CRUD, member queries |
315: | UserRepository | 8 | CRUD, tenant-scoped queries |

317: | CategoryRepository | 6 | Hierarchical queries |
318: | TagRepository | 6 | Tag CRUD, type filtering |

321: 
322: **Test patterns:**
323: ```csharp
324: [Test]
325: [ClassDataSource<PostgreSqlContainerFixture>(Shared = SharedType.PerAssembly)]
326: public async Task GetById_ReturnsEntity_WhenExists(PostgreSqlContainerFixture fixture)
327: {
328:     await using var context = fixture.CreateDbContext();
329:     var repo = new EventRepository(context);
330:     // Seed → Query → Assert
331: }
332: ```
333: 
334: **Key scenarios per repository:**
335: 1. Create entity → verify persisted
336: 2. GetById → verify includes/navigation properties
337: 3. Update entity → verify changes persisted
338: 4. Soft delete → verify IsDeleted flag

343: **Acceptance:** 50+ tests covering all repositories. All pass against TestContainers PostgreSQL.
344: 
345: ### 2.4 Event.Application.UnitTests — Fill Gaps (Priority: MEDIUM)
346: 
347: **Current state:** 143 tests covering most handlers.
348: 
349: **Gaps to fill (based on handler inventory):**

359: - Any handler that does conditional logic (not just delegation)

365: ---
366: 
367: ## Phase 3: Architecture & Integration Hardening (Weeks 5–6)
368: 
369: ### 3.1 Expand Architecture Tests
370: 
371: **New rules to enforce:**
372: 
373: | Rule | Description |
374: |------|-------------|
375: | Handler interface compliance | All handlers implement `IRequestHandler<,>` |
376: | Repository interface compliance | All repos implement `IGenericRepository<,>` or entity-specific interface |
377: | Validator base class | All validators extend `AbstractValidator<T>` |
378: | Controller attribute | All controllers have `[ApiController]` and `[Route]` |
379: | No forbidden namespaces | Domain must not reference `System.Net`, `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` |
380: | Sealed classes | Handlers, validators should be sealed (performance) |
381: 
382: **Acceptance:** 35+ architecture tests.
383: 
384: ### 3.2 Blazor Component Tests (bUnit)
385: 
386: **Priority components to test:**
387: 
388: | Component | Test Type | Key Behaviors |
389: |-----------|----------|---------------|
390: | EventList page | Rendering | Loads data, displays cards, handles empty state |
391: | EventDetails page | Rendering | Displays details, handles not-found |
392: | CreateEvent form | Interaction | Form submission, validation, error display |
393: | OrganizationList page | Rendering | Lists orgs, pagination |
394: | Login/Auth flows | State | Auth state changes, redirects |
395: 
396: **Pattern:**
397: ```csharp
398: [Test]
399: public async Task EventList_ShowsLoadingState_Initially()
400: {
401:     using var ctx = new BlazorTestContext();
402:     var cut = ctx.RenderComponent<EventList>();
403:     await Assert.That(cut.Find(".loading-indicator")).IsNotNull();
404: }
405: ```
406: 
407: **Acceptance:** 30+ component tests covering critical UI paths.
408: 
409: ### 3.3 API Integration Test Improvements
410: 
411: **Current gaps in 357 tests:**
412: - Auth bypass may not test real authorization logic
413: - Some tests may be too tightly coupled to response shape
414: 
415: **Actions:**
416: - Audit existing tests for behavioral compliance
417: - Add negative auth tests (unauthorized, forbidden)
418: - Add content negotiation tests
419: - Add rate limiting tests (if middleware exists)
420: 
421: ---
422: 
423: ## Phase 4: Continuous Quality (Ongoing)
424: 
425: ### 4.1 Test Quality Gates
426: 
427: | Gate | Threshold | Enforced By |
428: |------|-----------|-------------|
429: | No `Received()` on read operations | 0 violations | Code review + architecture test |
430: | All error paths verify logging | 100% | Code review |
431: | New services require tests | 100% | PR policy |
432: | Test naming convention | `Method_State_Expected` | Architecture test |
433: | No `#pragma warning disable` in tests | 0 violations | Architecture test |
434: 
435: ### 4.2 CI/CD Integration
436: 
437: ```yaml
438: # Recommended test execution order in CI
439: steps:
440:   - dotnet build --configuration Release --verbosity quiet
441:   - dotnet run --project Event.Architecture.Tests        # Fast, catches structure issues
442:   - dotnet run --project Event.Domain.UnitTests          # Fast, pure logic
443:   - dotnet run --project Event.Application.UnitTests     # Fast, handler logic
444:   - dotnet run --project Explore.Secrets.UnitTests       # Fast, library tests
445:   - dotnet run --project Explore.Blazor.Client.Tests     # Medium, service + component
446:   - dotnet run --project Event.Persistence.IntegrationTests  # Slow, TestContainers
447:   - dotnet run --project Event.API.IntegrationTests      # Slow, WebApplicationFactory
448: ```
449: 
450: ### 4.3 Test Maintenance
451: 
452: - **Monthly:** Review and remove tests that no longer provide value
453: - **Per PR:** Ensure new code has tests, existing tests not broken
454: - **Per Sprint:** Review test execution time, optimize slow tests
455: - **Quarterly:** Run coverage analysis, identify new gaps
456: 
457: ---
458: 
459: ## Risk Assessment
460: 
461: | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
462: |------|-----------|--------|------------|
463: | Over-testing simple lookups | HIGH | LOW | Use shared test bases, don't test library behavior |
464: | Test fragility from mock coupling | MEDIUM | HIGH | Phase 1 anti-pattern removal |
465: | TestContainers CI flakiness | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | Retry policies, container health checks |
466: | Large test suite slowing CI | LOW | MEDIUM | Parallel execution, test categorization |
467: | Domain entities have no testable logic | MEDIUM | LOW | Focus on entities WITH logic, skip pure data carriers |
468: 
469: ---
470:

472: 
473: | Phase | Duration | Tests Added | Cumulative |
474: |-------|----------|-------------|------------|

482: | Phase 3.3: API test improvements | Week 6 | +43 | 1,370 |
483: | **Total** | **6 weeks** | **+424** | **1,370** |

## File: dev/active/unified-search-api-implementation.md
````markdown
 1: the search layer—search is where most flexible architectures either shine or feel "broken" to the user.
 2: 
 3: To reassure you: **Yes, you can have a single, unified, fuzzy search that looks through everything (Title, Description, and JSONB) without building a fragmented mess.**
 4: 
 5: Here is the realistic, high-performance "Search Strategy" for your decentralized implementation.
 6: 
 7: ---
 8: 
 9: # THE SEARCH EXECUTION PLAN: THE "UNIFIED SEARCH SHADOW"
10: 
11: To avoid the performance hit of searching across raw JSONB for every user query, we will use a **Search Shadow Table**. This table acts as a flattened "index" of your entire event, combining relational and JSON data into one searchable record.
12: 
13: ## 1. DATA MODEL: `EventSearchIndex`
14: 
15: Instead of searching the `Events` table directly, create a specialized table optimized for **Full-Text** and **Vector** search.
16: 
17: * **Id:** `Guid` (FK to Event)
18: * **TenantId:** `Guid` (For security filtering)
19: * **SearchVector:** `tsvector` (Standard Postgres Full-Text Search)
20: * **SemanticEmbedding:** `vector(1536)` (Using **pgvector** for AI/Concept search)
21: * **RawContent:** `text` (A flat string of *everything* important: Title + Desc + JSONB Values)
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 2. THE SEARCH MODES (HYBRID SEARCH)
26: 
27: To get the "genius" results you want, the AI Agent should implement a **Hybrid Search** query.
28: 
29: ### A. The "Fuzzy" Keyword Search (Trigrams)
30: 
31: * **Technology:** `pg_trgm` extension.
32: * **How it works:** It breaks words into 3-letter chunks. If a user types "Islma" instead of "Islam," the trigram match (`isl`, `sla`, `lam`) still catches it.
33: * **Target:** `RawContent` column.
34: 
35: ### B. The "Semantic" Vector Search (pgvector)
36: 
37: * **Technology:** `pgvector`.
38: * **How it works:** When an event is saved, the API sends the text to an embedding model (like OpenAI or a local HuggingFace model). It converts the event into a list of numbers (a vector).
39: * **Benefit:** If a user searches for *"Gathering for tech-minded Muslims,"* the vector search will find your event even if those exact words aren't in the title, because it understands the **concept**.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 3. REAL-TIME SYNC LOGIC (NO REDIS NEEDED YET)
44: 
45: You mentioned caching software like Redis. For your scale, **stay inside PostgreSQL** using an **Outbox/Domain Event** pattern. This ensures your search index never drifts from your actual data.
46: 
47: 1. **Event Organizer** saves an event (Relational + JSONB).
48: 2. **MediatR Domain Event** (`EventCreated`) is fired.
49: 3. **SearchIndexer Handler** picks it up:
50: * Flattens the JSONB into a plain text string.
51: * Calls the Embedding API.
52: * Upserts the `EventSearchIndex` table.
53: 
54: 
55: 4. **Result:** The "Search Shadow" is updated in milliseconds.
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 4. REFACTORED PLAN FOR THE AI AGENT
60: 
61: **Command to AI Agent:** "Implement the Unified Search System for the Explore API."
62: 
63: 1. **Enable Extensions:** Ensure `pg_trgm` and `vector` are enabled in the database migrations.
64: 2. **Create Search Table:** Implement the `EventSearchIndex` table with `tsvector` and `vector` columns.
65: 3. **Implement Flattener Service:** Create a service that iterates through the `EventAspects` (JSONB) and extracts only the **Values** (not the keys) into a single large string.
66: 4. **The Search Handler:** Create a MediatR `SearchEventsQueryHandler` that performs a **Hybrid Search**:
67: * Use `pg_trgm` for typo-tolerant keyword matching.
68: * Use `pgvector` for semantic similarity.
69: * **Weighting:** Give the Title a weight of 1.0, the Description 0.6, and the JSONB Aspect data 0.4.
70: 
71: 
72: 5. **Multi-Tenancy:** Ensure every search query includes `WHERE TenantId = @tenantId` to prevent data leakage between communities.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## WHY THIS IS REALISTIC & SAFE:
77: 
78: * **Performance:** By searching a "Shadow Table" instead of raw JSONB, your queries will stay under 100ms even with hundreds of thousands of events.
79: * **No "Sync Pain":** Because the index is in the *same* database as your events, you get **ACID compliance**. You will never have a situation where an event exists in the DB but is "missing" from search because an external sync failed.
80: * **Future Proof:** If you decide to move to a dedicated search engine (like Typesense or Meilisearch) later, you just point the sync worker there. Your core logic doesn't change.
81: 
82: ### The Prediction:
83: 
84: If you implement the **pgvector + Trigram** hybrid, your users will feel like the search "reads their mind." It handles typos perfectly (Trigrams) and it handles "meaning" perfectly (Vectors). This is the gold standard for 2026 API design.
85: 
86: **Actionable Follow-up:**
87: Should I provide the specific SQL and C# `SearchIndex` entity configuration for your AI Agent to follow exactly?
````

## File: docs/ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md
````markdown
  1: # Administrative Hierarchy
  2: 
  3: > **Authority Model and Permission Boundaries**
  4: >
  5: > This document defines the administrative roles, their authorities, and the governance model
  6: > for the platform.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform implements a strict hierarchical authority model that separates infrastructure concerns from business operations. This ensures that SaaS providers, self-hosters, and community administrators each have appropriate control without overstepping boundaries.
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Role Definitions
 19: 
 20: ### Instance Administrator (Super Admin)
 21: 
 22: **Identity**: The organization or individual who operates the physical/virtual infrastructure.
 23: 
 24: **Examples**:
 25: - SaaS platform operator
 26: - IT department running self-hosted instance
 27: - DevOps team managing infrastructure
 28: 
 29: **Authority Scope**:
 30: 
 31: | Area | Can Do | Cannot Do |
 32: |------|--------|-----------|
 33: | **Infrastructure** | Server configuration, scaling, backups | Access tenant business data |
 34: | **Modules** | Enable/disable globally, set restrictions | Use modules within tenants |
 35: | **Tenants** | Create, suspend, archive, purge | Make business decisions for tenants |
 36: | **Policies** | Lock settings, enforce quotas | Override tenant preferences within allowed bounds |
 37: | **Security** | Authentication providers, encryption | Impersonate tenant users |
 38: 
 39: ### Tenant Administrator (Community Admin)
 40: 
 41: **Identity**: The organization or individual who manages a specific community/tenant.
 42: 
 43: **Examples**:
 44: - Mosque administrator
 45: - Event organizer for a community
 46: - Organization leadership
 47: 
 48: **Authority Scope**:
 49: 
 50: | Area | Can Do | Cannot Do |
 51: |------|--------|-----------|
 52: | **Configuration** | Customize allowed settings | Override locked settings |
 53: | **Modules** | Enable from allowed set | Enable globally disabled modules |
 54: | **Users** | Manage membership, roles | Access other tenants' users |
 55: | **Content** | Moderate, publish, archive | Bypass instance policies |
 56: | **Branding** | Colors, logos, themes | Change core UI patterns |
 57: 
 58: ### Organization Administrator
 59: 
 60: **Identity**: A user with elevated privileges within a specific organization entity.
 61: 
 62: **Authority Scope**:
 63: - Manage organization members and roles
 64: - Create and manage events
 65: - Approve registrations
 66: - Respond to reviews
 67: 
 68: ### Standard User
 69: 
 70: **Identity**: Regular platform user within a tenant.
 71: 
 72: **Authority Scope**:
 73: - View public content
 74: - Register for events (if permitted)
 75: - Manage own profile
 76: - Create content (if permitted by policies)
 77: 
 78: ---
 79: 
 80: ## Permission Boundaries
 81: 
 82: ### What Instance Admin CANNOT Do
 83: 
 84: These are hard boundaries protecting tenant autonomy:
 85: 
 86: | Restriction | Rationale |
 87: |-------------|-----------|
 88: | Access tenant business data | Privacy, data sovereignty |
 89: | Read individual user records | GDPR, privacy regulations |
 90: | Modify tenant content | Business autonomy |
 91: | Override tenant business rules | Operational independence |
 92: | Access tenant API tokens | Security isolation |
 93: 
 94: ### What Tenant Admin CANNOT Do
 95: 
 96: These are hard boundaries protecting platform integrity:
 97: 
 98: | Restriction | Rationale |
 99: |-------------|-----------|
100: | Disable enforced security policies | Platform security |
101: | Access other tenants' data | Multi-tenant isolation |
102: | Exceed resource quotas | Fair resource usage |
103: | Enable unapproved modules | Platform consistency |
104: | Modify system tables | Data integrity |
105: 
106: ---
107: 
108: ## Authority Cascade
109: 
110: ### Setting Resolution Order
111: 
112: 1. **System Default** → Baseline value
113: 2. **Instance Policy** → May override or lock
114: 3. **Tenant Configuration** → May override if not locked
115: 4. **User Preference** → May override if delegated
116: 
117: ### Lock States
118: 
119: | State | Instance Admin | Tenant Admin | User |
120: |-------|----------------|--------------|------|
121: | **System Default** | Override ✅ | Override ✅ | Override ✅ |
122: | **Instance Locked** | Override ✅ | Override ❌ | Override ❌ |
123: | **Tenant Locked** | Override ✅ | Override ✅ | Override ❌ |
124: | **User Preference** | Override ✅ | Override ✅ | Override ✅ |
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## Enforcement Policies
129: 
130: ### Policy Types
131: 
132: | Type | Enforced By | Example |
133: |------|-------------|---------|
134: | **Technical** | System code | Authentication required |
135: | **Configuration** | Settings engine | Render mode restrictions |
136: | **Resource** | Quota service | Storage limits |
137: | **Compliance** | Audit system | Data retention rules |
138: 
139: ### Policy Priority
140: 
141: When policies conflict:
142: 1. Legal/Compliance (highest priority)
143: 2. Security policies
144: 3. Instance policies
145: 4. Tenant policies
146: 5. User preferences (lowest priority)
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## Delegation Model
151: 
152: ### Instance → Tenant Delegation
153: 
154: Instance Admin can delegate specific authorities:
155: 
156: | Delegatable | Default | Rationale |
157: |-------------|---------|-----------|
158: | Module selection | ✅ Delegated | Business flexibility |
159: | Branding | ✅ Delegated | Community identity |
160: | User management | ✅ Delegated | Operational need |
161: | Security settings | ❌ Locked | Platform protection |
162: | Payment processing | ⚙️ Configurable | Business model dependent |
163: 
164: ### Tenant → Organization Delegation
165: 
166: Tenant Admin can delegate to Organization Admins:
167: 
168: | Delegatable | Default | Rationale |
169: |-------------|---------|-----------|
170: | Event management | ✅ Delegated | Core function |
171: | Member management | ✅ Delegated | Operational need |
172: | Content moderation | ⚙️ Configurable | Trust level dependent |
173: | Financial access | ❌ Restricted | Liability |
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: ## Audit and Accountability
178: 
179: ### Audit Requirements
180: 
181: | Role | Actions Audited | Retention |
182: |------|-----------------|-----------|
183: | Instance Admin | All system changes | Indefinite |
184: | Tenant Admin | Configuration, user management | Per policy |
185: | Organization Admin | Content, membership changes | Per policy |
186: | User | Security-relevant actions | Per policy |
187: 
188: ### Accountability Chain
189: 
190: Every administrative action must be:
191: 1. **Authenticated** - Verified identity
192: 2. **Authorized** - Proper role/permission
193: 3. **Logged** - Recorded with context
194: 4. **Traceable** - Linkable to human actor
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## Special Scenarios
199: 
200: ### Emergency Access
201: 
202: Instance Admin may bypass restrictions only when:
203: - Security incident response
204: - Legal compliance requirement
205: - Disaster recovery
206: - Explicit tenant consent
207: 
208: **All emergency access is fully audited and reported.**
209: 
210: ### Tenant Offboarding
211: 
212: When a tenant leaves:
213: 1. Data export provided to tenant
214: 2. Grace period for data retrieval
215: 3. Anonymization of shared data
216: 4. Complete deletion after retention period
217: 
218: ### Dispute Resolution
219: 
220: When tenant and instance policies conflict:
221: 1. Instance policies prevail for security/legal
222: 2. Tenant preferences prevail for business
223: 3. Escalation path defined in service agreement
224: 
225: ---
226: 
227: ## Related Documentation
228: 
229: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant isolation model
230: - **[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)** - Authentication and authorization
231: - **[OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md)** - Operational procedures
232: 
233: ## Implementation Reference
234: 
235: For code patterns:
236: - **`auth-patterns`** skill - Role-based authorization
237: - **`clean-architecture-rules`** skill - Layer boundaries
````

## File: docs/CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md
````markdown
  1: # Codebase Insights
  2: 
  3: > Non-intuitive patterns, hidden knowledge, and things requiring deep analysis.
  4: > This document captures what you cannot guess from reading ARCHITECTURE.md alone.
  5: > Last Updated: February 2026
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## 1. Multi-Tenancy Deep Mechanics
 10: 
 11: ### How Tenant Isolation Actually Works
 12: 
 13: Multi-tenancy is **not middleware-based** — it uses EF Core global query filters injected via the DbContext. The flow:
 14: 
 15: 1. **TenantContext** (API service) resolves the tenant from the HTTP request
 16: 2. **ExploreDbContext** receives TenantContext via **property injection** (not constructor injection) because the DbContext uses pooling
 17: 3. **Named query filters** on every tenant-scoped entity automatically filter by `TenantId`
 18: 4. The filter expression is: `TenantContext == null || e.TenantId == TenantContext.TenantId` — the null check allows migrations and seeding to bypass tenant filtering
 19: 
 20: ### Tenant Resolution Priority
 21: 
 22: TenantContext resolves the tenant in this order:
 23: 1. `X-Tenant-Id` HTTP header (explicit selection)
 24: 2. Custom domain lookup (checks `TenantSetting` for matching domain)
 25: 3. Subdomain extraction (extracts from host, looks up tenant by subdomain or slug)
 26: 4. Default tenant (from configuration or hardcoded fallback)
 27: 
 28: ### Runtime vs Static Deployment Mode
 29: 
 30: The system checks deployment mode (SingleTenant/MultiTenant) **at runtime from the database** (`SystemSettings` table), not just from `appsettings.json`. This means a running instance can be switched between modes without redeployment. The static config is only a fallback when the DB is unreachable.
 31: 
 32: ### Not All Entities Are Tenant-Scoped
 33: 
 34: - **Tenant-scoped** (implement `ITenantEntity`): Event, Organization, Actor, Location, StorageObject, Category, Tag, and their junction tables
 35: - **Global** (no tenant filter): User, lookup tables (EventType, Language, etc.), SystemSetting, ModuleDefinition, InstanceAdministrator
 36: - **Soft-delete only** (no tenant, has `ISoftDeletable`): User
 37: 
 38: ### The TenantSetting vs TenantSettings Distinction
 39: 
 40: There are **two different entities** for tenant settings:
 41: - `TenantSetting` — Individual key-value pairs per tenant (governance overrides, used by `SettingsResolver`)
 42: - `TenantSettings` — A snapshot entity with explicit properties per tenant (display name, theme, etc.)
 43: 
 44: The DbSet names reflect this: `TenantSettingOverrides` for `TenantSetting`, `TenantSettings` for `TenantSettings`.
 45: 
 46: ---
 47: 
 48: ## 2. DbContext Pooling and Property Injection
 49: 
 50: The `ExploreDbContext` uses **pooled DbContext factory** for performance. This has a critical implication:
 51: 
 52: - The constructor **cannot** accept scoped services (TenantContext, CurrentUserService)
 53: - Instead, these are set via **property injection** after the context is created from the pool
 54: - The scoped registration in `PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs` creates the context from the factory, then sets the properties
 55: 
 56: This means:
 57: - `TenantContext` and `CurrentUserService` can be `null` (during migrations, seeding, or background services)
 58: - All query filters and audit logic must handle null gracefully
 59: - If you add a new scoped dependency to DbContext, it must follow this property injection pattern
 60: 
 61: ---
 62: 
 63: ## 3. Soft Delete Interception in SaveChanges
 64: 
 65: When you call `Delete()` on an entity that implements `ISoftDeletable`, the `GenericRepository` sets `EntityState.Deleted`. But the entity is **never actually deleted** from the database. Here's what happens:
 66: 
 67: 1. `GenericRepository.Delete()` marks entity as `EntityState.Deleted`
 68: 2. `ExploreDbContext.SaveChangesAsync()` intercepts the Deleted state
 69: 3. Changes it to `EntityState.Modified` instead
 70: 4. Sets `IsDeleted = true`, `DeletedAt = now`, `DeletedBy = userId`
 71: 5. Also updates `UpdatedAt`/`UpdatedBy` if entity is `IAuditableEntity`
 72: 
 73: For entities that don't implement `ISoftDeletable`, `Delete()` performs a real hard delete.
 74: 
 75: `HardDelete()` method exists for admin operations that need permanent removal regardless of `ISoftDeletable`.
 76: 
 77: ---
 78: 
 79: ## 4. Named Query Filters (EF Core 10+)
 80: 
 81: This project uses EF Core 10's **named query filters** feature. Each entity can have multiple independently-controllable filters:
 82: 
 83: - `QueryFilterNames.Tenant` — Tenant isolation filter
 84: - `QueryFilterNames.SoftDelete` — Soft delete filter
 85: 
 86: You can selectively disable one without the other:
 87: - `IgnoreQueryFilter("SoftDelete")` — Shows deleted records but still respects tenant isolation
 88: - `IgnoreQueryFilter("Tenant")` — Cross-tenant query (admin operations) but still hides deleted records
 89: - `IgnoreQueryFilters()` — Disables ALL filters (dangerous — cross-tenant + deleted)
 90: 
 91: Not all entities have both filters. Check `ExploreDbContext.ApplyGlobalQueryFilters()` for the exact mapping.
 92: 
 93: ---
 94: 
 95: ## 5. Blazor Server + WASM Hybrid Architecture
 96: 
 97: ### The Two-Project Structure
 98: 
 99: - `Explore.Blazor` — Blazor Server host. Handles SSR, OIDC authentication, serves the WASM app, and acts as a BFF proxy
100: - `Explore.Blazor.Client` — Blazor WebAssembly. Contains all interactive UI components, pages, and services
101: 
102: ### How Authentication Flows
103: 
104: 1. User accesses the Blazor Server host
105: 2. OIDC challenge redirects to Keycloak for login
106: 3. After login, the server stores tokens in a `CircuitAccessTokenService` (per-circuit lifetime)
107: 4. For WASM: Authentication state is serialized to the client using `AddAuthenticationStateDeserialization()`
108: 5. WASM makes API calls through the same origin (BFF pattern)
109: 6. `BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler` adds cookies to all WASM HttpClient requests
110: 7. `BffUnauthorizedHandler` intercepts 401 responses and triggers server-side re-login
111: 
112: ### The BFF Pattern
113: 
114: The Blazor Server host proxies API requests. WASM never calls the API directly — it goes through the BFF:
115: - WASM `HttpClient.BaseAddress` = same origin as Blazor Server
116: - Blazor Server proxies `/api/*` requests to the actual API
117: - Cookies (including auth tokens) travel automatically
118: 
119: ### S3 Image Upload Exception
120: 
121: Image uploads bypass the BFF. They go directly to S3-compatible storage (Hetzner) using presigned URLs:
122: - `ImageStorageService` gets a presigned URL from the API
123: - `S3UploadMessageHandler` configures CORS mode for cross-origin PUT
124: - Direct browser-to-S3 upload avoids server bottleneck
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 6. Module Governance System
129: 
130: ### What Modules Are
131: 
132: The system supports pluggable modules that add domain-specific behavior:
133: - **Core** — Always enabled. Basic event functionality
134: - **Islamic** — Madhab selection, prayer times, gender segregation awareness
135: - **Tech** — GitHub repositories, skill levels, live coding flags
136: 
137: ### How Modules Work
138: 
139: 1. `ModuleDefinition` table defines available modules (seeded)
140: 2. `TenantCapability` maps which modules each tenant has enabled
141: 3. `IModuleService` checks if a module is enabled for the current tenant
142: 4. `EventIslamicAspect` / `EventTechAspect` — Optional 1:1 extension tables that store module-specific fields
143: 5. `IEventStrategy` / `StrategyResolver` — Module-specific behavior dispatched at runtime via strategy pattern
144: 
145: ### The Strategy Pattern
146: 
147: When creating/updating events, the `StrategyResolver` picks the right strategy based on enabled modules:
148: - `IslamicEventStrategy` — Handles Islamic-specific validation and field population
149: - `TechEventStrategy` — Handles tech-specific validation and field population
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## 7. Lookup Table Dual-Track System
154: 
155: Lookup tables are managed in **two synchronized places**:
156: 
157: ### Track 1: Domain Enums
158: `Explore.Domain/Enums/{EntityName}Enum.cs` — Defines the int IDs and names. Used in code for type-safe references.
159: 
160: ### Track 2: EF Core HasData Seeding
161: `Explore.Persistence/Configurations/Entities/{EntityName}Configuration.cs` — Uses `HasData()` to seed the database with matching values.
162: 
163: ### The Synchronization Rule
164: 
165: The enum values and HasData seed values **must always match**. If you add a new enum value, you must also add a matching `HasData()` entry. The `LookupTableSeeder` class helps ensure runtime synchronization.
166: 
167: ### Which ID Type for What
168: 
169: - **Lookup tables** use `int` PK (EventType, Language, etc.)
170: - **Main entities** use `Guid` PK (Event, Organization, etc.)
171: - **Link tables** use composite keys (EventId + CategoryId, etc.)
172: - Never use `long` except for file sizes or pagination cursors
173: 
174: ---
175: 
176: ## 8. Seed Data Architecture
177: 
178: ### Two Seeding Mechanisms
179: 
180: 1. **EF Configuration HasData()** — Lookup tables are seeded via entity configurations. This creates migration-tracked seed data. Used for: EventType, EventStatus, EventFormat, AudienceAge, etc.
181: 
182: 2. **Runtime DatabaseSeeder** — Called at startup via `DatabaseSeeder.cs`. Seeds main entities (Tenant, User, Organization, Actor, StorageObject, Event). Uses `SeedIds.cs` for deterministic GUIDs.
183: 
184: ### SeedIds and UUIDv7
185: 
186: All seed GUIDs use **UUIDv7** format (`018e4e5c-xxxx-7xxx-8xxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`) for:
187: - Time-ordered insertion (better index performance)
188: - Deterministic values (same GUIDs every run, prevents duplicates)
189: - Range-separated by entity type (different `xxxx` ranges for tenants vs users vs organizations)
190: 
191: **Critical rule:** Never change seed IDs after they've been used in production migrations.
192: 
193: ---
194: 
195: ## 9. HATEOAS Implementation
196: 
197: The API implements **HAL (Hypertext Application Language)** for hypermedia:
198: 
199: - `HalResource<T>` wraps response DTOs with `_links` section
200: - `HalCollectionResource<T>` wraps lists with pagination links
201: - `ResourceAssemblerBase<T>` generates links per entity type
202: - `HateoasLinkGenerator` resolves URLs from route names
203: - OpenAPI schema is transformed by `HalSchemaTransformer` to show HAL structure
204: 
205: The `PreferHeaderMiddleware` handles content negotiation: clients can request HAL format via `Prefer: return=representation` header.
206: 
207: ---
208: 
209: ## 10. The Actors System (Federation/ATProto)
210: 
211: ### What Actors Are
212: 
213: `Actor` is the federation identity concept from ATProto/ActivityPub:
214: - Every user gets a personal Actor
215: - Every organization gets an Actor
216: - Actors have DIDs (Decentralized Identifiers), key pairs, and can federate
217: 
218: ### Actor ↔ User/Organization Relationship
219: 
220: - An `Actor` has an `ActorType` (Personal, Organization, Bot, Service)
221: - A `User` owns one or more Actors
222: - An `Organization` is linked to exactly one Actor
223: - `ActorKeyStore` stores signing keys for federated operations
224: - `DidCustodyType` tracks who controls the DID (self, server, external)
225: 
226: ### Federation Sync
227: 
228: - `PdsSyncOutbox` — Outbox pattern for syncing changes to ATProto PDS
229: - `PdsSyncWorker` — Background service that processes the outbox
230: - `IndexedDid` / `SyncState` / `AtprotoRecord` — Firehose indexer state
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 11. Settings Resolution Chain
235: 
236: The governance settings system has a three-tier resolution:
237: 
238: 1. **SystemSetting** (instance-wide defaults) — e.g., "require event approval = true"
239: 2. **TenantSetting** (per-tenant overrides) — e.g., Tenant A overrides to "false"
240: 3. **PlatformDefaults** (code-level fallback) — if neither DB value exists
241: 
242: `SettingsResolver` implements this cascade. Settings values are stored as **JSON-serialized strings** in the database. The `TenantContext.cs` file shows the deserialization pattern: `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(rawValue)` with fallback to raw parsing.
243: 
244: ### GovernanceSettingKeys
245: 
246: Setting keys are string constants in `GovernanceSettingKeys.cs`. They use dot-separated hierarchical naming:
247: - `Deployment.Mode`
248: - `Events.MaxSessionsPerEvent`
249: - `Modules.Islamic.Enabled`
250: - `Domains.InstanceBaseDomain`
251: - `Domains.AllowTenantCustomDomain`
252: 
253: ---
254: 
255: ## 12. AutoMapper Profile Organization
256: 
257: All mappings live in a **single file**: `Explore.Application/Profiles/MappingProfile.cs`. This file maps every entity to every DTO. When adding a new entity/DTO pair, the mapping goes here — not in a separate profile file.
258: 
259: ---
260: 
261: ## 13. API Client Generation
262: 
263: The Blazor client uses an **NSwag-generated API client**:
264: 
265: - `EventApiClient.cs` — Hand-written interface (`IEventApiClient`) with additional methods
266: - `EventApiClient.g.cs` — Auto-generated code from `swagger.json`
267: - The generated client is registered in WASM `Program.cs` with the BFF HttpClient
268: 
269: To regenerate: update `swagger.json` from the API, then run the NSwag generator.
270: 
271: ---
272: 
273: ## 14. Exception Handling Flow
274: 
275: ### API Side
276: `ExceptionMiddleware` catches all unhandled exceptions and maps them to HTTP responses:
277: - `NotFoundException` → 404
278: - `BadRequestException` → 400
279: - `ValidationException` → 400 with error details
280: - Unhandled → 500
281: 
282: ### Command Response Pattern
283: Commands don't throw for validation failures. They return `BaseCommandResponse<TKey>`:
284: - `Success = true/false`
285: - `Errors` list with validation messages
286: - Controllers return `Ok(response)` or `BadRequest(response)` based on `Success`
287: 
288: ### Client Side
289: `ServiceResult<T>` wraps API responses in the Blazor client, providing a consistent error handling pattern.
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: ## 15. BlockInSingleTenant Filter
294: 
295: The `BlockInSingleTenantAttribute` action filter prevents certain endpoints from being called in single-tenant mode. This is used for multi-tenant management endpoints that don't make sense in single-tenant deployments.
296: 
297: ---
298: 
299: ## 16. DI Registration Locations
300: 
301: Services are registered in multiple places — knowing where to add yours is critical:
302: 
303: | What | Where | Method |
304: |---|---|---|
305: | Repositories | `Explore.Persistence/PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs` | `CongfigurePersistenceServices()` |
306: | Infrastructure services | `Explore.Infrastructure/InfrastructureServicesRegistration.cs` | `ConfigureInfrastructureServices()` |
307: | API-layer services | `Explore.API/Program.cs` | Direct registration |
308: | MediatR handlers | Auto-registered via `AddMediatR()` in `Program.cs` | Assembly scanning |
309: | AutoMapper profiles | Auto-registered via `AddAutoMapper()` | Assembly scanning |
310: | Blazor WASM services | `Explore.Blazor.Client/Program.cs` | Direct registration |
311: | Blazor Server services | `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs` | Direct registration |
312: | Secrets | `Explore.Secrets/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` | `AddSecrets()` |
313: 
314: **Note:** There is a typo in `CongfigurePersistenceServices` (missing `i` in "Configure"). This is existing and intentional — do not rename it without updating all call sites.
315: 
316: ---
317: 
318: ## 17. Aspire Integration
319: 
320: The project uses **.NET Aspire** for local development orchestration:
321: 
322: - `Explore.AppHost` — Defines the service topology (API + Blazor + PostgreSQL + dependencies)
323: - `Explore.ServiceDefaults` — Shared configuration (OpenTelemetry, health checks, resilience)
324: - Database connection is configured via Aspire's `AddNpgsqlDbContext` in the API project, while `PersistenceServicesRegistration` uses `AddPooledDbContextFactory` for production
325: 
326: The Aspire integration is intentionally **not** in the Persistence project to avoid an ASP.NET Core dependency in the persistence layer.
327: 
328: ---
329: 
330: ## 18. Migration Service
331: 
332: `Event.MigrationService` is a **worker service** that applies EF Core migrations at startup:
333: - Runs as a separate process in the Aspire topology
334: - Applies pending migrations to the database
335: - Calls `DatabaseSeeder` to ensure seed data exists
336: - Exits after completion
337: 
338: This decouples migration execution from the API startup, allowing the API to assume the database is ready.
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## 19. Image Storage Flow
343: 
344: Images are stored in **S3-compatible object storage** (Hetzner):
345: 
346: 1. Client requests a presigned upload URL from the API (`StorageObjectController`)
347: 2. API generates presigned URL via `ObjectStorageService` and creates a `StorageObject` record
348: 3. Client uploads directly to S3 using the presigned URL (bypasses BFF)
349: 4. `S3Image.razor` component renders images using the S3 URL
350: 5. `StorageObject` entity tracks: bucket, key, content type, size, and owner (via `OwnerType`)
351: 
352: ---
353: 
354: ## 20. Organization Review System
355: 
356: Organization reviews use a slightly different CQRS structure:
357: 
358: - `OrganizationReviews/Commands/` and `OrganizationReviews/Queries/` (flattened, no `Handlers/Requests` split)
359: - This is the only feature that uses this alternative structure — all others use the standard nested pattern
360: 
361: ---
362: 
363: ## 21. ABOUTME File Comments
364: 
365: Every file should start with a two-line comment:
366: ```
367: // ABOUTME: Brief description of what this file does.
368: // ABOUTME: Second line with additional context.
369: ```
370: 
371: Not all files have this yet, but it's the convention. Add it when modifying a file.
372: 
373: ---
374: 
375: ## 22. Client-Side Lookup Caching
376: 
377: `LookupCacheService` caches lookup table data (EventTypes, AudienceAges, Languages, etc.) in the WASM client to avoid repeated API calls. When adding a new lookup table:
378: 
379: 1. Add the API call to the relevant service
380: 2. Add caching in `LookupCacheService`
381: 3. Use the cached version in page components
382: 
383: ---
384: 
385: ## 23. Route Guards (Blazouter)
386: 
387: The Blazor client uses **Blazouter** library for client-side routing with guards:
388: 
389: - `AuthenticatedRouteGuard` — Requires authentication
390: - `AdminRouteGuard` — Requires admin role
391: 
392: Guards are registered in `Program.cs` and applied via Blazouter's routing configuration.
393: 
394: ---
395: 
396: ## 25. Specification Pattern Implementation
397: 
398: The application uses a custom **Specification Pattern** to handle complex filtering logic, particularly for the `Event` entity which has modular aspects.
399: 
400: ### Core Components
401: - **`IQuerySpecification<T>`**: Interface defining the contract for query specifications.
402: - **`EventQuerySpecification`**: The main specification for event retrieval. It orchestrates sub-filters.
403: - **`IFilterSpecification<T>`**: Interface for individual filter components.
404: 
405: ### Modular Filtering Strategy
406: Instead of a massive `Where()` clause in the repository, filters are broken down into small, reusable classes:
407: 
408: 1.  **`EventFilter`**: Handles core fields (Date, Location, Category).
409: 2.  **`AspectPresenceFilter`**: Handles "HasIslamicAspect" / "HasTechAspect" flags.
410: 3.  **`IslamicAspectFilter`**: Handles Islamic-specific fields (Madhab, GenderMode).
411: 4.  **`TechAspectFilter`**: Handles Tech-specific fields (SkillLevel, Stack).
412: 
413: The `EventQuerySpecification` applies these filters sequentially to the `IQueryable<Event>`. This allows module-specific filters to be applied only when relevant.
414: 
415: ---
416: 
417: ## 26. Hybrid Caching Strategy (L1 + L2)
418: 
419: We use **.NET 9+ HybridCache** for application-level caching, which provides L1 (In-Memory) + L2 (Redis) caching with built-in stampede protection.
420: 
421: ### Usage Pattern
422: HybridCache is injected into **MediatR Handlers**, not Controllers.
423: 
424: **Read-Through (Query Handlers):**
425: ```csharp
426: return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
427:     key: $"event:{request.Id}",
428:     factory: async cancel => await _repo.GetById(request.Id),
429:     options: new HybridCacheEntryOptions { Expiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) }
430: );
431: ```
432: 
433: **Invalidation (Command Handlers):**
434: ```csharp
435: // In Create/Update/Delete handlers
436: await _cache.RemoveAsync($"event:{request.Id}");
437: ```
438: 
439: **Key Distinction:**
440: - **OutputCache**: Caches the *HTTP response* (Controllers). Good for anonymous public lists.
441: - **HybridCache**: Caches the *Domain Entity/DTO* (Handlers). Good for shared data, authenticated views, and internal logic.
442: 
443: ---
444: 
445: ## 27. Validation Architecture
446: 
447: ### The "Manual Instantiation" Rule
448: Validators are **never** injected via DI. They are manually instantiated in the Handler.
449: 
450: **Why?**
451: Our validators often require database access (e.g., "Does this CategoryId exist?", "Is this User an Admin?"). Injecting Repositories into Validators via DI can cause lifetime issues and circular dependencies if not careful.
452: 
453: **The Pattern:**
454: ```csharp
455: public class CreateEventCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<...>
456: {
457:     public CreateEventCommandHandler(
458:         IEventRepository eventRepo,
459:         IOrganizationRepository orgRepo) // Inject repos into Handler
460:     { ... }
461: 
462:     public async Task<Response> Handle(...)
463:     {
464:         // Pass repos to Validator constructor manually
465:         var validator = new CreateEventDtoValidator(_eventRepo, _orgRepo);
466:         var result = await validator.ValidateAsync(request.Dto);
467:         // ...
468:     }
469: }
470: ```
471: 
472: This ensures the validator uses the same repository instances (and DbContext) as the handler transaction.
````

## File: docs/DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md
````markdown
  1: # Deployment Modes
  2: 
  3: > **Single-Tenant vs Multi-Tenant Deployment Strategies**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes how the platform supports both dedicated single-tenant
  6: > and shared multi-tenant deployments from a single codebase.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform supports two deployment modes from the **same codebase**:
 15: 
 16: | Mode | Description | Target Use Case |
 17: |------|-------------|-----------------|
 18: | **Single-Tenant** | One community per installation | Self-hosted, dedicated deployments |
 19: | **Multi-Tenant** | Multiple communities per installation | SaaS, shared infrastructure |
 20: 
 21: **Key Insight**: The codebase is always multi-tenant internally. Single-tenant mode is a "mask" that simplifies the experience while preserving the underlying architecture.
 22: 
 23: ---
 24: 
 25: ## Virtual Tenant Strategy
 26: 
 27: ### How It Works
 28: 
 29: Instead of maintaining two codebases:
 30: 1. Multi-tenant code is the foundation
 31: 2. Single-tenant mode forces `TenantId = Default`
 32: 3. Tenant management UI is hidden/shown based on mode
 33: 4. Mode can be switched at runtime
 34: 
 35: ### Benefits
 36: 
 37: | Benefit | Description |
 38: |---------|-------------|
 39: | **One Codebase** | No divergence between modes |
 40: | **Upgrade Path** | Single-tenant can become multi-tenant |
 41: | **Testing Simplicity** | One set of tests covers both modes |
 42: | **Consistent Security** | Same isolation mechanisms apply |
 43: 
 44: ---
 45: 
 46: ## Mode Characteristics
 47: 
 48: ### Single-Tenant Mode
 49: 
 50: **Behavior**:
 51: - `TenantId` hardcoded to `Default` tenant
 52: - Tenant management UI hidden
 53: - Instance Admin and Tenant Admin permissions merged
 54: - No subdomain/header-based routing
 55: - Simplified first-run experience
 56: 
 57: **Experience**:
 58: - Feels like a traditional single-user application
 59: - Admin sees combined settings panel
 60: - No awareness of multi-tenant engine underneath
 61: 
 62: ### Multi-Tenant Mode
 63: 
 64: **Behavior**:
 65: - `TenantId` resolved from subdomain or header
 66: - Full tenant management UI visible
 67: - Clear separation between Instance and Tenant Admin
 68: - Tenant-specific routing (e.g., `mosque.app.com`)
 69: 
 70: **Experience**:
 71: - Full SaaS platform capabilities
 72: - Tenant isolation clearly visible
 73: - Self-service or managed onboarding
 74: 
 75: ---
 76: 
 77: ## First-Run Experience
 78: 
 79: ### Single-Tenant Default
 80: 
 81: 1. Application installs with seeded data:
 82:    - `DeploymentMode = Single`
 83:    - `RegistrationPolicy = Closed`
 84:    - Default tenant created
 85: 2. First user visits application
 86: 3. Middleware detects single mode, forces default tenant
 87: 4. User registers as Admin of default tenant
 88: 5. Application feels like standard single-user app
 89: 
 90: ### No Configuration Required
 91: 
 92: The single-tenant first run requires:
 93: - ❌ No tenant creation
 94: - ❌ No subdomain setup
 95: - ❌ No complex configuration
 96: - ✅ Just install and use
 97: 
 98: ---
 99: 
100: ## Runtime Mode Switching
101: 
102: ### Enabling Multi-Tenant
103: 
104: When the deployment grows beyond a single community:
105: 
106: 1. Instance Admin navigates to Settings → Instance
107: 2. Toggles "Deployment Mode" to Multi-Tenant
108: 3. Application clears relevant caches
109: 4. Immediate effects:
110:    - Tenant sidebar menu appears
111:    - "Create Tenant" button visible
112:    - Subdomain routing activates
113:    - Original tenant becomes first of many
114: 
115: ### Switching Back
116: 
117: Multi-tenant → Single-tenant is possible with constraints:
118: - Only one active tenant can exist
119: - Other tenants must be archived/purged
120: - Warning displayed about data implications
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## Tenant Resolution
125: 
126: ### Single-Tenant Mode
127: 
128: | Mechanism | Behavior |
129: |-----------|----------|
130: | Middleware | Short-circuits, returns `Default` |
131: | Routing | Standard routes, no subdomain |
132: | Context | Always populated with default tenant |
133: 
134: ### Multi-Tenant Mode
135: 
136: | Mechanism | Options |
137: |-----------|---------|
138: | **Subdomain** | `tenant1.app.com` → Tenant1 |
139: | **Header** | `X-Tenant-Id: tenant1` → Tenant1 |
140: | **Path** | `/tenants/tenant1/...` → Tenant1 |
141: | **Claim** | JWT contains tenant ID → Tenant from token |
142: 
143: ### Resolution Priority
144: 
145: 1. Explicit header (highest priority)
146: 2. JWT claim
147: 3. Subdomain
148: 4. Path segment
149: 5. Default tenant (fallback)
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## Configuration Model
154: 
155: ### System Settings
156: 
157: | Setting | Values | Description |
158: |---------|--------|-------------|
159: | `DeploymentMode` | `Single` / `Multi` | Current mode |
160: | `TenantRegistrationPolicy` | `Open` / `InviteOnly` / `Closed` | New tenant policy |
161: | `DefaultTenantId` | Tenant ID | Virtual tenant for single mode |
162: 
163: ### Environment Overrides
164: 
165: For containerized deployments:
166: 
167: | Environment Variable | Purpose |
168: |---------------------|---------|
169: | `DEPLOYMENT_MODE` | Force mode (overrides database) |
170: | `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` | Custom default tenant |
171: | `ALLOW_MODE_SWITCH` | Enable/disable runtime switching |
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## Infrastructure Considerations
176: 
177: ### Single-Tenant Infrastructure
178: 
179: | Component | Configuration |
180: |-----------|---------------|
181: | Database | Single schema, single connection string |
182: | DNS | Single domain |
183: | SSL | Single certificate |
184: | Storage | Shared bucket/container |
185: 
186: ### Multi-Tenant Infrastructure
187: 
188: | Component | Configuration |
189: |-----------|---------------|
190: | Database | Shared schema with tenant isolation |
191: | DNS | Wildcard domain (`*.app.com`) or tenant subdomains |
192: | SSL | Wildcard certificate or per-tenant |
193: | Storage | Tenant-prefixed paths or separate containers |
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: ## Migration Paths
198: 
199: ### Single → Multi (Growth)
200: 
201: **Trigger**: Organization wants to host other communities
202: 
203: **Steps**:
204: 1. Enable multi-tenant mode
205: 2. Configure DNS for subdomains
206: 3. Update SSL certificate (wildcard)
207: 4. Create additional tenants
208: 5. Original tenant continues as-is
209: 
210: ### Multi → Single (Consolidation)
211: 
212: **Trigger**: SaaS shutting down, moving to dedicated
213: 
214: **Steps**:
215: 1. Export target tenant data
216: 2. Archive/purge other tenants
217: 3. Switch to single-tenant mode
218: 4. Remove multi-tenant infrastructure
219: 
220: ---
221: 
222: ## Tenant Registration Policies
223: 
224: ### Registration Flow Options
225: 
226: | Policy | Description | Visible UI |
227: |--------|-------------|------------|
228: | **Open** | Anyone can create tenant | "Start Your Community" button |
229: | **Invite-Only** | Instance Admin sends link | Hidden signup, invite link works |
230: | **Closed** | No new tenants | No signup UI |
231: 
232: ### Policy Use Cases
233: 
234: | Scenario | Recommended Policy |
235: |----------|-------------------|
236: | Public SaaS | Open |
237: | Enterprise SaaS | Invite-Only |
238: | Pilot/Beta | Invite-Only |
239: | Maintenance | Closed |
240: | Single-Tenant | Closed (default) |
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ## Related Documentation
245: 
246: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant isolation model
247: - **[ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md](ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md)** - Authority boundaries
248: - **[OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md)** - Deployment procedures
249: - **[CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md)** - Environment setup
250: 
251: ## Implementation Reference
252: 
253: For code patterns:
254: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Tenant query filters
255: - **`auth-patterns`** skill - Tenant context middleware
````

## File: docs/EXTENSIBILITY.md
````markdown
  1: # Extensibility Architecture
  2: 
  3: > **Metadata-Driven Modular Design**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes the aspect-based extensibility model that enables deep customization
  6: > without database schema changes or application restarts.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform uses a **Metadata-Driven Aspect Architecture** to handle diverse requirements (cultural, religious, technical) dynamically. This allows:
 15: - Adding new "aspects" to entities without schema changes
 16: - Enabling/disabling features per tenant
 17: - Cultural customization (e.g., Islamic prayer-based scheduling)
 18: - Technical configuration (e.g., render modes, API versioning)
 19: 
 20: ---
 21: 
 22: ## Core Concept: Aspects vs Inheritance
 23: 
 24: ### The Problem with Inheritance
 25: 
 26: Traditional OOP inheritance creates combinatorial explosion:
 27: - `IslamicEvent`, `TechEvent` - 2 types
 28: - `IslamicTechEvent` - need a third?
 29: - Every combination requires a new class
 30: 
 31: ### The Aspect Solution
 32: 
 33: Instead of "Is this an Islamic Event?", ask "Does this Event have Islamic details?"
 34: 
 35: **Key Insight**: An event is a generic container that can "wear" different hats (aspects) simultaneously.
 36: 
 37: | Approach | Flexibility | Schema Changes | Runtime Cost |
 38: |----------|-------------|----------------|--------------|
 39: | Inheritance | Low | Every combination | None |
 40: | Aspects | High | Never | Minimal |
 41: 
 42: ---
 43: 
 44: ## Data Architecture: The Relational Aspect Pattern
 45: 
 46: ### Core Entity Structure
 47: 
 48: Core entities contain only universal properties:
 49: - Identity fields (`Id`, `TenantId`)
 50: - Common properties (`Title`, `CreatedAt`)
 51: - Audit fields (`CreatedBy`, `UpdatedAt`)
 52: 
 53: ### Extension Tables (Aspects)
 54: 
 55: Aspects are optional 1:1 relationships using **shared primary key**:
 56: 
 57: | Table | Purpose | Links To |
 58: |-------|---------|----------|
 59: | `Events` | Core event data | - |
 60: | `EventIslamicDetails` | Islamic-specific attributes | `Events.Id` |
 61: | `EventTechDetails` | Tech-specific attributes | `Events.Id` |
 62: 
 63: **Key Design**: The aspect table's primary key IS also its foreign key to the core entity.
 64: 
 65: ### Composition Example
 66: 
 67: An event that is **both** Islamic and Tech simply has rows in all relevant tables sharing the same ID:
 68: 
 69: | Event #100 | Has Row In |
 70: |------------|------------|
 71: | Core data | `Events` |
 72: | Islamic data | `EventIslamicDetails` |
 73: | Tech data | `EventTechDetails` |
 74: 
 75: ---
 76: 
 77: ## Module Governance Pattern
 78: 
 79: ### Three-Tier Module Availability
 80: 
 81: Modules (sets of aspects and logic) cascade through three levels:
 82: 
 83: | Tier | Scope | Example |
 84: |------|-------|---------|
 85: | **Instance** | What's physically possible | "Server has Islamic + Tech modules" |
 86: | **Tenant** | What's active for this org | "Our mosque only uses Islamic" |
 87: | **Entity** | What's selected for this item | "This event is Islamic-only" |
 88: 
 89: ### Module Visibility Rules
 90: 
 91: A module appears in UI only if:
 92: 1. ✅ Instance Admin has enabled it globally
 93: 2. ✅ Tenant Admin has activated it for their community
 94: 3. ✅ User has permission to use it
 95: 
 96: **Result**: Tenant A (Mosque) never sees "Hackathon" field; Tenant B (Tech Hub) never sees "Madhab" dropdown.
 97: 
 98: ---
 99: 
100: ## Logic Architecture: Request-Scoped Strategies
101: 
102: ### Strategy Selection at Runtime
103: 
104: Business logic adapts per-request without application restart:
105: 
106: 1. **HTTP Request** → User attempts action
107: 2. **Tenant Context** → Middleware identifies tenant
108: 3. **Module Check** → System determines active modules
109: 4. **Strategy Selection** → Resolver returns appropriate implementation
110: 
111: ### Strategy Pattern Examples
112: 
113: | Module | Strategy Interface | Implementation |
114: |--------|-------------------|----------------|
115: | Islamic | `ISchedulingStrategy` | Calculates time based on prayer schedule |
116: | Tech | `ISchedulingStrategy` | Standard datetime scheduling |
117: | Default | `ISchedulingStrategy` | Fallback implementation |
118: 
119: ### Policy Engine
120: 
121: Cross-cutting policies evaluate before operations:
122: - **Submission Policy**: Can this user create this entity type?
123: - **Visibility Policy**: Can this user view this entity?
124: - **Approval Policy**: Does this require moderation?
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## Dynamic Taxonomies
129: 
130: ### User-Defined Metadata
131: 
132: For flexibility beyond compiled modules, use a metadata schema:
133: 
134: | Concept | Purpose |
135: |---------|---------|
136: | **Taxonomy Definition** | Defines a field (name, type, allowed values) |
137: | **Taxonomy Value** | Stores data linked to an entity |
138: 
139: ### When to Use
140: 
141: | Scenario | Use Module? | Use Taxonomy? |
142: |----------|-------------|---------------|
143: | Complex business logic | ✅ | ❌ |
144: | Simple categorization | ❌ | ✅ |
145: | Requires validation | ✅ | ❌ |
146: | User-defined labels | ❌ | ✅ |
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## API Architecture: Polymorphic Responses
151: 
152: ### Discriminated DTOs
153: 
154: API responses include a base DTO plus a list of active aspects:
155: 
156: | Response Field | Purpose |
157: |----------------|---------|
158: | `id`, `title`, etc. | Core entity data |
159: | `aspects[]` | List of active aspect types |
160: | `islamicDetails` | Islamic aspect data (if present) |
161: | `techDetails` | Tech aspect data (if present) |
162: 
163: ### Client-Side Mapping
164: 
165: Frontend dynamically renders components based on aspect presence:
166: 
167: | Aspect Type | Renders Component |
168: |-------------|-------------------|
169: | `Islamic` | Prayer time selector, Madhab dropdown |
170: | `Tech` | GitHub link, hackathon track |
171: | (none) | Generic form only |
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## UI Architecture: Dynamic Forms
176: 
177: ### Blueprint-Driven Forms
178: 
179: The API sends form definitions, not hardcoded UIs:
180: 1. Client requests entity creation form
181: 2. Server returns schema based on tenant's active modules
182: 3. Client renders form dynamically
183: 4. Submission includes only relevant aspect data
184: 
185: ### Step Sequencer Pattern
186: 
187: Complex wizards use dynamic step loading:
188: 1. User selects intent ("What type of event?")
189: 2. System fetches module's wizard steps
190: 3. UI loads appropriate components
191: 4. Data saved with module discriminator
192: 
193: ---
194: 
195: ## Module Development Guidelines
196: 
197: ### Adding a New Module
198: 
199: 1. **Define Aspect Table** - Schema for module-specific data
200: 2. **Create Strategy Implementations** - Business logic variations
201: 3. **Register in Module Catalog** - Make discoverable to system
202: 4. **Build UI Components** - Forms, displays, wizards
203: 5. **Document Configuration** - Tenant-facing settings
204: 
205: ### Module Independence
206: 
207: Modules should be:
208: - **Self-contained** - No hard dependencies on other modules
209: - **Gracefully degrading** - Works if dependencies missing
210: - **Tenant-configurable** - Respects tenant settings
211: - **Performance-conscious** - Lazy-loaded when possible
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ## Related Documentation
216: 
217: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant isolation model
218: - **[DOMAIN.md](DOMAIN.md)** - Core entity definitions
219: - **[RENDER_POLICIES.md](RENDER_POLICIES.md)** - UI flexibility patterns
220: 
221: ## Implementation Reference
222: 
223: For code patterns and implementation details:
224: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Optional 1:1 relationships
225: - **`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`** skill - Handler patterns for aspects
226: - **`blazor-ui-conventions`** skill - Dynamic component rendering
````

225: ## Domain Model Summary
226: 
227: ### Core Entities
228: 
229: | Entity | Purpose | Relationships |
230: |--------|---------|---------------|
231: | `Event` | Primary aggregate | EventSessions, Categories, Tags, Location |
232: | `EventSession` | Session within event | AgendaItems, Speakers, Languages |
233: | `Organization` | Event organizer | Members, Reviews, Events |
234: | `Actor` | People/groups | Can be User or external |
235: | `Location` | Physical/virtual venues | Events |
236: | `Category` | Event categorization | Events (many-to-many) |
237: | `Tag` | Flexible tagging | Events (many-to-many) |
238: 
239: ### Lookup Tables
240: 
241: `EventType` • `EventStatus` • `EventFormat` • `AudienceAge` • `AudienceGender` • `Madhab` • `Language` • `ActorType` • `ApprovalStatus` • `VisibilityType` • `RegistrationMode` • `Role` • `OrganizationPosition` • `FileType` • `TagType` • `DidCustodyType`
242: 
243: ### Multi-Tenancy
244: 
245: All entities implement `ITenantEntity` with `TenantId` for data isolation:
246: - `Tenant` - Tenant configuration
247: - `TenantSettings` - Per-tenant settings
248: - `TenantUser` - User-tenant membership
249: 
250: **See**: [MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md) for the complete tenant isolation model, and [ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md](ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md) for the authority model.
251: 
252: ### Federation (ATProto)
253: 
254: - `IndexedDid` - Indexed DIDs from network
255: - `AtprotoRecord` - Federated records
256: - `ActorKeyStore` - Cryptographic keys
257: - `SyncState` - Synchronization tracking
