466:         <MudButton Color="Color.Primary"
467:                    Variant="Variant.Filled"
468:                    OnClick="Submit"
469:                    Disabled="_isSubmitting">
470:             Create
471:         </MudButton>
472:     </DialogActions>
473: </MudDialog>
474: 
475: @code {
476:     [CascadingParameter]
477:     private MudDialogInstance MudDialog { get; set; } = null!;
478: 
479:     private Create{Entity}Dto _dto = new();
480:     private DateTime? _startDate;
481:     private bool _isSubmitting;
482: 
483:     private void Cancel() => MudDialog.Cancel();
484: 
485:     private async Task Submit()
486:     {
487:         _isSubmitting = true;
488:         try
489:         {
490:             // ... validation and API call ...
491:             var command = new Create{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = _dto };
492:             var result = await Mediator.Send(command);
493: 
494:             if (result.Success)
495:             {
496:                 Snackbar.Add("{Entity} created", Severity.Success);
497:                 MudDialog.Close(DialogResult.Ok(result.Id)); // Return the new {entity} ID
498:             }
499:             else
500:             {
501:                 Snackbar.Add("Failed to create {entity}", Severity.Error);
502:                 MudDialog.Close(DialogResult.Cancel()); // Or pass back errors
503:             }
504:         }
505:         finally
506:         {
507:             _isSubmitting = false;
508:         }
509:     }
510: }
511: ```
512: 
513: ---
514: 
515: ## 6. MudTable - Data Tables
516: 
517: MudTable is a versatile component for displaying tabular data, offering sorting, pagination, and filtering.
518: 
519: ### Simple Table
520: 
521: ```razor
522: <MudTable Items="@_{entities}" Hover="true" Breakpoint="Breakpoint.Sm">
523:     <HeaderContent>
524:         <MudTh>Title</MudTh>
525:         <MudTh>Date</MudTh>
526:         <MudTh>Location</MudTh>
527:         <MudTh>Actions</MudTh>
528:     </HeaderContent>
529:     <RowTemplate>
530:         <MudTd DataLabel="Title">@context.Title</MudTd>
531:         <MudTd DataLabel="Date">@context.StartDate.ToShortDateString()</MudTd>
532:         <MudTd DataLabel="Location">@context.Location</MudTd>
533:         <MudTd DataLabel="Actions">
534:             <MudIconButton Icon="@Filled.Edit" Size="Size.Small" OnClick="@(() => Edit(context.Id))" />
535:             <MudIconButton Icon="@Filled.Delete" Size="Size.Small" Color="Color.Error" OnClick="@(() => Delete(context.Id))" />
536:         </MudTd>
537:     </RowTemplate>
538: </MudTable>
539: 
540: @code {
541:     private List<{Entity}ListDto> _{entities} = new();
542: }
543: ```
544: 
545: ### Table with Sorting
546: 
547: ```razor
548: <MudTable Items="@_{entities}"
549:           Hover="true"
550:           SortLabel="Sort By" @* Accessibility label for sorting *@
551:           Breakpoint="Breakpoint.Sm">
552:     <HeaderContent>
553:         <MudTh>
554:             <MudTableSortLabel SortBy="new Func<{Entity}ListDto, object>(x => x.Title)"> @* Sort by Title property *@
555:                 Title
556:             </MudTableSortLabel>
557:         </MudTh>
558:         <MudTh>
559:             <MudTableSortLabel SortBy="new Func<{Entity}ListDto, object>(x => x.StartDate)"> @* Sort by StartDate property *@
560:                 Date
561:             </MudTableSortLabel>
562:         </MudTh>
563:         <MudTh>Location</MudTh>
564:     </HeaderContent>
565:     <RowTemplate>
566:         <MudTd DataLabel="Title">@context.Title</MudTd>
567:         <MudTd DataLabel="Date">@context.StartDate.ToShortDateString()</MudTd>
568:         <MudTd DataLabel="Location">@context.Location</MudTd>
569:     </RowTemplate>
570: </MudTable>
571: ```
572: 
573: ### Server-Side Table with Pagination and Search
574: 
575: For large datasets, fetching and processing data on the server is more efficient.
576: 
577: ```razor
578: @inject IMediator Mediator
579: 
580: <MudTable ServerData="@LoadServerData" @* Key for server-side operations *@
581:           Dense="true"
582:           Hover="true"
583:           @ref="_table"> @* Ref to component instance for programmatic control *@
584:     <ToolBarContent>
585:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">{Entities}</MudText>
586:         <MudSpacer />
587:         <MudTextField @bind-Value="_searchString"
588:                       Placeholder="Search"
589:                       Adornment="Adornment.Start"
590:                       AdornmentIcon="@Filled.Search"
591:                       IconSize="Size.Medium"
592:                       Class="mt-0"
593:                       Immediate="true"
594:                       DebounceInterval="300"
595:                       OnDebounceIntervalElapsed="OnSearch" /> @* Debounced search *@
596:     </ToolBarContent>
597:     <HeaderContent>
598:         <MudTh>
599:             <MudTableSortLabel SortLabel="title" T="{Entity}ListDto"> @* SortLabel is key for ServerData *@
600:                 Title
601:             </MudTableSortLabel>
602:         </MudTh>
603:         <MudTh>
604:             <MudTableSortLabel SortLabel="date" T="{Entity}ListDto">
605:                 Date
606:             </MudTableSortLabel>
607:         </MudTh>
608:         <MudTh>Location</MudTh>
609:     </HeaderContent>
610:     <RowTemplate>
611:         <MudTd DataLabel="Title">@context.Title</MudTd>
612:         <MudTd DataLabel="Date">@context.StartDate.ToShortDateString()</MudTd>
613:         <MudTd DataLabel="Location">@context.Location</MudTd>
614:     </RowTemplate>
615:     <NoRecordsContent>
616:         <MudText>No {entities} found</MudText>
617:     </NoRecordsContent>
618:     <LoadingContent>
619:         <MudProgressCircular Indeterminate="true" />
620:     </LoadingContent>
621:     <PagerContent> @* Table pager component *@
622:         <MudTablePager PageSizeOptions="new int[] { 10, 25, 50, 100 }" />
623:     </PagerContent>
624: </MudTable>
625: 
626: @code {
627:     private MudTable<{Entity}ListDto>? _table;
628:     private string _searchString = string.Empty;
629: 
630:     // This method is called by MudTable for server-side data fetching
631:     private async Task<TableData<{Entity}ListDto>> LoadServerData(
632:         TableState state,
633:         CancellationToken token)
634:     {
635:         // Build request for backend (e.g., CQRS Query)
636:         var request = new Get{Entity}ListRequest
637:         {
638:             Page = state.Page + 1,  // MudTable is 0-indexed, API is 1-indexed
639:             PageSize = state.PageSize,
640:             SearchTerm = _searchString,
641:             SortBy = state.SortLabel,
642:             SortDescending = state.SortDirection == SortDirection.Descending
643:         };
644: 
645:         var response = await Mediator.Send(request, token); // Assume response has {Entities} and TotalCount
646: 
647:         return new TableData<{Entity}ListDto>
648:         {
649:             Items = response.{Entities},
650:             TotalItems = response.TotalCount
651:         };
652:     }
653: 
654:     private void OnSearch()
655:     {
656:         _table?.ReloadServerData(); // Trigger data reload on search change
657:     }
658: }
659: ```
660: 
661: ---
662: 
663: ## 7. MudCard - Information Cards
664: 
665: MudCard is a flexible content container with options for media, header, content, and actions.
666: 
667: ```razor
668: <MudCard Elevation="4" Class="my-4">
669:     <MudCardMedia Image="@{entity}ImageUrl" Height="200" />
670:     <MudCardHeader>
671:         <CardHeaderContent>
672:             <MudText Typo="Typo.h5">@{entity}Title</MudText>
673:             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary">
674:                 @{entity}Date.ToShortDateString()
675:             </MudText>
676:         </CardHeaderContent>
677:     </MudCardHeader>
678:     <MudCardContent>
679:         <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Class="mt-2">
680:             @{entity}Description
681:         </MudText>
682:     </MudCardContent>
683:     <MudCardActions Class="d-flex justify-end">
684:         <MudButton Variant="Variant.Text" Color="Color.Primary">
685:             Learn More
686:         </MudButton>
687:         <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled" Color="Color.Primary">
688:             Register
689:         </MudButton>
690:     </MudCardActions>
691: </MudCard>
692: ```
693: 
694: ---
695: 
696: ## 8. MudSnackbar - Notifications
697: 
698: MudSnackbar provides transient messages to users, used for success, error, warning, and info notifications.
699: 
700: ```razor
701: @inject ISnackbar Snackbar
702: 
703: <MudButton OnClick="ShowSuccess">Show Success</MudButton>
704: <MudButton OnClick="ShowError">Show Error</MudButton>
705: <MudButton OnClick="ShowWarning">Show Warning</MudButton>
706: <MudButton OnClick="ShowInfo">Show Info</MudButton>
707: 
708: @code {
709:     private void ShowSuccess()
710:     {
711:         Snackbar.Add("{Entity} created successfully!", Severity.Success, config =>
712:         {
713:             config.ShowCloseIcon = false; // Custom config for this snackbar
714:         });
715:     }
716: 
717:     private void ShowError()
718:     {
719:         Snackbar.Add("Failed to delete {entity}", Severity.Error);
720:     }
721: 
722:     private void ShowWarning()
723:     {
724:         Snackbar.Add("{Entity} capacity almost full", Severity.Warning);
725:     }
726: 
727:     private void ShowInfo()
728:     {
729:         Snackbar.Add("{Entity} updated", Severity.Info);
730:     }
731: }
732: ```
733: 
734: ### Snackbar Configuration
735: 
736: Configure global Snackbar behavior in `{Project}.Blazor/Program.cs`.
737: 
738: ```csharp
739: // File: {Project}.Blazor/Program.cs
740: builder.Services.AddMudServices(config =>
741: {
742:     config.SnackbarConfiguration.PositionClass = Defaults.Classes.Position.BottomRight; // Position
743:     config.SnackbarConfiguration.PreventDuplicates = false; // Allow duplicate messages
744:     config.SnackbarConfiguration.NewestOnTop = true; // Stack new messages on top
745:     config.SnackbarConfiguration.ShowCloseIcon = true; // Display close icon
746:     config.SnackbarConfiguration.VisibleStateDuration = 4000; // Duration in ms
747:     config.SnackbarConfiguration.HideTransitionDuration = 500;
748:     config.SnackbarConfiguration.ShowTransitionDuration = 500;
749:     config.SnackbarConfiguration.SnackbarVariant = Variant.Filled; // Default appearance
750: });
751: ```
752: 
753: ---
754: 
755: ## 9. MudContainer - Layout Container
756: 
757: Used to center and constrain content within a page, providing consistent margins.
758: 
759: ```razor
760: <MudContainer MaxWidth="MaxWidth.Large" Class="my-4"> @* MaxWidth constrains content, my-4 adds vertical margin *@
761:     <MudText Typo="Typo.h4">{Entities} Overview</MudText>
762:     @* All your page content goes here *@
763: </MudContainer>
764: ```
765: 
766: ### `MaxWidth` Options
767: 
768: *   `MaxWidth.ExtraSmall` - 600px
769: *   `MaxWidth.Small` - 960px
770: *   `MaxWidth.Medium` - 1280px
771: *   `MaxWidth.Large` - 1920px
772: *   `MaxWidth.ExtraLarge` - 2560px
773: *   `MaxWidth.False` - No maximum width (fills available space)
774: 
775: ---
776: 
777: ## Best Practices for MudBlazor Components
778: 
779: | Component | Best Practice |
780: |-----------|---------------|
781: | **MudGrid** | Always use `MudGrid` and `MudItem` for layout, leverage `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` for responsiveness. |
782: | **MudButton** | Use `Variant.Filled` for primary actions, `Variant.Outlined` for secondary, `Variant.Text` for tertiary. Prefer `Color.Primary` or `Color.Secondary` for main actions. |
783: | **MudTextField** | Always include `Label`, use `Variant.Outlined`. Leverage `Required`, `RequiredError`, `MaxLength`, `Counter`, and `Validation` for input. |
784: | **MudSelect** | Use `ToStringFunc` when binding to complex objects. Consider `Clearable` and `MultiSelection` as needed. |
785: | **MudDialog** | Use `IDialogService` for programmatic control. Centralize common dialogs (e.g., confirmation) into reusable components. |
786: | **MudTable** | For large datasets, use `ServerData` for efficient pagination, sorting, and filtering. |
787: | **MudCard** | Great for displaying grouped information. Use `Elevation` and `Class` for styling. |
788: | **MudSnackbar** | Use `Snackbar.Add` with appropriate `Severity` levels. Configure global settings in `Program.cs`. |
789: | **MudContainer** | Use with `MaxWidth` to ensure content readability and alignment across screen sizes. |
790: 
791: ---
792: 
793: **Related Resources**:
794: - [component-design.md](component-design.md) - General Blazor component best practices.
795: - [state-management.md](state-management.md) - Handling state interactions with UI components.
796: - [common-patterns.md](common-patterns.md) - Full examples of forms, tables, and dialogs.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-ui-conventions/resources/render-modes.md
````markdown
  1: # Render Modes - Blazor Interactive Modes
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Blazor Render Mode Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: This document explains the various Blazor render modes and provides guidance on when to use each in hybrid Blazor applications. Understanding render modes is crucial for optimizing performance, user experience, and resource usage.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. Blazor Hybrid Architecture
 12: 
 13: A typical hybrid Blazor application combines Blazor Server for initial page loads and server-side logic, and Blazor WebAssembly for client-side interactivity and offline capabilities. This is achieved primarily through the `InteractiveAuto` render mode.
 14: 
 15: ```mermaid
 16: graph TD
 17:     subgraph Blazor Hybrid Application
 18:         A[{Project}.Blazor (Server Project)] -- Initial Render / Server Interactivity --> B[Browser (Client)]
 19:         C[{Project}.Blazor.Client (WASM Project)] -- Client-side Interactivity --> B
 20:     end
 21: 
 22:     subgraph Key Characteristics
 23:         S1[Blazor Server (BFF)] --> S2(OIDC Auth, HttpContext, YARP Proxy)
 24:         W1[Blazor WebAssembly] --> W2(Runs in browser, Offline, Low Latency)
 25:         Auto[InteractiveAuto Render Mode] --> Auto1(Starts Server-side, transitions to WASM)
 26:     end
 27: 
 28:     B -- Downloads WASM in background --> C
 29:     BFF -- Forwards API calls --> API_Backend[{Project}.API (Backend)]
 30: 
 31:     S2 --- S1
 32:     W2 --- W1
 33:     Auto1 --- Auto
 34: ```
 35: 
 36: ---
 37: 
 38: ## 2. Overview of Available Render Modes
 39: 
 40: Blazor provides four primary render modes, each with distinct characteristics regarding where the UI is rendered and where event handling occurs.
 41: 
 42: | Render Mode | Execution Location | Interactivity | Initial Load Time | Server Load | Offline Support | Use Case |
 43: |-------------|--------------------|---------------|-------------------|-------------|-----------------|----------|
 44: | **Static Server Rendering (SSR)** | Server | No | Fastest | Low | No | Static pages (About, Privacy) |
 45: | **Interactive Server** | Server (via SignalR) | Yes | Fast | High | No | Server-dependent logic (HttpContext), administrative dashboards |
 46: | **Interactive WebAssembly** | Browser (WASM) | Yes | Slow (initial) | Low | Yes | Highly interactive, offline-capable features (games, rich editors) |
 47: | **Interactive Auto** | Server (initially) then Browser (WASM) | Yes | Fast | Medium (initially) | Partial | Default for most interactive pages in hybrid apps |
 48: 
 49: ---
 50: 
 51: ## 3. InteractiveAuto (Project Default)
 52: 
 53: **InteractiveAuto** mode is the recommended default for most interactive components in a Blazor Hybrid application. It offers a balance between fast initial load times and client-side performance.
 54: 
 55: ### How It Works:
 56: 
 57: 1.  **Initial Load**: The component is rendered and handled server-side (like Interactive Server). This ensures a very fast first page load.
 58: 2.  **WASM Download**: In the background, the Blazor WebAssembly runtime and application assets (`.wasm` files) are downloaded to the client's browser.
 59: 3.  **Seamless Transition**: Once the WebAssembly assets are downloaded, the component's interactivity is seamlessly transferred to the client. The SignalR connection is terminated, and subsequent interactions are handled directly by the browser-side WebAssembly.
 60: 4.  **Subsequent Visits**: On later visits, if the WebAssembly assets are cached, the component will render and operate client-side immediately.
 61: 
 62: ### Usage:
 63: 
 64: Apply `InteractiveAuto` to routable components (`@page` directive) or individual interactive components.
 65: 
 66: ```razor
 67: @page "/{entities}"
 68: @rendermode InteractiveAuto @* Apply to the root component of the interactive part *@
 69: 
 70: <PageTitle>{Entities}</PageTitle>
 71: 
 72: <MudContainer>
 73:     <MudText Typo="Typo.h4">Upcoming {Entities}</MudText>
 74:     @* Your interactive component content here *@
 75: </MudContainer>
 76: 
 77: @code {
 78:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 79:     {
 80:         // This method will execute twice with prerendering: once on the server, then on the client.
 81:         // Be mindful of side effects that should only occur once (e.g., fetching data that's already part of the prerendered HTML).
 82:     }
 83: }
 84: ```
 85: 
 86: ### When to Use InteractiveAuto:
 87: 
 88: *   **Default for Interactive Components**: When you need client-side interactivity (buttons, forms, dynamic content).
 89: *   **Optimized User Experience**: Provides a fast initial page load (server-rendered) and low-latency interactivity (client-rendered).
 90: *   **Most Pages**: Suitable for most application pages where interactivity is key.
 91: 
 92: ### When NOT to Use InteractiveAuto:
 93: 
 94: *   **Server-Only Dependencies**: If a component *must* access server-side resources like `HttpContext` or the file system (use `InteractiveServer`).
 95: *   **Very Small Static Content**: For purely static pages, `Static Server Rendering` is more efficient (no WASM download overhead).
 96: 
 97: ---
 98: 
 99: ## 4. InteractiveServer
100: 
101: **Interactive Server** mode keeps the component's UI and event handling on the server, using a SignalR connection to communicate UI updates and events to/from the client.
102: 
103: ### How It Works:
104: 
105: 1.  **Server-Side Rendering**: The UI is rendered on the server and sent as HTML to the client.
106: 2.  **SignalR Connection**: A persistent SignalR connection is established between the client and the server.
107: 3.  **Event Handling**: User interactions (e.g., button clicks) are sent via SignalR to the server.
108: 4.  **UI Updates**: The server processes the event, updates the component's state, recalculates the UI diff, and sends only the necessary changes back to the client via SignalR, which then updates the DOM.
109: 
110: ### Usage:
111: 
112: ```razor
113: @page "/admin/system-status"
114: @rendermode InteractiveServer
115: 
116: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor @* Access to HttpContext is server-only *@
117: 
118: <MudContainer>
119:     <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">Server Time: @_serverTime</MudText>
120:     <MudText>User IP: @_userIp</MudText>
121:     <MudButton OnClick="RefreshStatus">Refresh</MudButton>
122: </MudContainer>
123: 
124: @code {
125:     private string _serverTime = string.Empty;
126:     private string _userIp = string.Empty;
127: 
128:     protected override void OnInitialized()
129:     {
130:         // Can directly access server-side resources like HttpContext
131:         _serverTime = DateTime.Now.ToString("F");
132:         _userIp = HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString() ?? "Unknown";
133:     }
134: 
135:     private void RefreshStatus()
136:     {
137:         _serverTime = DateTime.Now.ToString("F");
138:         // StateHasChanged() is implicitly called after event handlers
139:     }
140: }
141: ```
142: 
143: ### When to Use InteractiveServer:
144: 
145: *   **Server-Side Access**: When a component *needs* direct access to server-side APIs, `HttpContext` (for cookies, IP address, headers), or the server's file system.
146: *   **Heavy Dependencies**: For components that rely on large server-side libraries or perform computationally intensive tasks.
147: *   **Real-Time Updates**: Ideal for applications requiring frequent, low-latency updates from the server (e.g., chat applications, dashboards).
148: 
149: ### When NOT to Use InteractiveServer:
150: 
151: *   **High Latency Concerns**: Each user interaction involves a round trip to the server, which can introduce noticeable latency for users geographically distant from the server.
152: *   **High Server Load**: Maintaining SignalR connections and rendering components server-side for many concurrent users can consume significant server resources.
153: *   **Offline Functionality**: Components in this mode cannot function offline.
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: ## 5. InteractiveWebAssembly
158: 
159: **Interactive WebAssembly** mode executes the component entirely client-side within the browser using WebAssembly.
160: 
161: ### How It Works:
162: 
163: 1.  **Initial Download**: The client browser downloads the .NET runtime (as WebAssembly) and the application's DLLs. This can be a significant initial download.
164: 2.  **Client-Side Execution**: Once downloaded, the entire component (UI, logic, event handling) runs directly in the user's browser, without any server round-trips for interactivity.
165: 3.  **API Communication**: Client-side components communicate with backend APIs via standard HTTP requests.
166: 
167: ### Usage:
168: 
169: ```razor
170: @page "/offline-editor"
171: @rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly
172: 
173: @inject HttpClient Http
174: 
175: <MudContainer>
176:     <MudText Typo="Typo.h4">Offline {Entity} Editor</MudText>
177:     <MudTextField @bind-Value="{entity}Title" Label="{Entity} Title" />
178:     <MudButton OnClick="SaveDraft">Save Draft Locally</MudButton>
179:     <MudButton OnClick="SyncToServer">Sync to Server</MudButton>
180: </MudContainer>
181: 
182: @code {
183:     private string {entity}Title = string.Empty;
184: 
185:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
186:     {
187:         // Runs entirely in the browser (low interaction latency)
188:         // Can access browser storage APIs for offline persistence
189:     }
190: 
191:     private async Task SaveDraft()
192:     {
193:         // Logic to save draft to browser's IndexedDB or localStorage
194:     }
195: 
196:     private async Task SyncToServer()
197:     {
198:         // Make HTTP call to backend API
199:         // await Http.PostAsJsonAsync("api/v1/{entities}/drafts", draft{Entity});
200:     }
201: }
202: ```
203: 
204: ### When to Use InteractiveWebAssembly:
205: 
206: *   **Offline Functionality**: Essential for applications that need to work fully or partially offline (e.g., using service workers).
207: *   **Low Interaction Latency**: Ideal for highly interactive components (e.g., rich text editors, games, interactive diagrams) where immediate UI feedback is crucial.
208: *   **Reduced Server Load**: Once downloaded, the client handles all processing, significantly reducing the load on the server.
209: 
210: ### When NOT to Use InteractiveWebAssembly:
211: 
212: *   **Large Initial Download**: The initial download of the .NET runtime and application DLLs can be substantial (several MBs), leading to a slower initial page load.
213: *   **No Server-Side Access**: Components cannot directly access server-side resources (`HttpContext`, file system).
214: *   **SEO Concerns**: Prerendering helps, but dynamic content might still pose SEO challenges compared to pure server-rendered pages.
215: 
216: ---
217: 
218: ## 6. Static Server Rendering (SSR)
219: 
220: **Static Server Rendering (SSR)** is the most basic render mode, where components are rendered once on the server into static HTML. There is no interactivity.
221: 
222: ### How It Works:
223: 
224: 1.  **Server-Side Render**: The component is rendered into HTML on the server.
225: 2.  **Static HTML Delivery**: The resulting static HTML is sent to the client.
226: 3.  **No Interactivity**: No JavaScript bundle is loaded, and no SignalR connection is established for the component. User interactions on such pages will require a full page refresh.
227: 
228: ### Usage:
229: 
230: For static pages like "About Us" or "Privacy Policy," where no client-side interaction is needed.
231: 
232: ```razor
233: @page "/about"
234: @* No @rendermode directive means Static SSR by default *@
235: 
236: <PageTitle>About {Project}</PageTitle>
237: 
238: <MudContainer MaxWidth="MaxWidth.Medium">
239:     <MudText Typo="Typo.h4" Class="mb-4">About Us</MudText>
240:     <MudText Class="mb-3">
241:         {Project} is a platform designed to connect
242:         communities with engaging content.
243:     </MudText>
244:     <MudText Class="mb-3">
245:         Our mission is to foster knowledge, strengthen bonds, and facilitate access
246:         to high-quality resources.
247:     </MudText>
248:     <MudLink Href="https://example.org" Target="_blank">Learn more</MudLink>
249: </MudContainer>
250: 
251: @code {
252:     // No interactive C# code here, as the component is static
253: }
254: ```
255: 
256: ### When to Use Static SSR:
257: 
258: *   **Static Content**: Ideal for pages with purely static content that doesn't require any client-side interaction.
259: *   **SEO Optimization**: Best for search engine optimization (SEO) as the full content is available in the initial HTML.
260: *   **Fastest Initial Load**: Since no WebAssembly runtime or SignalR connection is involved, these pages load extremely quickly.
261: 
262: ### When NOT to Use Static SSR:
263: 
264: *   **Any Interactivity**: Not suitable for pages that require any form of user interaction (buttons, forms, dynamic updates).
265: 
266: ---
267: 
268: ## 7. Mixing Render Modes
269: 
270: You can use different render modes for different components within the same application, or even on the same page.
271: 
272: ### Page-Level Render Mode
273: 
274: Apply `@rendermode` to the `@page` directive for the entire page's interactivity.
275: 
276: ```razor
277: @page "/{entities}"
278: @rendermode InteractiveAuto @* This page and its children are InteractiveAuto *@
279: ```
280: 
281: ### Per-Component Render Mode
282: 
283: Apply `@rendermode` to individual component tags to override the page's render mode or make a specific component interactive on a static page.
284: 
285: ```razor
286: @page "/static-page" @* Static SSR by default *@
287: 
288: <MudContainer>
289:     <MudText Typo="Typo.h4">Static Content</MudText>
290: 
291:     @* This component will be interactive, running in InteractiveServer mode *@
292:     <LoginFormComponent @rendermode="InteractiveServer" />
293: 
294: </MudContainer>
295: ```
296: 
297: ---
298: 
299: ## 8. Prerendering
300: 
301: **Prerendering** is enabled by default for `InteractiveAuto`, `InteractiveServer`, and `InteractiveWebAssembly` components. It involves rendering the component on the server first to generate static HTML, which is sent to the client. Once the interactive host starts, the component is rendered again.
302: 
303: ### How Prerendering Affects Lifecycle:
304: 
305: *   **`OnInitializedAsync` runs twice**: Once during the server prerender, and again when the component is rendered interactively on the client.
306: *   **`OnAfterRenderAsync(true)` runs twice**: The first `firstRender` will be on the server, the second on the client.
307: 
308: ### Implications of Prerendering:
309: 
310: *   **Fast Initial UX**: Users see content immediately while the interactive client loads.
311: *   **SEO Friendly**: Search engines index the fully rendered HTML.
312: *   **Careful with Side Effects**: Avoid side effects (e.g., API calls, database writes) in `OnInitializedAsync` that should only happen once.
313: 
314: ### Best Practice for Prerendering with Side Effects:
315: 
316: Move logic with side effects to `OnAfterRenderAsync(true)` or ensure your code handles duplicate execution gracefully.
317: 
318: ```csharp
319: @page "/{entities}"
320: @rendermode @(new InteractiveAutoRenderMode(prerender: true)) @* Prerendering enabled *@
321: 
322: <MudContainer>
323:     @if (_{entities} == null)
324:     {
325:         <MudProgressCircular Indeterminate="true" />
326:     }
327:     else
328:     {
329:         @foreach (var item in _{entities})
330:         {
331:             <MudCard>@item.Title</MudCard>
332:         }
333:     }
334: </MudContainer>
335: 
336: @code {
337:     private List<{Entity}ListDto>? _{entities};
338: 
339:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
340:     {
341:         // Only fetch data once if it's not going to be part of the prerendered HTML or if side effects are handled
342:         // For data that is not critical for prerendering, consider fetching it only client-side.
343:     }
344: 
345:     protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
346:     {
347:         if (firstRender && OperatingSystem.IsBrowser()) // Ensure this only runs once on the client-side
348:         {
349:             // Fetch data here if it shouldn't run on the server prerender,
350:             // or if it's dependent on client-side state.
351:             // _{entities} = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<{Entity}ListDto>>("api/v1/{entities}");
352:             // StateHasChanged(); // Required if you update state after async operation in OnAfterRenderAsync
353:         }
354:     }
355: }
356: ```
357: 
358: ---
359: 
360: ## 9. Server vs. WASM Context Differences
361: 
362: It's critical to understand the differences in environment when developing Blazor Hybrid applications.
363: 
364: | Feature | Blazor Server | Blazor WebAssembly |
365: |---------|---------------|--------------------|
366: | **`HttpContext`** | Available | Not available |
367: | **File System Access** | Full server access | No direct access |
368: | **Database Access** | Direct via ORM | Via API calls only |
369: | **Environment Variables** | Server's variables | No direct access |
370: | **`IJSRuntime`** | Via SignalR (latency) | Direct browser access (low latency) |
371: | **`localStorage`/`sessionStorage`** | Via JS interop | Via JS interop (direct) |
372: | **Network Latency** | Higher (server round-trips) | Lower (client-side execution) |
373: | **CPU-Intensive Tasks** | On server | On client browser |
374: 
375: ### Server-Only Code Example:
376: 
377: ```razor
378: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor
379: 
380: @code {
381:     private string _userAgent = string.Empty;
382: 
383:     protected override void OnInitialized()
384:     {
385:         // This code will only run correctly in Blazor Server or during server prerendering
386:         _userAgent = HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Headers.UserAgent.ToString() ?? "Unknown";
387:     }
388: }
389: ```
390: 
391: ### WASM-Only Code Example:
392: 
393: ```razor
394: @inject IJSRuntime JSRuntime
395: 
396: @code {
397:     private string _themePreference = string.Empty;
398: 
399:     protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
400:     {
401:         if (firstRender && OperatingSystem.IsBrowser())
402:         {
403:             // This code is specifically for the browser environment
404:             _themePreference = await JSRuntime.InvokeAsync<string>("localStorage.getItem", "theme");
405:             StateHasChanged();
406:         }
407:     }
408: }
409: ```
410: 
411: ---
412: 
413: ## Best Practices for Render Modes
414: 
415: ### DO:
416: 
417: *   **Default to `InteractiveAuto`**: For most interactive components, `InteractiveAuto` provides the best balance of performance and user experience in a hybrid app.
418: *   **Use `InteractiveServer` for Server-Specific Needs**: Reserve `InteractiveServer` for components that genuinely require direct server-side access (e.g., `HttpContext`, file system).
419: *   **Use `InteractiveWebAssembly` for Offline/High Interactivity**: Leverage `InteractiveWebAssembly` for parts of the application that benefit from offline capabilities or extremely low interaction latency.
420: *   **Use Static SSR for Non-Interactive Content**: Optimize SEO and initial load times for purely static pages.
421: *   **Handle Prerendering Carefully**: Be aware of `OnInitializedAsync` running twice; move side effects to `OnAfterRenderAsync(firstRender && OperatingSystem.IsBrowser())` if they should only happen once on the client.
422: *   **Conditional Code Execution**: Use `OperatingSystem.IsBrowser()` or `OperatingSystem.IsOSPlatform("BROWSER")` to execute client-side specific code when needed.
423: 
424: ### DON'T:
425: 
426: *   **Don't Overuse `InteractiveServer`**: Avoid using `InteractiveServer` unnecessarily due to its higher server resource consumption and potential latency.
427: *   **Don't Assume `HttpContext` Availability**: Components in `InteractiveAuto` or `InteractiveWebAssembly` modes cannot reliably access `HttpContext`. Use the BFF pattern or server-side services for such needs.
428: *   **Don't Put Server-Side Logic in WASM**: Business logic that requires server resources (database, external APIs directly) should remain on the server (API project) and be accessed via HTTP calls from WASM.
429: 
430: ---
431: 
432: **Related Resources**:
433: - [component-design.md](component-design.md) - General Blazor component structure and lifecycle.
434: - [mudblazor-usage.md](mudblazor-usage.md) - UI framework-specific components.
435: - [state-management.md](state-management.md) - How render modes impact state management patterns.
436: - [`blazor-bff-patterns`](../../blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md) - Context on the Backend-for-Frontend architecture.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-ui-conventions/resources/state-management.md
````markdown
  1: # State Management - Blazor Application
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic State Management Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: This document provides a comprehensive overview of state management patterns and best practices for Blazor applications. Effective state management is crucial for building responsive, scalable, and maintainable Blazor UIs.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. State Management Approaches
 12: 
 13: Blazor offers several approaches to manage component state, each suited for different scenarios:
 14: 
 15: | Approach | Use Case | Scope | Mutability | Examples |
 16: |----------|----------|-------|------------|----------|
 17: | **Component State** | Simple, isolated data within a single component. | Single component instance | Mutable | Counter, form input values |
 18: | **Parameters** | Passing data from a parent component to a child component. | Parent to immediate child | Read-only (child perspective) | {Entity} data to a card component |
 19: | **EventCallback** | Notifying a parent component of events or changes from a child. | Child to immediate parent | N/A (event notification) | Button click, form submission |
 20: | **CascadingValue** | Sharing data down a deeply nested component hierarchy without prop-drilling. | Component tree | Read-only (typically) | Authentication state, theme settings |
 21: | **Scoped Services** | Sharing mutable state across multiple, unrelated components within the same user session (Blazor Server) or application instance (Blazor WebAssembly). | User session / App instance | Mutable | Filter criteria, shopping cart |
 22: | **Singleton Services** | Global, application-wide immutable state or configuration. Use sparingly for mutable state, and ensure thread safety. | Entire application | Mutable (carefully) / Read-only | Feature flags, application settings |
 23: 
 24: ---
 25: 
 26: ## 2. Component State
 27: 
 28: This is the most basic form of state management, where data is stored directly within the component's `@code` block.
 29: 
 30: ```razor
 31: @code {
 32:     private List<{Entity}ListDto> _{entities} = new(); // Private field for component's data
 33:     private bool _isLoading = false;
 34:     private string _searchTerm = string.Empty;
 35: 
 36:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 37:     {
 38:         _isLoading = true;
 39:         // Fetch {entities}
 40:         _isLoading = false;
 41:     }
 42: 
 43:     private void HandleSearch(string newSearchTerm)
 44:     {
 45:         _searchTerm = newSearchTerm;
 46:         // Re-filter {entities}
 47:     }
 48: }
 49: ```
 50: 
 51: **Best Practices**:
 52: *   Use private fields (often prefixed with `_`) for internal component state.
 53: *   Initialize collections (`new List<T>()`) to prevent null reference exceptions.
 54: *   Use nullable types (`?`) for optional data.
 55: 
 56: ---
 57: 
 58: ## 3. Parameters - Parent to Child Communication
 59: 
 60: Parameters are used to pass data from a parent component to its direct child component. They are typically unidirectional.
 61: 
 62: **Parent Component Example**:
 63: ```razor
 64: <{Entity}Card {Entity}="@selected{Entity}"
 65:            ShowDetails="true"
 66:            On{Entity}Selected="Handle{Entity}Selected" /> @* On{Entity}Selected is an EventCallback *@
 67: 
 68: @code {
 69:     private {Entity}Dto? selected{Entity}; // Data held by the parent
 70: 
 71:     private void Handle{Entity}Selected({IdType} {entity}Id)
 72:     {
 73:         // Logic to update parent state based on child action
 74:     }
 75: }
 76: ```
 77: 
 78: **Child Component (`{Entity}Card.razor`) Example**:
 79: ```razor
 80: <MudCard>
 81:     <MudCardContent>
 82:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">@{Entity}.Title</MudText>
 83:         @if (ShowDetails)
 84:         {
 85:             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2">@{Entity}.Description</MudText>
 86:         }
 87:     </MudCardContent>
 88: </MudCard>
 89: 
 90: @code {
 91:     [Parameter] // Marks this property as a parameter
 92:     public {Entity}Dto {Entity} { get; set; } = null!; // Parent passes {Entity} object
 93: 
 94:     [Parameter]
 95:     public bool ShowDetails { get; set; } // Parent passes a boolean flag
 96: }
 97: ```
 98: *For detailed usage and best practices for parameters, refer to [component-design.md](component-design.md).*
 99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ## 4. EventCallback - Child to Parent Communication
103: 
104: `EventCallback<T>` is the standard Blazor mechanism for a child component to notify its parent component about an event or a change, allowing the parent to react.
105: 
106: ### Basic EventCallback
107: 
108: ```razor
109: @* Child Component *@
110: <MudButton OnClick="NotifyParentSave">Save</MudButton>
111: 
112: @code {
113:     [Parameter]
114:     public EventCallback OnSave { get; set; } // No data passed
115: 
116:     private async Task NotifyParentSave()
117:     {
118:         await OnSave.InvokeAsync(); // Invokes the parent's registered method
119:     }
120: }
121: ```
122: 
123: ### EventCallback with Data
124: 
125: ```razor
126: @* Child Component *@
127: @code {
128:     [Parameter]
129:     public EventCallback<{IdType}> On{Entity}Deleted { get; set; } // Pass a {IdType} ({entity}Id) to parent
130: 
131:     private async Task Delete{Entity}()
132:     {
133:         // ... deletion logic ...
134:         await On{Entity}Deleted.InvokeAsync({entity}Id); // Notify parent with the deleted {entity}'s ID
135:     }
136: }
137: 
138: @* Parent Component *@
139: <{Entity}List On{Entity}Deleted="Handle{Entity}Deleted" />
140: 
141: @code {
142:     private async Task Handle{Entity}Deleted({IdType} {entity}Id)
143:     {
144:         Snackbar.Add($"{Entity} {{entity}Id} deleted successfully", Severity.Success);
145:         await Load{Entities}(); // Parent reloads its list of {entities}
146:     }
147: }
148: ```
149: *For detailed usage and best practices for EventCallback, refer to [component-design.md](component-design.md).*
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## 5. CascadingValue - Deep Hierarchy Data Sharing
154: 
155: `CascadingValue` is ideal for sharing data down a deeply nested component hierarchy without explicitly passing it through every intermediate component (prop-drilling). Common uses include authentication state, themes, or application-wide settings.
156: 
157: ### Basic CascadingValue Example
158: 
159: **`App.razor` (or a root layout component)**:
160: ```razor
161: <CascadingAuthenticationState> @* Provides AuthenticationStateProvider *@
162:     <CascadingValue Value="@_appTheme" Name="AppTheme"> @* Custom cascading value *@
163:         <Router AppAssembly="@typeof(App).Assembly">
164:             <Found Context="routeData">
165:                 <RouteView RouteData="@routeData" DefaultLayout="@typeof(MainLayout)" />
166:             </Found>
167:             <NotFound>
168:                 <LayoutView Layout="@typeof(MainLayout)">
169:                     <p role="alert">Sorry, there's nothing at this address.</p>
170:                 </LayoutView>
171:             </NotFound>
172:         </Router>
173:     </CascadingValue>
174: </CascadingAuthenticationState>
175: 
176: @code {
177:     private MudTheme _appTheme = new MudTheme(); // Example theme object
178: }
179: ```
180: 
181: **Consuming in a deeply nested child component**:
182: ```csharp
183: @code {
184:     [CascadingParameter] // For AuthenticationState, no Name needed
185:     public Task<AuthenticationState> AuthenticationState { get; set; } = null!;
186: 
187:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "AppTheme")] // Use Name to specify which value to cascade
188:     public MudTheme Theme { get; set; } = null!;
189: 
190:     private bool _isAuthenticated;
191:     private string _userName = string.Empty;
192: 
193:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
194:     {
195:         var authState = await AuthenticationState;
196:         _isAuthenticated = authState.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true;
197:         _userName = authState.User.Identity?.Name ?? "Guest";
198:         // Use Theme object
199:     }
200: }
201: ```
202: 
203: ### Theme Management Pattern
204: 
205: The application's dark/light theme setting is cascaded from `App.razor` based on a cookie, then consumed in `MainLayout.razor`.
206: 
207: **`App.razor`**:
208: ```razor
209: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor // Only available in Blazor Server
210: 
211: @code {
212:     private bool _isDarkTheme;
213: 
214:     protected override void OnInitialized()
215:     {
216:         // Read theme preference from cookie for initial render
217:         var themeCookie = HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Cookies["theme"];
218:         _isDarkTheme = themeCookie == "dark";
219:     }
220: }
221: 
222: <CascadingValue Value="_isDarkTheme" Name="InitialTheme">
223:     <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" /> @* Renders root routes *@
224: </CascadingValue>
225: ```
226: 
227: **`MainLayout.razor`**:
228: ```razor
229: @inherits LayoutComponentBase
230: 
231: @code {
232:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")]
233:     public bool InitialIsDarkTheme { get; set; } // Consumes the cascaded value
234: 
235:     private MudTheme _currentTheme = new MudTheme();
236:     private bool _isDarkMode;
237: 
238:     protected override void OnInitialized()
239:     {
240:         _isDarkMode = InitialIsDarkTheme; // Initialize local state from cascaded value
241:         // Further theme customization if needed
242:     }
243: }
244: 
245: <MudThemeProvider @bind-IsDarkMode="_isDarkMode" Theme="_currentTheme" />
246: <MudDialogProvider />
247: <MudSnackbarProvider />
248: 
249: @body
250: ```
251: *For more details on theming, refer to [theming.md](theming.md).*
252: 
253: ---
254: 
255: ## 6. Scoped Services - Shared State Across Components
256: 
257: Scoped services are excellent for managing shared, mutable state that needs to persist across multiple components within the same user session (Blazor Server) or application instance (Blazor WebAssembly).
258: 
259: ### Create a State Service
260: 
261: ```csharp
262: // Services/{Entity}StateService.cs
263: using System;
264: using System.Collections.Generic;
265: 
266: public class {Entity}StateService
267: {
268:     private {IdType}? _selected{Entity}Id; // The shared state
269: 
270:     // Event to notify subscribers when state changes
271:     public event Action? OnChange;
272: 
273:     public {IdType}? Selected{Entity}Id
274:     {
275:         get => _selected{Entity}Id;
276:         set
277:         {
278:             if (_selected{Entity}Id != value) // Only update if value changed
279:             {
280:                 _selected{Entity}Id = value;
281:                 NotifyStateChanged(); // Notify subscribers
282:             }
283:         }
284:     }
285: 
286:     private void NotifyStateChanged() => OnChange?.Invoke();
287: }
288: ```
289: 
290: ### Register the Service
291: 
292: Register scoped services in `Program.cs` for both `{Project}.Blazor` (Server) and `{Project}.Blazor.Client` (WebAssembly).
293: 
294: **`Program.cs` (Blazor Server or WASM)**:
295: ```csharp
296: builder.Services.AddScoped<{Entity}StateService>();
297: ```
298: 
299: ### Use the Service in Components
300: 
301: **Component A (Sets State)**:
302: ```razor
303: @inject {Entity}StateService {Entity}State // Inject the service
304: 
305: <MudButton OnClick="Select{Entity}">Select This {Entity}</MudButton>
306: 
307: @code {
308:     [Parameter] public {IdType} {Entity}Id { get; set; }
309: 
310:     private void Select{Entity}()
311:     {
312:         {Entity}State.Selected{Entity}Id = {Entity}Id; // Update the shared state
313:     }
314: }
315: ```
316: 
317: **Component B (Reacts to State)**:
318: ```razor
319: @inject {Entity}StateService {Entity}State
320: @implements IDisposable // Implement IDisposable for event cleanup
321: 
322: <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">Currently Selected {Entity}: @{Entity}State.Selected{Entity}Id</MudText>
323: 
324: @code {
325:     protected override void OnInitialized()
326:     {
327:         {Entity}State.OnChange += StateHasChanged; // Subscribe to state changes, force re-render
328:     }
329: 
330:     public void Dispose()
331:     {
332:         {Entity}State.OnChange -= StateHasChanged; // Unsubscribe to prevent memory leaks
333:     }
334: }
335: ```
336: 
337: ### Advanced State Service with `IMediator`
338: 
339: Services can also encapsulate logic for fetching or updating state using `IMediator`.
340: 
341: ```csharp
342: // Services/{ParentEntity}StateService.cs
343: using System;
344: using System.Collections.Generic;
345: using System.Threading.Tasks;
346: using MediatR;
347: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{ParentEntity};
348: using {Project}.Application.Features.{ParentEntities}.Requests.Queries;
349: 
350: public class {ParentEntity}StateService
351: {
352:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
353:     private List<{ParentEntity}Dto> _{parentEntities} = new();
354:     private bool _isLoaded;
355: 
356:     public {ParentEntity}StateService(IMediator mediator)
357:     {
358:         _mediator = mediator;
359:     }
360: 
361:     public event Action? OnChange;
362: 
363:     public IReadOnlyList<{ParentEntity}Dto> {ParentEntities} => _{parentEntities}.AsReadOnly(); // Read-only access
364: 
365:     public async Task Load{ParentEntities}Async()
366:     {
367:         if (_isLoaded) return; // Load only once per session/instance
368: 
369:         var request = new Get{ParentEntity}ListRequest();
370:         _{parentEntities} = await _mediator.Send(request);
371:         _isLoaded = true;
372:         NotifyStateChanged();
373:     }
374: 
375:     public async Task Refresh{ParentEntities}Async()
376:     {
377:         _isLoaded = false; // Force reload
378:         await Load{ParentEntities}Async();
379:     }
380: 
381:     private void NotifyStateChanged() => OnChange?.Invoke();
382: }
383: ```
384: 
385: ---
386: 
387: ## 7. Singleton Services - Global State
388: 
389: Singleton services persist for the entire application lifetime. They are best suited for truly global, immutable data (e.g., application configuration, feature flags). Avoid using them for mutable state unless carefully managed for thread safety, especially in Blazor Server.
390: 
391: ```csharp
392: // Services/ApplicationConfigService.cs
393: public class ApplicationConfigService
394: {
395:     public string AppVersion { get; } = "1.0.0";
396:     public bool FeatureXEnabled { get; } = true;
397:     public DateTime AppStartUpTime { get; } = DateTime.UtcNow;
398: }
399: ```
400: 
401: **Register**:
402: ```csharp
403: builder.Services.AddSingleton<ApplicationConfigService>();
404: ```
405: 
406: **Use**:
407: ```razor
408: @inject ApplicationConfigService Config
409: 
410: <MudText>App Version: @Config.AppVersion</MudText>
411: ```
412: 
413: **Warning**: In Blazor Server, a singleton service is shared across *all users*. Any mutable state in a singleton will be visible and modifiable by every connected user, potentially leading to critical bugs and security vulnerabilities. Use `AddScoped` for per-user state.
414: 
415: ---
416: 
417: ## 8. State Management Patterns Summary
418: 
419: ### Pattern 1: Parent Manages State
420: 
421: The parent component holds the shared state and passes it down to children via parameters. Children use `EventCallback` to inform the parent of changes.
422: 
423: ```razor
424: @* Parent Component *@
425: <{Entity}List {Entities}="@_{entities}" On{Entity}Selected="HandleSelection" />
426: <{Entity}Details {Entity}="@_selected{Entity}" />
427: 
428: @code {
429:     private List<{Entity}ListDto> _{entities} = new();
430:     private {Entity}Dto? _selected{Entity};
431: 
432:     private async Task HandleSelection({IdType} {entity}Id)
433:     {
434:         // Parent fetches details and updates state, which re-renders {Entity}Details
435:         var request = new Get{Entity}DetailRequest { Id = {entity}Id };
436:         _selected{Entity} = await Mediator.Send(request);
437:     }
438: }
439: ```
440: 
441: ### Pattern 2: Service Manages State (Recommended for Unrelated Components)
442: 
443: A scoped service holds the shared state, and components inject the service to read/update the state and subscribe to change notifications.
444: 
445: ```csharp
446: // Component A (Publishes change)
447: @inject {Entity}StateService State
448: 
449: <MudButton OnClick="Select">Select {Entity}</MudButton>
450: 
451: @code {
452:     [Parameter] public {IdType} {Entity}Id { get; set; }
453:     private void Select() => State.Selected{Entity}Id = {Entity}Id;
454: }
455: 
456: // Component B (Subscribes to change)
457: @inject {Entity}StateService State
458: @implements IDisposable
459: 
460: <MudText>Currently Selected {Entity}: @State.Selected{Entity}Id</MudText>
461: 
462: @code {
463:     protected override void OnInitialized() => State.OnChange += StateHasChanged;
464:     public void Dispose() => State.OnChange -= StateHasChanged;
465: }
466: ```
467: 
468: ---
469: 
470: ## 9. Authentication State
471: 
472: Blazor provides robust built-in mechanisms for managing user authentication and authorization state.
473: 
474: ### Accessing Authentication State Declaratively (`AuthorizeView`)
475: 
476: ```razor
477: <CascadingAuthenticationState>
478:     <AuthorizeView>
479:         <Authorized>
480:             <MudText>Welcome, @context.User.Identity?.Name!</MudText>
481:             <MudButton OnClick="Create{Entity}">Create {Entity}</MudButton>
482:         </Authorized>
483:         <NotAuthorized>
484:             <MudButton Href="/login">Login to Create {Entities}</MudButton>
485:         </NotAuthorized>
486:         <Authorizing>
487:             <MudProgressCircular Indeterminate="true" Size="Size.Small" /> Loading authentication...
488:         </Authorizing>
489:     </AuthorizeView>
490: </CascadingAuthenticationState>
491: ```
492: 
493: ### Accessing Authentication State Programmatically
494: 
495: ```razor
496: @inject AuthenticationStateProvider AuthStateProvider
497: 
498: @code {
499:     private UserDto? _currentUser;
500:     private bool _isAuthenticated;
501: 
502:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
503:     {
504:         var authState = await AuthStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();
505:         var user = authState.User; // ClaimsPrincipal object
506: 
507:         _isAuthenticated = user.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true;
508: 
509:         if (_isAuthenticated)
510:         {
511:             _currentUser = new UserDto
512:             {
513:                 Id = {IdType}.TryParse(user.FindFirst("sub")?.Value, out var id) ? id : default,
514:                 Email = user.FindFirst("email")?.Value ?? string.Empty,
515:                 Name = user.Identity.Name ?? string.Empty,
516:                 // Extract other claims as needed
517:             };
518:         }
519:     }
520: }
521: ```
522: 
523: ### Role-Based Authorization
524: 
525: ```razor
526: <AuthorizeView Roles="Admin,{ParentEntity}Manager"> @* Only visible to users with Admin OR {ParentEntity}Manager role *@
527:     <Authorized>
528:         <MudButton>Delete {Entity}</MudButton>
529:     </Authorized>
530:     <NotAuthorized>
531:         <MudText Color="Color.Error">Access Denied: Insufficient Permissions</MudText>
532:     </NotAuthorized>
533: </AuthorizeView>
534: ```
535: 
536: ---
537: 
538: **Related Resources**:
539: - [component-design.md](component-design.md) - Component lifecycle and parameter basics.
540: - [`blazor-bff-patterns`](../../blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md) - Authentication state serialization and token forwarding for hybrid apps.
541: - [`auth-patterns`](../../auth-patterns/SKILL.md) - General authentication and authorization rules.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-ui-conventions/resources/theming.md
````markdown
  1: # Theming - Consistent UI Styling
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Theming Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: This document outlines the theming strategy for Blazor applications using MudBlazor, focusing on customizing themes, managing dark/light modes, and ensuring a consistent visual identity.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. MudBlazor Theming Basics
 12: 
 13: MudBlazor uses a theming system that allows customization of colors, typography, shadows, and more. The primary entry point for customization is the `MudThemeProvider` component, typically placed in `MainLayout.razor`.
 14: 
 15: ### `MainLayout.razor` Theme Setup
 16: 
 17: ```razor
 18: @inherits LayoutComponentBase
 19: 
 20: <MudThemeProvider @bind-IsDarkMode="_isDarkMode" Theme="_currentTheme" />
 21: <MudDialogProvider />
 22: <MudSnackbarProvider />
 23: 
 24: <MudLayout>
 25:     <MudAppBar Elevation="0">
 26:         <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Menu" Color="Color.Inherit" Edge="Edge.Start" OnClick="@((e) => DrawerToggle())" />
 27:         <MudSpacer />
 28:         <MudSwitch @bind-Checked="@_isDarkMode" Color="Color.Primary" Label="Dark Mode" />
 29:         <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Custom.Brands.GitHub" Color="Color.Inherit" Link="https://github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor" Target="_blank" />
 30:     </MudAppBar>
 31:     <MudDrawer @bind-Open="@_drawerOpen" Elevation="1">
 32:         <MudDrawerHeader>
 33:             <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">{Project}</MudText>
 34:         </MudDrawerHeader>
 35:         <NavMenu />
 36:     </MudDrawer>
 37:     <MudMainContent>
 38:         <MudContainer MaxWidth="MaxWidth.Large" Class="my-4 pt-4">
 39:             @Body
 40:         </MudContainer>
 41:     </MudMainContent>
 42: </MudLayout>
 43: 
 44: @code {
 45:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")] // Consumed from App.razor
 46:     public bool InitialIsDarkTheme { get; set; }
 47: 
 48:     private bool _drawerOpen = true;
 49:     private bool _isDarkMode; // Bound to MudThemeProvider and MudSwitch
 50:     private MudTheme _currentTheme = new MudTheme(); // Default theme instance
 51: 
 52:     protected override void OnInitialized()
 53:     {
 54:         _isDarkMode = InitialIsDarkTheme; // Initialize from cascaded value
 55:         _currentTheme = {Project}Theme.CreateTheme(); // Load custom theme
 56:     }
 57: 
 58:     private void DrawerToggle()
 59:     {
 60:         _drawerOpen = !_drawerOpen;
 61:     }
 62: }
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: ### Custom `MudTheme` Definition
 66: 
 67: Define your custom theme settings in a static class or a dedicated file (e.g., `Shared/{Project}Theme.cs`).
 68: 
 69: **`Shared/{Project}Theme.cs`**:
 70: ```csharp
 71: using MudBlazor;
 72: 
 73: namespace {Project}.Blazor.Shared;
 74: 
 75: public static class {Project}Theme
 76: {
 77:     public static MudTheme CreateTheme()
 78:     {
 79:         var theme = new MudTheme()
 80:         {
 81:             Palette = new Palette()
 82:             {
 83:                 Primary = "#34685D", // Primary brand color
 84:                 Secondary = "#E0BBE4", // Secondary accent color
 85:                 Tertiary = "#957DAD", // Tertiary color
 86:                 Info = "#2196F3",
 87:                 Success = "#4CAF50",
 88:                 Warning = "#FFC107",
 89:                 Error = "#F44336",
 90:                 Dark = "#27272f",
 91:                 TextPrimary = "#34685D", // Primary text color
 92:                 TextSecondary = "rgba(0,0,0, 0.54)",
 93:                 AppbarBackground = "#34685D", // App bar color
 94:                 AppbarText = Colors.Shades.White,
 95:                 Background = Colors.Grey.Lighten5,
 96:                 DrawerBackground = "#34685D", // Drawer background color
 97:                 DrawerText = Colors.Shades.White,
 98:                 Surface = Colors.Shades.White,
 99:                 // ... more color definitions
100:             },
101:             PaletteDark = new Palette()
102:             {
103:                 Primary = "#58A293", // Lighter primary for dark mode
104:                 Secondary = "#FFD700", // Gold for accent
105:                 Tertiary = "#BB86FC",
106:                 Info = "#90CAF9",
107:                 Success = "#A5D6A7",
108:                 Warning = "#FFEB3B",
109:                 Error = "#EF9A9A",
110:                 Dark = "#27272f",
111:                 TextPrimary = Colors.Shades.White,
112:                 TextSecondary = "rgba(255,255,255, 0.70)",
113:                 AppbarBackground = "#27272f", // Dark app bar
114:                 AppbarText = Colors.Shades.White,
115:                 Background = "#303030", // Dark background
116:                 DrawerBackground = "#212121",
117:                 DrawerText = "rgba(255,255,255, 0.70)",
118:                 Surface = "#424242",
119:                 // ... more dark mode color definitions
120:             },
121:             Typography = new Typography()
122:             {
123:                 Default = new Default() { FontFamily = new[] { "Roboto", "Helvetica", "Arial", "sans-serif" } },
124:                 H1 = new H1() { FontSize = "3rem", FontWeight = 300, LineHeight = 1.167 },
125:                 // ... other typography settings
126:             },
127:             Shadows = new Shadow()
128:             {
129:                 // Custom shadows if needed
130:             },
131:             // ... other theme properties
132:         };
133:         return theme;
134:     }
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 2. Dark/Light Mode Switching
141: 
142: The application supports dynamic dark/light mode switching, with the preference persisted via cookies.
143: 
144: ### `App.razor` Theme Initialization (Server-side)
145: 
146: The `App.razor` component, running on the server initially, reads the theme preference from a cookie and cascades it down to `MainLayout.razor`.
147: 
148: ```razor
149: // File: {Project}.Blazor/App.razor
150: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor // Provides access to HttpContext
151: 
152: @code {
153:     private bool _isDarkTheme;
154: 
155:     protected override void OnInitialized()
156:     {
157:         // Read the 'theme' cookie to determine initial dark mode state
158:         var themeCookie = HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Cookies["theme"];
159:         _isDarkTheme = themeCookie == "dark";
160:     }
161: }
162: 
163: <CascadingValue Value="_isDarkTheme" Name="InitialTheme"> @* Cascades the initial theme state *@
164:     <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" /> @* Renders root routes *@
165: </CascadingValue>
166: ```
167: 
168: ### `MainLayout.razor` Theme Consumption and Persistence
169: 
170: `MainLayout.razor` consumes the cascaded theme value and includes a `MudSwitch` to allow users to toggle dark/light mode. The choice is then saved to a cookie.
171: 
172: ```razor
173: // File: {Project}.Blazor/Shared/MainLayout.razor
174: @inject IJSRuntime JS
175: 
176: @code {
177:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")]
178:     public bool InitialIsDarkTheme { get; set; } // Consumes the cascaded value
179: 
180:     private bool _isDarkMode; // Bound to MudThemeProvider and MudSwitch
181:     private MudTheme _currentTheme = new MudTheme();
182: 
183:     protected override void OnInitialized()
184:     {
185:         _isDarkMode = InitialIsDarkTheme;
186:         _currentTheme = {Project}Theme.CreateTheme(); // Load custom theme
187:     }
188: 
189:     protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
190:     {
191:         if (firstRender)
192:         {
193:             // Set up a watcher or initial check from local storage if needed in WASM
194:         }
195:     }
196: 
197:     private async Task OnDarkModeChanged(bool value)
198:     {
199:         // Save the theme preference to a cookie via JavaScript interop
200:         await JS.InvokeVoidAsync("setCookie", "theme", value ? "dark" : "light", 365);
201:         _isDarkMode = value; // Update local state, MudThemeProvider will react
202:         StateHasChanged(); // Force re-render if necessary
203:     }
204: }
205: 
206: <MudThemeProvider @bind-IsDarkMode="_isDarkMode" Theme="_currentTheme" />
207: <MudDialogProvider />
208: <MudSnackbarProvider />
209: 
210: <MudLayout>
211:     <MudAppBar>
212:         <MudSpacer />
213:         <MudSwitch @bind-Checked="_isDarkMode"
214:                    Color="Color.Primary"
215:                    Label="Dark Mode"
216:                    ValueChanged="OnDarkModeChanged" /> @* Event for persistence *@
217:     </MudAppBar>
218:     @* ... rest of layout ... *@
219: </MudLayout>
220: ```
221: 
222: ### JavaScript for Cookie Management
223: 
224: A simple JavaScript function to set/get cookies.
225: 
226: **`wwwroot/js/site.js`**:
227: ```javascript
228: window.setCookie = (name, value, days) => {
229:     let expires = "";
230:     if (days) {
231:         let date = new Date();
232:         date.setTime(date.getTime() + (days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
233:         expires = "; expires=" + date.toUTCString();
234:     }
235:     document.cookie = name + "=" + (value || "") + expires + "; path=/; SameSite=Lax";
236: };
237: 
238: window.getCookie = (name) => {
239:     let nameEQ = name + "=";
240:     let ca = document.cookie.split(';');
241:     for(let i=0; i < ca.length; i++) {
242:         let c = ca[i];
243:         while (c.charAt(0) === ' ') c = c.substring(1, c.length);
244:         if (c.indexOf(nameEQ) === 0) return c.substring(nameEQ.length, c.length);
245:     }
246:     return null;
247: };
248: ```
249: 
250: ---
251: 
252: ## 3. Custom CSS Overrides and Variables
253: 
254: For fine-grained control or overrides not possible through the `MudTheme` object, use custom CSS.
255: 
256: ### `wwwroot/css/site.css`
257: 
258: This file is for global styles and overrides.
259: 
260: ```css
261: /* Custom properties for consistency, e.g., for BEM blocks */
262: :root {
263:     --{project}-primary-color: #34685D;
264:     --{project}-secondary-color: #E0BBE4;
265:     --{project}-font-family: 'Roboto', sans-serif;
266: }
267: 
268: /* Override MudBlazor default typography */
269: body {
270:     font-family: var(--{project}-font-family);
271: }
272: 
273: h1.mud-typography-h1 {
274:     color: var(--{project}-primary-color);
275: }
276: 
277: /* Custom styles for components */
278: .{entity}-card {
279:     border: 1px solid var(--mud-palette-lines-default);
280:     border-radius: var(--mud-default-border-radius);
281:     box-shadow: var(--mud-shadow-1);
282: }
283: 
284: .{entity}-card__title {
285:     color: var(--{project}-primary-color);
286: }
287: ```
288: 
289: ### `wwwroot/css/variables.css` (Optional, for more granular control)
290: 
291: This file can define CSS variables for colors, spacing, etc., making them easily reusable across the application.
292: 
293: ```css
294: /* Global CSS variables */
295: :root {
296:     /* Colors */
297:     --{project}-color-primary: #34685D;
298:     --{project}-color-secondary: #E0BBE4;
299:     --{project}-color-accent: #FFD700;
300: 
301:     /* Spacing */
302:     --{project}-spacing-unit: 8px;
303:     --{project}-spacing-xs: var(--{project}-spacing-unit);
304:     --{project}-spacing-sm: calc(var(--{project}-spacing-unit) * 2);
305:     /* ... */
306: }
307: 
308: /* Use in other CSS files */
309: .my-component {
310:     padding: var(--{project}-spacing-sm);
311:     background-color: var(--{project}-color-primary);
312: }
313: ```
314: 
315: ---
316: 
317: ## 4. Best Practices for Theming
318: 
319: *   **Centralize `MudTheme`**: Define your primary light and dark themes in a dedicated static class (e.g., `{Project}Theme.cs`).
320: *   **Use CSS Variables**: Leverage MudBlazor's CSS variables (e.g., `var(--mud-palette-primary)`) and define your own (`--{project}-primary-color`) for consistent styling.
321: *   **BEM for Custom CSS**: Combine theming with BEM methodology for maintainable custom component styles.
322: *   **Minimal Global Overrides**: Keep `site.css` lean, focusing on broad overrides and global utilities.
323: *   **Test Dark/Light Mode**: Always test your application thoroughly in both dark and light modes to ensure readability and visual harmony.
324: *   **Accessible Colors**: Ensure sufficient contrast between text and background colors, especially for accessibility.
325: 
326: ---
327: 
328: **Related Resources**:
329: - [mudblazor-usage.md](mudblazor-usage.md) - For how to apply styling to specific MudBlazor components.
330: - [bem-methodology.md](bem-methodology.md) - Guidelines for structured CSS naming.
331: - [state-management.md](state-management.md) - How theme state is managed and cascaded.
````

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/dbcontext-patterns.md
````markdown
  1: # DbContext Patterns
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic DbContext Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## DbContext Structure
 10: 
 11: The DbContext is the central class for Entity Framework Core data access.
 12: 
 13: ### Basic DbContext
 14: 
 15: ```csharp
 16: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
 17: using {Project}.Domain;
 18: 
 19: namespace {Project}.Persistence;
 20: 
 21: public class {DbContext} : DbContext
 22: {
 23:     public {DbContext}(DbContextOptions<{DbContext}> options)
 24:         : base(options)
 25:     {
 26:     }
 27: 
 28:     protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
 29:     {
 30:         base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
 31: 
 32:         // Apply all IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> from assembly
 33:         modelBuilder.ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(typeof({DbContext}).Assembly);
 34:     }
 35: 
 36:     // DbSet properties for each entity
 37:     public DbSet<{Entity}> {Entities} { get; set; }
 38:     public DbSet<{ParentEntity}> {ParentEntities} { get; set; }
 39:     public DbSet<User> Users { get; set; }
 40: }
 41: ```
 42: 
 43: ---
 44: 
 45: ## DbSet Properties
 46: 
 47: DbSets represent tables in the database.
 48: 
 49: ```csharp
 50: public class {DbContext} : DbContext
 51: {
 52:     // ✅ Public DbSet properties
 53:     public DbSet<{Entity}> {Entities} { get; set; }
 54:     public DbSet<{ParentEntity}> {ParentEntities} { get; set; }
 55:     public DbSet<{LinkEntity}> {LinkEntities} { get; set; }
 56: 
 57:     // ⚠️ Nullable for optional entities
 58:     public DbSet<{Entity}Categories>? {Entity}Categories { get; set; }
 59: 
 60:     // ✅ Non-nullable for required entities (compiler nullability)
 61:     public DbSet<User> Users { get; set; } = null!;
 62: }
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: **Naming Convention**:
 66: - Plural form: `{Entities}`, `{ParentEntities}`, `Users`
 67: - PascalCase
 68: - Descriptive names matching domain language
 69: 
 70: ---
 71: 
 72: ## OnModelCreating - Entity Configuration
 73: 
 74: ### Apply Configurations from Assembly
 75: 
 76: **✅ Recommended** (project standard pattern):
 77: 
 78: ```csharp
 79: protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
 80: {
 81:     base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
 82: 
 83:     // ✅ Automatically applies all IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> in assembly
 84:     modelBuilder.ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(typeof({DbContext}).Assembly);
 85: }
 86: ```
 87: 
 88: ### Manual Configuration Application
 89: 
 90: ```csharp
 91: protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
 92: {
 93:     base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
 94: 
 95:     // ❌ Manual (not recommended - use ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly)
 96:     modelBuilder.ApplyConfiguration(new {Entity}Configuration());
 97:     modelBuilder.ApplyConfiguration(new {ParentEntity}Configuration());
 98:     // ... many more
 99: }
100: ```
101: 
102: **Why ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly?**
103: - ✅ Automatic discovery of all configurations
104: - ✅ No need to manually register each configuration
105: - ✅ Easier to maintain as new entities are added
106: 
107: ---
108: 
109: ## SaveChangesAsync Override
110: 
111: Override `SaveChangesAsync` for cross-cutting concerns.
112: 
113: ### Audit Logging Pattern
114: 
115: ```csharp
116: public override Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
117: {
118:     foreach (var entry in ChangeTracker.Entries())
119:     {
120:         if (entry.State == EntityState.Added)
121:         {
122:             // Log entity creation
123:             Console.WriteLine($"Creating {entry.Entity.GetType().Name}");
124:         }
125:         else if (entry.State == EntityState.Modified)
126:         {
127:             // Log entity update
128:             Console.WriteLine($"Updating {entry.Entity.GetType().Name}");
129:         }
130:         else if (entry.State == EntityState.Deleted)
131:         {
132:             // Log entity deletion
133:             Console.WriteLine($"Deleting {entry.Entity.GetType().Name}");
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:     return base.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
138: }
139: ```
140: 
141: ### Automatic Timestamps
142: 
143: ```csharp
144: public override Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
145: {
146:     var entries = ChangeTracker.Entries()
147:         .Where(e => e.Entity is BaseEntity &&
148:                     (e.State == EntityState.Added || e.State == EntityState.Modified));
149: 
150:     foreach (var entry in entries)
151:     {
152:         var entity = (BaseEntity)entry.Entity;
153: 
154:         if (entry.State == EntityState.Added)
155:         {
156:             entity.CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
157:         }
158: 
159:         entity.UpdatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
160:     }
161: 
162:     return base.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
163: }
164: ```
165: 
166: ### Soft Delete Pattern
167: 
168: ```csharp
169: public override Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
170: {
171:     var deletedEntries = ChangeTracker.Entries()
172:         .Where(e => e.Entity is ISoftDeletable && e.State == EntityState.Deleted);
173: 
174:     foreach (var entry in deletedEntries)
175:     {
176:         // Convert Delete to Update with IsDeleted flag
177:         entry.State = EntityState.Modified;
178:         ((ISoftDeletable)entry.Entity).IsDeleted = true;
179:         ((ISoftDeletable)entry.Entity).DeletedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
180:     }
181: 
182:     return base.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
183: }
184: ```
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## DbContext Configuration (Program.cs)
189: 
190: ### PostgreSQL Configuration
191: 
192: ```csharp
193: // Program.cs
194: using Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL;
195: 
196: builder.Services.AddDbContext<{DbContext}>(options =>
197: {
198:     options.UseNpgsql(
199:         builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection"),
200:         npgsqlOptions =>
201:         {
202:             // Enable retry on failure
203:             npgsqlOptions.EnableRetryOnFailure(
204:                 maxRetryCount: 3,
205:                 maxRetryDelay: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30),
206:                 errorCodesToAdd: null);
207: 
208:             // Use NetTopologySuite for PostGIS spatial data
209:             npgsqlOptions.UseNetTopologySuite();
210: 
211:             // Set command timeout
212:             npgsqlOptions.CommandTimeout(30);
213:         });
214: 
215:     // Enable sensitive data logging in development
216:     if (builder.Environment.IsDevelopment())
217:     {
218:         options.EnableSensitiveDataLogging();
219:         options.EnableDetailedErrors();
220:     }
221: });
222: ```
223: 
224: ### Connection String
225: 
226: **appsettings.json**:
227: ```json
228: {
229:   "ConnectionStrings": {
230:     "DefaultConnection": "Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database={project}_db;Username=postgres;Password=yourpassword;Include Error Detail=true"
231:   }
232: }
233: ```
234: 
235: **appsettings.Development.json**:
236: ```json
237: {
238:   "ConnectionStrings": {
239:     "DefaultConnection": "Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database={project}_dev;Username=postgres;Password=dev;Include Error Detail=true"
240:   }
241: }
242: ```
243: 
244: ---
245: 
246: ## DbContext Lifetime and Scoping
247: 
248: ### Scoped Lifetime (Default - Recommended)
249: 
250: ```csharp
251: // ✅ Scoped (one instance per HTTP request)
252: builder.Services.AddDbContext<{DbContext}>(options =>
253:     options.UseNpgsql(connectionString));
254: ```
255: 
256: **Why Scoped?**
257: - ✅ One DbContext instance per HTTP request
258: - ✅ Proper change tracking
259: - ✅ Automatic disposal
260: - ✅ Thread-safe within a request
261: 
262: ### Transient Lifetime (Not Recommended)
263: 
264: ```csharp
265: // ❌ DON'T use Transient for DbContext
266: builder.Services.AddDbContext<{DbContext}>(
267:     options => options.UseNpgsql(connectionString),
268:     ServiceLifetime.Transient);
269: ```
270: 
271: **Why Not Transient?**
272: - ❌ Multiple instances per request
273: - ❌ Change tracking issues
274: - ❌ Performance overhead
275: 
276: ### Singleton Lifetime (Never!)
277: 
278: ```csharp
279: // ❌ NEVER use Singleton for DbContext
280: builder.Services.AddDbContext<{DbContext}>(
281:     options => options.UseNpgsql(connectionString),
282:     ServiceLifetime.Singleton);
283: ```
284: 
285: **Why Never Singleton?**
286: - ❌ Not thread-safe
287: - ❌ Memory leaks
288: - ❌ Stale data
289: - ❌ Connection pool exhaustion
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: ## Change Tracker
294: 
295: The ChangeTracker tracks entity state changes.
296: 
297: ### Accessing Tracked Entities
298: 
299: ```csharp
300: public override Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
301: {
302:     // Get all tracked entities
303:     var entries = ChangeTracker.Entries();
304: 
305:     // Filter by state
306:     var addedEntities = ChangeTracker.Entries()
307:         .Where(e => e.State == EntityState.Added);
308: 
309:     var modifiedEntities = ChangeTracker.Entries()
310:         .Where(e => e.State == EntityState.Modified);
311: 
312:     // Filter by type
313:     var {entities} = ChangeTracker.Entries<{Entity}>();
314: 
315:     return base.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
316: }
317: ```
318: 
319: ### Entity States
320: 
321: | State | Description |
322: |-------|-------------|
323: | `Detached` | Entity not tracked by DbContext |
324: | `Unchanged` | Entity tracked, no changes |
325: | `Added` | Entity will be inserted |
326: | `Modified` | Entity will be updated |
327: | `Deleted` | Entity will be deleted |
328: 
329: ### Modifying Entity State
330: 
331: ```csharp
332: // Attach existing entity and mark as modified
333: var existing{Entity} = new {Entity} { Id = {entity}Id };
334: _dbContext.Attach(existing{Entity});
335: _dbContext.Entry(existing{Entity}).State = EntityState.Modified;
336: 
337: // Mark specific properties as modified
338: _dbContext.Entry(existing{Entity}).Property(e => e.Title).IsModified = true;
339: _dbContext.Entry(existing{Entity}).Property(e => e.Description).IsModified = true;
340: 
341: await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
342: ```
343: 
344: ---
345: 
346: ## Query Filters (Global Filters)
347: 
348: Global filters apply to all queries.
349: 
350: ### Soft Delete Filter
351: 
352: ```csharp
353: protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
354: {
355:     base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
356: 
357:     // Apply soft delete filter to all ISoftDeletable entities
358:     modelBuilder.Entity<{Entity}>()
359:         .HasQueryFilter(e => !e.IsDeleted);
360: 
361:     modelBuilder.Entity<{ParentEntity}>()
362:         .HasQueryFilter(o => !o.IsDeleted);
363: }
364: ```
365: 
366: ### Multi-Tenancy Filter
367: 
368: ```csharp
369: protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
370: {
371:     base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
372: 
373:     // Apply tenant filter (requires current tenant from DI)
374:     modelBuilder.Entity<{Entity}>()
375:         .HasQueryFilter(e => e.TenantId == _currentTenantId);
376: }
377: ```
378: 
379: ### Ignoring Query Filters
380: 
381: ```csharp
382: // Include soft-deleted entities
383: var all{Entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
384:     .IgnoreQueryFilters()
385:     .ToListAsync();
386: ```
387: 
388: ---
389: 
390: ## Performance Optimization
391: 
392: ### Disable Change Tracking for Read-Only Queries
393: 
394: ```csharp
395: // ✅ No tracking (faster for read-only)
396: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
397:     .AsNoTracking()
398:     .ToListAsync();
399: 
400: // ❌ With tracking (unnecessary for read-only)
401: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.ToListAsync();
402: ```
403: 
404: ### Split Queries for Large Includes
405: 
406: ```csharp
407: // ✅ Split into multiple queries (avoids cartesian explosion)
408: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
409:     .Include(o => o.{Entities})
410:     .Include(o => o.Members)
411:     .AsSplitQuery()
412:     .ToListAsync();
413: 
414: // ❌ Single query (can cause performance issues with multiple includes)
415: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
416:     .Include(o => o.{Entities})
417:     .Include(o => o.Members)
418:     .ToListAsync();
419: ```
420: 
421: ---
422: 
423: ## Best Practices
424: 
425: | Practice | Reason |
426: |----------|--------|
