106: ## 📚 Resources
107: 
108: *For more detailed examples, refer to the `resources/` folder within this skill.*
109: 
110: | Resource | Description |
111: |----------|-------------|
112: | [bff-configuration.md](resources/bff-configuration.md) | YARP setup, route configuration |
113: | [token-forwarding.md](resources/token-forwarding.md) | Access token extraction and forwarding |
114: | [auth-state-management.md](resources/auth-state-management.md) | Authentication state serialization |
115: | [service-layer-patterns.md](resources/service-layer-patterns.md) | Service wrappers for API clients |
116: 
117: ## ⚡ Quick Reference
118: 
119: ### 1. YARP Reverse Proxy Configuration
120: 
121: **Purpose**: Forward API requests from BFF to backend API with token attachment.
122: 
123: **Generic Template**:
124: 
125: ```csharp
126: // File: {Project}.Blazor/Program.cs
127: var {project}ApiBaseUrl = builder.Configuration["{Project}Api:BaseUrl"] ?? "https://localhost:7039/";
128: 
129: var proxyRoutes = new[]
130: {
131:     new RouteConfig
132:     {
133:         RouteId = "{project}-api",
134:         ClusterId = "{project}-api",
135:         Match = new RouteMatch
136:         {
137:             Path = "/api/v1/{**catchall}"  // Catch all API routes
138:         }
139:     }
140: };
141: 
142: var proxyClusters = new[]
143: {
144:     new ClusterConfig
145:     {
146:         ClusterId = "{project}-api",
147:         Destinations = new Dictionary<string, DestinationConfig>
148:         {
149:             ["primary"] = new() { Address = {project}ApiBaseUrl }
150:         }
151:     }
152: };
153: 
154: builder.Services.AddReverseProxy()
155:     .LoadFromMemory(proxyRoutes, proxyClusters)
156:     .AddTransforms(context =>
157:     {
158:         context.AddRequestTransform(async transformContext =>
159:         {
160:             var httpContext = transformContext.HttpContext;
161:             var token = await httpContext.GetTokenAsync("access_token"); // Get token from cookie
162:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
163:             {
164:                 transformContext.ProxyRequest.Headers.Authorization =
165:                     new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token); // Attach as Bearer token
166:             }
167:         });
168:     });
169: ```
170: 
171: **Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event**:
172: 
173: ```csharp
174: // File: Explore.Blazor/Program.cs
175: var exploreApiBaseUrl = builder.Configuration["ExploreApi:BaseUrl"] ?? "https://localhost:7039/";
176: 
177: var proxyRoutes = new[]
178: {
179:     new RouteConfig
180:     {
181:         RouteId = "explore-api",
182:         ClusterId = "explore-api",
183:         Match = new RouteMatch
184:         {
185:             Path = "/api/v1/{**catchall}"  // Catch all API routes
186:         }
187:     }
188: };
189: 
190: var proxyClusters = new[]
191: {
192:     new ClusterConfig
193:     {
194:         ClusterId = "explore-api",
195:         Destinations = new Dictionary<string, DestinationConfig>
196:         {
197:             ["primary"] = new() { Address = exploreApiBaseUrl }
198:         }
199:     }
200: };
201: 
202: builder.Services.AddReverseProxy()
203:     .LoadFromMemory(proxyRoutes, proxyClusters)
204:     .AddTransforms(context =>
205:     {
206:         context.AddRequestTransform(async transformContext =>
207:         {
208:             var httpContext = transformContext.HttpContext;
209:             var token = await httpContext.GetTokenAsync("access_token"); // Get token from cookie
210:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
211:             {
212:                 transformContext.ProxyRequest.Headers.Authorization =
213:                     new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token); // Attach as Bearer token
214:             }
215:         });
216:     });
217: ```
218: 
219: *For more details, see [bff-configuration.md](resources/bff-configuration.md).*
220: 
221: ### 2. Authentication Configuration (OIDC + Cookies)
222: 
223: **Purpose**: Configure OIDC authentication and cookie-based session management for the Blazor Server BFF.
224: 
225: **Generic Template** (works with any OIDC provider):
226: 
227: ```csharp
228: // File: {Project}.Blazor/Program.cs
229: builder.Services.AddAuthentication(options =>
230: {
231:     options.DefaultScheme = CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme;
232:     options.DefaultChallengeScheme = OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme;
233: })
234: .AddCookie(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme, options =>
235: {
236:     options.LoginPath = "/login";
237:     options.LogoutPath = "/logout";
238:     options.ExpireTimeSpan = TimeSpan.FromDays(7);
239:     options.SlidingExpiration = true;
240:     options.Cookie.HttpOnly = true;
241:     options.Cookie.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest;
242:     options.Cookie.SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax;
243: })
244: .AddOpenIdConnect(options =>
245: {
246:     options.Authority = builder.Configuration["OIDC:Authority"];
247:     options.ClientId = builder.Configuration["OIDC:ClientId"];
248:     options.ClientSecret = builder.Configuration["OIDC:ClientSecret"];
249:     options.ResponseType = "code";
250:     options.UsePkce = true;
251:     options.SaveTokens = true;  // Store tokens in cookie
252:     options.GetClaimsFromUserInfoEndpoint = true;
253: 
254:     options.Scope.Clear();
255:     options.Scope.Add("openid");
256:     options.Scope.Add("profile");
257:     options.Scope.Add("email");
258:     options.Scope.Add("offline_access");  // Request refresh token
259: });
260: ```
261: 
262: **Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event** (uses Keycloak):
263: 
264: ```csharp
265: // File: Explore.Blazor/Program.cs
266: builder.Services.AddAuthentication(options =>
267: {
268:     options.DefaultScheme = CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme;
269:     options.DefaultChallengeScheme = OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme;
270: })
271: .AddCookie(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme, options =>
272: {
273:     options.LoginPath = "/login";
274:     options.LogoutPath = "/logout";
275:     options.ExpireTimeSpan = TimeSpan.FromDays(7);
276:     options.SlidingExpiration = true;
277:     options.Cookie.HttpOnly = true;
278:     options.Cookie.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest;
279:     options.Cookie.SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax;
280: })
281: .AddOpenIdConnect(options =>
282: {
283:     options.Authority = builder.Configuration["Keycloak:Authority"];
284:     options.ClientId = builder.Configuration["Keycloak:ClientId"];
285:     options.ClientSecret = builder.Configuration["Keycloak:ClientSecret"];
286:     options.ResponseType = "code";
287:     options.UsePkce = true;
288:     options.SaveTokens = true;  // Store tokens in cookie
289:     options.GetClaimsFromUserInfoEndpoint = true;
290: 
291:     options.Scope.Clear();
292:     options.Scope.Add("openid");
293:     options.Scope.Add("profile");
294:     options.Scope.Add("email");
295:     options.Scope.Add("offline_access");  // Request refresh token
296: });
297: ```
298: 
299: *For more details, see [auth-state-management.md](resources/auth-state-management.md).*
300: 
301: ### 3. Token Forwarding for InteractiveServer Components
302: 
303: **Purpose**: In Blazor Hybrid apps, `HttpContext` is not always available in interactive components. Access tokens need to be explicitly forwarded to HTTP clients.
304: 
305: **Generic Template**:
306: 
307: ```csharp
308: // File: {Project}.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs (Scoped service)
309: public interface ICircuitAccessTokenService
310: {
311:     void SetAccessToken(string? token);
312:     string? GetAccessToken();
313: }
314: 
315: // File: {Project}.Blazor/Services/AccessTokenForwardingHandler.cs (DelegatingHandler)
316: public class AccessTokenForwardingHandler : DelegatingHandler
317: {
318:     private readonly ICircuitAccessTokenService _tokenService;
319:     public AccessTokenForwardingHandler(ICircuitAccessTokenService tokenService) => _tokenService = tokenService;
320:     protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
321:     {
322:         var token = _tokenService.GetAccessToken();
323:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
324:         {
325:             request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);
326:         }
327:         return await base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);
328:     }
329: }
330: 
331: // Registration in Program.cs
332: builder.Services.AddScoped<ICircuitAccessTokenService, CircuitAccessTokenService>();
333: builder.Services.AddTransient<AccessTokenForwardingHandler>();
334: builder.Services.AddHttpClient<I{Entity}ApiClient, {Entity}ApiClient>(client =>
335: {
336:     client.BaseAddress = new Uri({project}ApiBaseUrl);
337: })
338: .AddHttpMessageHandler<AccessTokenForwardingHandler>();  // Attach token
339: ```
340: 
341: **Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event**:
342: 
343: ```csharp
344: // File: Explore.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs (Scoped service)
345: public interface ICircuitAccessTokenService
346: {
347:     void SetAccessToken(string? token);
348:     string? GetAccessToken();
349: }
350: 
351: // File: Explore.Blazor/Services/AccessTokenForwardingHandler.cs (DelegatingHandler)
352: public class AccessTokenForwardingHandler : DelegatingHandler
353: {
354:     private readonly ICircuitAccessTokenService _tokenService;
355:     public AccessTokenForwardingHandler(ICircuitAccessTokenService tokenService) => _tokenService = tokenService;
356:     protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
357:     {
358:         var token = _tokenService.GetAccessToken();
359:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
360:         {
361:             request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);
362:         }
363:         return await base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);
364:     }
365: }
366: 
367: // Registration in Program.cs
368: builder.Services.AddScoped<ICircuitAccessTokenService, CircuitAccessTokenService>();
369: builder.Services.AddTransient<AccessTokenForwardingHandler>();
370: builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IEventApiClient, EventApiClient>(client =>
371: {
372:     client.BaseAddress = new Uri(exploreApiBaseUrl);
373: })
374: .AddHttpMessageHandler<AccessTokenForwardingHandler>();  // Attach token
375: ```
376: 
377: *For more details, see [token-forwarding.md](resources/token-forwarding.md).*
378: 
379: ### 4. Service Layer Pattern
380: 
381: **Purpose**: Wrap NSwag-generated API clients with a service layer for error handling, logging, and providing safe defaults.
382: 
383: **Generic Template**:
384: 
385: ```csharp
386: // File: {Project}.Blazor.Client/Services/{Entity}Service.cs
387: public interface I{Entity}Service { /* ... */ }
388: 
389: public class {Entity}Service : I{Entity}Service
390: {
391:     private readonly I{Entity}ApiClient _apiClient; // NSwag-generated
392:     private readonly ILogger<{Entity}Service> _logger;
393: 
394:     public {Entity}Service(I{Entity}ApiClient apiClient, ILogger<{Entity}Service> logger) { /* ... */ }
395: 
396:     public async Task<ICollection<{Entity}ListDto>> GetAll{Entities}Async()
397:     {
398:         try
399:         {
400:             return await _apiClient.{Entity}AllAsync() ?? new List<{Entity}ListDto>();
401:         }
402:         catch (ApiException ex)
403:         {
404:             _logger.LogError(ex, "API error: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
405:             return new List<{Entity}ListDto>();  // Safe default
406:         }
407:     }
408: }
409: ```
410: 
411: **Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event**:
412: 
413: ```csharp
414: // File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/EventService.cs
415: public interface IEventService { /* ... */ }
416: 
417: public class EventService : IEventService
418: {
419:     private readonly IEventApiClient _apiClient; // NSwag-generated
420:     private readonly ILogger<EventService> _logger;
421: 
422:     public EventService(IEventApiClient apiClient, ILogger<EventService> logger) { /* ... */ }
423: 
424:     public async Task<ICollection<EventListDto>> GetAllEventsAsync()
425:     {
426:         try
427:         {
428:             return await _apiClient.EventAllAsync() ?? new List<EventListDto>();
429:         }
430:         catch (ApiException ex)
431:         {
432:             _logger.LogError(ex, "API error: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
433:             return new List<EventListDto>();  // Safe default
434:         }
435:     }
436: }
437: ```
438: 
439: *For more details, see [service-layer-patterns.md](resources/service-layer-patterns.md).*
440: 
441: ## ✅ Do's
442: 
443: -   ✅ **DO** use YARP for API proxying (not custom middleware).
444: -   ✅ **DO** store tokens in server-side cookies (not `localStorage`).
445: -   ✅ **DO** forward Bearer token to API in YARP transform.
446: -   ✅ **DO** use a service layer to wrap API clients.
447: -   ✅ **DO** handle errors and return safe defaults in the service layer.
448: -   ✅ **DO** log API operations for debugging.
449: -   ✅ **DO** use `BrowserRequestCredentials.Include` for WASM requests.
450: -   ✅ **DO** redirect to login on `401 Unauthorized` responses.
451: -   ✅ **DO** serialize authentication state for WASM components.
452: 
453: ## ❌ Don'ts
454: 
455: -   ❌ **DON'T** expose tokens to the browser.
456: -   ❌ **DON'T** call API directly from WASM; always go through the BFF.
457: -   ❌ **DON'T** store sensitive data in `localStorage`.
458: -   ❌ **DON'T** bypass the service layer; use services, not API client directly.
459: -   ❌ **DON'T** forget CSRF protection (use antiforgery tokens).
460: -   ❌ **DON'T** hardcode API URLs; use configuration.
461: 
462: ---
463: 
464: **Related Documentation**:
465: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture.
466: - [`auth-patterns`](../auth-patterns/SKILL.md) - Authentication and authorization patterns.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-ui-conventions/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: blazor-ui-conventions
  3: description: Comprehensive UI conventions for Blazor applications. Covers MudBlazor usage, BEM methodology, theming, component structure, state management, and render modes.
  4: type: ui
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Blazor UI Conventions & MudBlazor Guidelines
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic Blazor UI Patterns**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: This skill provides comprehensive guidelines and best practices for developing UI components in Blazor applications. It covers MudBlazor usage, BEM methodology for CSS, theming, component structure, lifecycle, state management, and render modes to ensure consistency, maintainability, and optimal user experience.
 18: 
 19: ## When This Skill Activates
 20: 
 21: **Triggered by**:
 22: - Keywords: "blazor", "component", "razor", "mudblazor", "ui", "page", "dialog", "render", "parameter", "css", "theme", "state", "lifecycle"
 23: - File patterns: `**/*.razor`, `**/*.razor.cs`, `**/*.Client/**/*.cs`, `**/*.css`, `**/*.scss`
 24: - Content patterns: `@page`, `@inject`, `<Mud`, `Parameter`, `EventCallback`, `::deep`, `::part`, `BEM` class names.
 25: 
 26: ## Blazor Hybrid Architecture
 27: 
 28: ```mermaid
 29: graph TD
 30:     subgraph Blazor Hybrid App
 31:         BFF[{Project}.Blazor (Server-side BFF)]
 32:         WASM[{Project}.Blazor.Client (WebAssembly)]
 33:         Router[Router / InteractiveAuto]
 34:     end
 35: 
 36:     subgraph UI Layer
 37:         Components[UI Components (.razor)]
 38:         MudBlazor[MudBlazor Library]
 39:         CSS[BEM-structured CSS]
 40:     end
 41: 
 42:     Router -- Renders on --> BFF
 43:     Router -- Interactivity via --> WASM
 44:     Components -- Built with --> MudBlazor
 45:     Components -- Styled with --> CSS
 46:     WASM -- Communicates with --> BFF
 47: ```
 48: 
 49: ## Resources
 50: 
 51: | Resource | Description |
 52: |----------|-------------|
 53: | [mudblazor-usage.md](resources/mudblazor-usage.md) | Detailed usage of common MudBlazor components (Grid, Buttons, Forms, Dialogs, Tables, Snackbar, Cards). |
 54: | [component-design.md](resources/component-design.md) | Blazor component structure, lifecycle, parameters, `EventCallback`, and best practices for parent-child communication. |
 55: | [state-management.md](resources/state-management.md) | Comprehensive guide to Blazor state management techniques (component state, parameters, cascading values, scoped/singleton services). |
 56: | [render-modes.md](resources/render-modes.md) | Explanation of Blazor render modes (InteractiveAuto, Server, WebAssembly, Static SSR) and their appropriate use cases. |
 57: | [bem-methodology.md](resources/bem-methodology.md) | Guidelines for BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) CSS naming convention for maintainable stylesheets. |
 58: | [theming.md](resources/theming.md) | Customizing MudBlazor themes, dark/light mode switching, and consistent styling. |
 59: | [common-patterns.md](resources/common-patterns.md) | Real-world Blazor implementation patterns for forms, dialogs, tables, navigation, loading states, error handling, search/filter, and infinite scroll. |
 60: 
 61: ## Quick Reference
 62: 
 63: ### 1. BEM Methodology
 64: 
 65: **Rule**: All custom CSS should follow the BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) naming convention.
 66: 
 67: ```css
 68: /* Block: .{entity}-card */
 69: .{entity}-card {
 70:     border: 1px solid var(--mud-palette-lines-default);
 71:     border-radius: var(--mud-default-border-radius);
 72:     box-shadow: var(--mud-shadow-1);
 73: }
 74: 
 75: /* Element: .{entity}-card__title */
 76: .{entity}-card__title {
 77:     font-size: var(--mud-typography-h6-size);
 78:     color: var(--mud-palette-primary);
 79: }
 80: 
 81: /* Modifier: .{entity}-card--featured */
 82: .{entity}-card--featured {
 83:     border-color: var(--mud-palette-success);
 84:     box-shadow: var(--mud-shadow-2);
 85: }
 86: ```
 87: *For more details, see [bem-methodology.md](resources/bem-methodology.md).*
 88: 
 89: ### 2. MudBlazor Usage
 90: 
 91: **Rule**: Prefer MudBlazor components over custom HTML for consistent UI and functionality.
 92: 
 93: ```razor
 94: @* Grid Layout *@
 95: <MudGrid Spacing="3">
 96:     <MudItem xs="12" sm="6" md="4" lg="3">
 97:         <MudCard>
 98:             <MudCardMedia Image="@item.CoverImageUrl" Height="200" />
 99:             <MudCardContent>
100:                 <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">@item.Title</MudText>
101:             </MudCardContent>
102:         </MudCard>
103:     </MudItem>
104: </MudGrid>
105: 
106: @* Buttons *@
107: <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled" Color="Color.Primary" StartIcon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Add">
108:     Create {Entity}
109: </MudButton>
110: 
111: @* Forms *@
112: <MudTextField @bind-Value="title" Label="{Entity} Title" Required="true" />
113: <MudSelect @bind-Value="selectedId" Label="{LookupEntity}">
114:     <MudSelectItem Value="1">Option 1</MudSelectItem>
115: </MudSelect>
116: ```
117: *For more details, see [mudblazor-usage.md](resources/mudblazor-usage.md).*
118: 
119: ### 3. Theming
120: 
121: **Rule**: Global styles and theme overrides are managed in `wwwroot/css/StyleGlobal.css` and `wwwroot/css/variables.css`. Dark/Light mode switching is handled via a `CascadingValue`.
122: 
123: ```csharp
124: // App.razor logic for cascading theme
125: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor
126: 
127: @code {
128:     var theme = HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Cookies["theme"];
129:     var isDark = theme == "dark";
130: }
131: 
132: <CascadingValue Value="isDark" Name="InitialTheme">
133:     <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" />
134: </CascadingValue>
135: 
136: // MainLayout.razor consuming the theme
137: @code {
138:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")]
139:     public bool IsDarkMode { get; set; }
140: 
141:     private MudTheme _theme = new();
142:     private bool _isDarkMode;
143: 
144:     protected override void OnInitialized()
145:     {
146:         _isDarkMode = IsDarkMode;
147:     }
148: }
149: 
150: <MudThemeProvider @bind-IsDarkMode="_isDarkMode" Theme="_theme" />
151: ```
152: *For more details, see [theming.md](resources/theming.md).*
153: 
154: ### 4. Component Structure & Lifecycle
155: 
156: **Rule**: Use `ParameterState` for MudBlazor components to prevent infinite re-render loops. Use `OnInitializedAsync` for initial data fetching and `EventCallback` for child-to-parent communication.
157: 
158: #### MudBlazor ParameterState Framework (Preferred)
159: 
160: **Critical Pattern**: MudBlazor components (v7+) must use `ParameterState<T>` to avoid infinite loops when parameters change.
161: 
162: ```razor
163: @* Child Component: {Entity}Card.razor (MudBlazor) *@
164: @using MudBlazor.State
165: 
166: <MudCard>
167:     <MudCardContent>
168:         <MudText>@_entityState.Value.Title</MudText>
169:     </MudCardContent>
170:     <MudCardActions>
171:         <MudButton OnClick="DeleteClicked">Delete</MudButton>
172:     </MudCardActions>
173: </MudCard>
174: 
175: @code {
176:     // ✅ CORRECT: Use ParameterState for MudBlazor components
177:     private readonly ParameterState<{Entity}Dto> _entityState;
178: 
179:     [Parameter]
180:     public {Entity}Dto {Entity}
181:     {
182:         get => _entityState.Value;
183:         set => _entityState.SetValue(value);
184:     }
185: 
186:     [Parameter]
187:     public EventCallback<{IdType}> OnDelete { get; set; }
188: 
189:     public {Entity}Card()
190:     {
191:         // Initialize state, optionally with a change handler
192:         _entityState = RegisterParameter(nameof({Entity}), () => {Entity}, () =>
193:         {
194:             // Optional: Logic when parameter changes
195:         });
196:     }
197: 
198:     private async Task DeleteClicked()
199:     {
200:         await OnDelete.InvokeAsync({Entity}.Id);
201:     }
202: }
203: ```
204: 
205: **Why ParameterState?** Prevents infinite re-render loops in MudBlazor components by managing parameter change tracking separately from Blazor's built-in mechanism. It is the standard for MudBlazor v7 component development.
206: 
207: *For more details, see [component-design.md](resources/component-design.md).*
208: 
209: ### 5. State Management
210: 
211: **Rule**: Choose the appropriate state management pattern based on the component relationship and data scope.
212: 
213: -   **Component State**: For isolated component data.
214: -   **Parameters/EventCallback**: For direct parent-child communication.
215: -   **CascadingValue**: For sharing state deep in the component hierarchy (e.g., `AuthenticationState`, theme).
216: -   **Scoped Services**: For sharing state across multiple, unrelated components within the same user session.
217: -   **Singleton Services**: For global, read-only application data.
218: 
219: *For more details, see [state-management.md](resources/state-management.md).*
220: 
221: ### 6. Render Modes
222: 
223: **Rule**: Use `InteractiveAuto` as the default render mode for interactive components. Use `InteractiveServer` for server-only features (e.g., `HttpContext` access) and `InteractiveWebAssembly` for offline-first or highly client-side interactive components.
224: 
225: ```razor
226: @page "/{entities}"
227: @rendermode InteractiveAuto // Default for interactive pages
228: ```
229: *For more details, see [render-modes.md](resources/render-modes.md).*
230: 
231: ### 7. Common Patterns
232: 
233: **Rule**: Implement common UI patterns like forms, dialogs, tables, and loading states consistently across the application.
234: 
235: ```razor
236: @* Confirmation Dialog *@
237: @inject IDialogService DialogService
238: 
239: <MudButton OnClick="Delete{Entity}">Delete</MudButton>
240: 
241: @code {
242:     private async Task Delete{Entity}()
243:     {
244:         var dialog = await DialogService.ShowAsync<ConfirmDialog>("Confirm Delete");
245:         var result = await dialog.Result;
246:         if (!result.Canceled) { /* Perform delete */ }
247:     }
248: }
249: ```
250: *For more details, see [common-patterns.md](resources/common-patterns.md).*
251: 
252: ## Do's
253: 
254: -   **DO** use `@rendermode="InteractiveAuto"` as the default for interactive pages.
255: -   **DO** prefer MudBlazor components over custom HTML for consistency.
256: -   **DO** follow the BEM methodology for all custom CSS classes.
257: -   **DO** use `[Parameter]` for inputs and `EventCallback<T>` for child-to-parent events.
258: -   **DO** load data in `OnInitializedAsync` for initial setup.
259: -   **DO** use `IDialogService` for modals and `ISnackbar` for notifications.
260: -   **DO** implement `IDisposable` for event clean-up in services and components.
261: -   **DO** use scoped services for state management across components within a user session.
262: -   **DO** centralize theme customization in `wwwroot/css/site.css` and `wwwroot/css/variables.css`.
263: 
264: ## Don'ts
265: 
266: -   **DON'T** use raw HTML when a suitable MudBlazor component exists.
267: -   **DON'T** modify `[Parameter]` properties directly from within a child component.
268: -   **DON'T** access `HttpContext` in components rendered with `InteractiveAuto` or `InteractiveWebAssembly` (use `InteractiveServer` or BFF pattern).
269: -   **DON'T** use JavaScript interop for tasks that MudBlazor or Blazor itself can handle.
270: -   **DON'T** call `StateHasChanged()` unnecessarily (can lead to performance issues).
271: -   **DON'T** use static state in Blazor Server apps (can cause data leakage between users).
272: 
273: ---
274: 
275: **Related Documentation**:
276: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture, especially Blazor Hybrid.
277: - [`blazor-bff-patterns`](../blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md) - Details on YARP, token forwarding, and cookie-based auth.
278: - [`auth-patterns`](../auth-patterns/SKILL.md) - Authentication and authorization patterns in Blazor.
````

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/entity-configuration.md
````markdown
  1: # Entity Configuration
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Entity Configuration Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## IEntityTypeConfiguration Pattern
 10: 
 11: Separate configuration classes for each entity.
 12: 
 13: ### Basic Configuration
 14: 
 15: ```csharp
 16: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
 17: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Metadata.Builders;
 18: using {Project}.Domain;
 19: 
 20: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Configurations.Entities;
 21: 
 22: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
 23: {
 24:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
 25:     {
 26:         // Project standard: TPT + UUIDv7
 27:         builder.UseTptMappingStrategy();
 28:         builder.Property(e => e.Id).HasDefaultValueSql("uuidv7()");
 29: 
 30:         // DB-level defaults are OK here (do not add defaults in Domain entities)
 31:         builder.Property(e => e.ViewCount).HasDefaultValue(0);
 32: 
 33:         builder.Property(e => e.Title).HasMaxLength(200).IsRequired();
 34:         builder.Property(e => e.Description).HasMaxLength(5000);
 35:         builder.Property(e => e.Slug).HasMaxLength(500);
 36:         builder.Property(e => e.CurrencyCode).HasMaxLength(3);
 37:         builder.Property(e => e.ExternalUrl).HasMaxLength(500);
 38:         builder.Property(e => e.Timezone).HasMaxLength(100);
 39: 
 40:         // Relationships (use Restrict for most FK deletes)
 41:         builder.HasOne(e => e.{ParentEntity})
 42:             .WithMany()
 43:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
 44:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
 45:     }
 46: }
 47: ```
 48: 
 49: ---
 50: 
 51: ## Common Patterns
 52: 
 53: ### TPT (Table Per Type) Strategy
 54: 
 55: ```csharp
 56: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
 57: {
 58:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
 59:     {
 60:         // ✅ TPT Strategy (project standard)
 61:         builder.UseTptMappingStrategy();
 62: 
 63:         // Each derived type gets its own table
 64:         // Base {Entity} table + derived tables
 65:     }
 66: }
 67: ```
 68: 
 69: **Why TPT?**
 70: - ✅ Normalized data (no discriminator column)
 71: - ✅ No null columns for unused properties
 72: - ✅ Clean separation of types
 73: 
 74: **Alternatives**:
 75: - `UseTphMappingStrategy()` - Table Per Hierarchy (single table with discriminator)
 76: - `UseTpcMappingStrategy()` - Table Per Concrete (one table per concrete type)
 77: 
 78: ### PostgreSQL UUIDv7 Primary Keys
 79: 
 80: ```csharp
 81: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
 82: {
 83:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
 84:     {
 85:         // ✅ PostgreSQL function for UUIDv7
 86:         builder.Property(e => e.Id)
 87:                .HasDefaultValueSql("uuidv7()");
 88:     }
 89: }
 90: ```
 91: 
 92: **Why UUIDv7?**
 93: - ✅ Time-ordered (better index performance than random UUIDs)
 94: - ✅ Globally unique
 95: - ✅ No identity column contention
 96: 
 97: ### Default Values
 98: 
 99: ```csharp
100: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
101: {
102:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
103:     {
104:         // Default value in database
105:         builder.Property(e => e.ViewCount)
106:                .HasDefaultValue(0);
107: 
108:         // Use DB defaults only for stable, cross-cutting values.
109:         // Prefer setting business defaults in Application handlers.
110:     }
111: }
112: ```
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## Property Configuration
117: 
118: ### Required Properties
119: 
120: ```csharp
121: builder.Property(e => e.Title)
122:        .IsRequired()
123:        .HasMaxLength(200);
124: 
125: builder.Property(e => e.Email)
126:        .IsRequired()
127:        .HasMaxLength(255);
128: ```
129: 
130: ### Optional Properties
131: 
132: ```csharp
133: // Nullable reference type (C# 10+)
134: builder.Property(e => e.Description)
135:        .HasMaxLength(2000);  // Optional - no IsRequired()
136: 
137: // Nullable value type
138: builder.Property(e => e.EndDate)
139:        .HasColumnType("timestamp");  // DateTime? is automatically optional
140: ```
141: 
142: ### Max Length
143: 
144: ```csharp
145: builder.Property(e => e.Title).HasMaxLength(200);
146: builder.Property(e => e.ShortDescription).HasMaxLength(500);
147: builder.Property(e => e.Description).HasMaxLength(2000);
148: builder.Property(e => e.Email).HasMaxLength(255);
149: ```
150: 
151: ### Column Types (PostgreSQL)
152: 
153: ```csharp
154: // Text
155: builder.Property(e => e.Description)
156:        .HasColumnType("text");
157: 
158: // Timestamp
159: // If your entity uses DateTimeOffset/DateTime columns:
160: // builder.Property(e => e.CreatedAt)
161: //        .HasColumnType("timestamp with time zone");
162: 
163: // JSON
164: builder.Property(e => e.Metadata)
165:        .HasColumnType("jsonb");
166: 
167: // Decimal with precision
168: builder.Property(e => e.Price)
169:        .HasColumnType("decimal(18,2)");
170: 
171: // Geography (PostGIS)
172: builder.Property(e => e.Location)
173:        .HasColumnType("geography(point)");
174: ```
175: 
176: ---
177: 
178: ## Relationships
179: 
180: ### One-to-Many
181: 
182: ```csharp
183: // {ParentEntity} has many {Entities} (current model: {Entity} references {ParentEntity}, but {ParentEntity} doesn't expose a collection navigation)
184: builder.HasOne(e => e.{ParentEntity})
185:        .WithMany()
186:        .HasForeignKey(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
187:        .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Many-to-One
191: 
192: ```csharp
193: // {Entity} belongs to one Tenant
194: builder.HasOne(e => e.Tenant)
195:        .WithMany()
196:        .HasForeignKey(e => e.TenantId)
197:        .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
198: ```
199: 
200: ### Many-to-Many
201: 
202: ```csharp
203: // {Entity} <-> Category uses a mapping entity with its own Id
204: public class {Entity}CategoriesConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}Categories>
205: {
206:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}Categories> builder)
207:     {
208:         builder.HasOne(e => e.{Entity})
209:             .WithMany()
210:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.{Entity}Id)
211:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Cascade);
212: 
213:         builder.HasOne(e => e.Category)
214:             .WithMany()
215:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.CategoryId)
216:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Cascade);
217: 
218:         builder.HasOne(e => e.Tenant)
219:             .WithMany()
220:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.TenantId)
221:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
222:     }
223: }
224: ```
225: 
226: ### One-to-One
227: 
228: ```csharp
229: // User has one Profile
230: public class UserConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<User>
231: {
232:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<User> builder)
233:     {
234:         builder.HasOne(u => u.Profile)
235:                .WithOne(p => p.User)
236:                .HasForeignKey<UserProfile>(p => p.UserId);
237:     }
238: }
239: ```
240: 
241: ---
242: 
243: ## Delete Behavior
244: 
245: ```csharp
246: builder.HasOne(e => e.{ParentEntity})
247:        .WithMany()
248:        .HasForeignKey(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
249:        .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
250: ```
251: 
252: | Behavior | Description |
253: |----------|-------------|
254: | `Cascade` | Delete dependents when principal deleted |
255: | `Restrict` | Prevent delete if dependents exist |
256: | `SetNull` | Set foreign key to null when principal deleted |
257: | `NoAction` | No action (database handles it) |
258: 
259: ---
260: 
261: ## Indexes
262: 
263: ### Simple Index
264: 
265: ```csharp
266: builder.HasIndex(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id);
267: builder.HasIndex(e => e.TenantId);
268: ```
269: 
270: ### Composite Index
271: 
272: ```csharp
273: builder.HasIndex(e => new { e.TenantId, e.{ParentEntity}Id });
274: ```
275: 
276: ### Unique Index
277: 
278: ```csharp
279: builder.HasIndex(e => e.Email).IsUnique();
280: ```
281: 
282: ### Named Index
283: 
284: ```csharp
285: builder.HasIndex(e => e.Title)
286:        .HasDatabaseName("IX_{Entities}_Title");
287: ```
288: 
289: ### Filtered Index (PostgreSQL)
290: 
291: ```csharp
292: builder.HasIndex(e => e.Email)
293:        .IsUnique()
294:        .HasFilter("\"Email\" IS NOT NULL");
295: ```
296: 
297: ---
298: 
299: ## Value Conversions
300: 
301: ### Enum to String
302: 
303: ```csharp
304: builder.Property(e => e.Status)
305:        .HasConversion<string>();  // Store enum as string in database
306: ```
307: 
308: ### JSON Column
309: 
310: ```csharp
311: builder.Property(e => e.Metadata)
312:        .HasConversion(
313:            v => JsonSerializer.Serialize(v, (JsonSerializerOptions)null!),
314:            v => JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Dictionary<string, string>>(v, (JsonSerializerOptions)null!)!)
315:        .HasColumnType("jsonb");
316: ```
317: 
318: ### Custom Value Converter
319: 
320: ```csharp
321: var converter = new ValueConverter<List<string>, string>(
322:     v => string.Join(',', v),
323:     v => v.Split(',', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries).ToList());
324: 
325: builder.Property(e => e.Tags)
326:        .HasConversion(converter);
327: ```
328: 
329: ---
330: 
331: ## Owned Types
332: 
333: For value objects that don't have their own identity.
334: 
335: ```csharp
336: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
337: {
338:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
339:     {
340:         // Address is an owned type
341:         builder.OwnsOne(e => e.Address, address =>
342:         {
343:             address.Property(a => a.Street).HasMaxLength(200);
344:             address.Property(a => a.City).HasMaxLength(100);
345:             address.Property(a => a.Country).HasMaxLength(100);
346:         });
347:     }
348: }
349: ```
350: 
351: ---
352: 
353: ## Table Splitting
354: 
355: Multiple entities mapped to same table.
356: 
357: ```csharp
358: // {Entity} and {Entity}Details share same table
359: builder.ToTable("{Entities}");
360: builder.HasOne(e => e.Details)
361:        .WithOne()
362:        .HasForeignKey<{Entity}Details>(d => d.{Entity}Id);
363: 
364: // {Entity}Details configuration
365: builder.ToTable("{Entities}");  // Same table as {Entity}
366: ```
367: 
368: ---
369: 
370: ## Temporal Tables (SQL Server)
371: 
372: ```csharp
373: // Enable temporal table (SQL Server only)
374: builder.ToTable("{Entities}", b => b.IsTemporal(
375:     temporal =>
376:     {
377:         temporal.HasPeriodStart("ValidFrom");
378:         temporal.HasPeriodEnd("ValidTo");
379:         temporal.UseHistoryTable("{Entities}History");
380:     }));
381: ```
382: 
383: ---
384: 
385: ## Best Practices
386: 
387: | Practice | Reason |
388: |----------|--------|
389: | ✅ One configuration class per entity | Separation of concerns |
390: | ✅ Use `HasMaxLength` for strings | Database optimization |
391: | ✅ Specify `IsRequired` explicitly | Clear intent |
392: | ✅ Use `TPT` for inheritance (project standard) | Clean separation |
393: | ✅ Use PostgreSQL functions (`uuidv7()`) | Better performance |
394: | ✅ Configure indexes for foreign keys | Query performance |
395: | ✅ Use `DeleteBehavior.Cascade` carefully | Data integrity |
396: | ❌ Don't configure in OnModelCreating | Use IEntityTypeConfiguration |
397: | ❌ Don't use magic strings for column types | Use HasColumnType |
398: 
399: ---
400: 
401: **Related Resources**:
402: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
403: - [repository-pattern.md](repository-pattern.md) - Repository implementations
404: - [migrations.md](migrations.md) - Creating migrations
````

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/migrations.md
````markdown
  1: # Migrations
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Migration Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## What are Migrations?
 10: 
 11: Migrations are version-controlled schema changes that allow you to evolve your database schema over time.
 12: 
 13: ```
 14: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 15: │                       MIGRATION WORKFLOW                            │
 16: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 17: │                                                                     │
 18: │  1. Change Domain Model (Add/Remove/Modify entities)                │
 19: │     ↓                                                               │
 20: │  2. Create Migration (dotnet ef migrations add)                     │
 21: │     ↓                                                               │
 22: │  3. Review Generated SQL                                            │
 23: │     ↓                                                               │
 24: │  4. Apply Migration (dotnet ef database update)                     │
 25: │     ↓                                                               │
 26: │  5. Database Schema Updated                                         │
 27: │                                                                     │
 28: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 29: ```
 30: 
 31: ---
 32: 
 33: ## Creating Migrations
 34: 
 35: ### Add Migration
 36: 
 37: ```bash
 38: # Basic migration
 39: dotnet ef migrations add Add{Entity}Entity --project {Project}.Persistence
 40: ```
 41: 
 42: ### Migration Naming Conventions
 43: 
 44: | Pattern | Example | Use Case |
 45: |---------|---------|----------|
 46: | `Add{Entity}` | `AddEvent` | New entity |
 47: | `Add{Property}To{Entity}` | `AddDescriptionToEvent` | New property |
 48: | `Remove{Property}From{Entity}` | `RemoveOldFieldFromEvent` | Remove property |
 49: | `Update{Entity}{Property}` | `UpdateEventTitleMaxLength` | Modify property |
 50: | `Add{Entity}{Relationship}` | `AddEventOrganizationRelationship` | New relationship |
 51: | `Initial` | `InitialCreate` | First migration |
 52: 
 53: ---
 54: 
 55: ## Migration Structure
 56: 
 57: A migration consists of two methods:
 58: 
 59: ```csharp
 60: public partial class Add{Entity}Entity : Migration
 61: {
 62:     // Applied when migrating up (forward)
 63:     protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
 64:     {
 65:         migrationBuilder.CreateTable(
 66:             name: "{Entities}",
 67:             columns: table => new
 68:             {
 69:                 Id = table.Column<Guid>(type: "uuid", nullable: false, defaultValueSql: "uuidv7()"),
 70:                 Title = table.Column<string>(type: "character varying(200)", maxLength: 200, nullable: false),
 71:                 Description = table.Column<string>(type: "text", nullable: true),
 72:                 StartDate = table.Column<DateTime>(type: "timestamp with time zone", nullable: false),
 73:                 ViewCount = table.Column<int>(type: "integer", nullable: false, defaultValue: 0)
 74:             },
 75:             constraints: table =>
 76:             {
 77:                 table.PrimaryKey("PK_{Entities}", x => x.Id);
 78:             });
 79:     }
 80: 
 81:     // Applied when rolling back (backward)
 82:     protected override void Down(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
 83:     {
 84:         migrationBuilder.DropTable(name: "{Entities}");
 85:     }
 86: }
 87: ```
 88: 
 89: ---
 90: 
 91: ## Applying Migrations
 92: 
 93: ### Update Database
 94: 
 95: ```bash
 96: # Apply all pending migrations
 97: dotnet ef database update --project {Project}.Persistence
 98: 
 99: # Apply to specific migration
100: dotnet ef database update Add{Entity}Entity --project {Project}.Persistence
101: 
102: # Rollback to previous migration
103: dotnet ef database update PreviousMigrationName --project {Project}.Persistence
104: 
105: # Rollback all migrations
106: dotnet ef database update 0 --project {Project}.Persistence
107: ```
108: 
109: ### Generate SQL Script
110: 
111: ```bash
112: # Generate SQL for all migrations
113: dotnet ef migrations script \
114:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
115:   --output migration.sql
116: 
117: # Generate SQL for specific migration
118: dotnet ef migrations script Add{Entity}Entity \
119:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
120:   --output add-{entity}.sql
121: 
122: # Generate SQL from specific migration to another
123: dotnet ef migrations script Migration1 Migration2 \
124:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
125:   --output migration-1-to-2.sql
126: 
127: # Idempotent script (can run multiple times)
128: dotnet ef migrations script \
129:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
130:   --idempotent \
131:   --output migration.sql
132: ```
133: 
134: ---
135: 
136: ## Custom Migration Code
137: 
138: ### Add Custom SQL
139: 
140: ```csharp
141: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
142: {
143:     // Create table
144:     migrationBuilder.CreateTable(/* ... */);
145: 
146:     // ✅ Add custom SQL
147:     migrationBuilder.Sql(@"
148:         CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION uuidv7() RETURNS uuid AS $$
149:         DECLARE
150:             unix_ts_ms BIGINT;
151:             uuid_bytes BYTEA;
152:         BEGIN
153:             unix_ts_ms = (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CLOCK_TIMESTAMP()) * 1000)::BIGINT;
154:             uuid_bytes = E'\\x' ||
155:                 LPAD(TO_HEX(unix_ts_ms), 12, '0') ||
156:                 GEN_RANDOM_BYTES(10)::TEXT;
157:             RETURN uuid_bytes::UUID;
158:         END;
159:         $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
160:     ");
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: ### Create Index
165: 
166: ```csharp
167: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
168: {
169:     // ✅ Create index
170:     migrationBuilder.CreateIndex(
171:         name: "IX_{Entities}_StartDate",
172:         table: "{Entities}",
173:         column: "StartDate");
174: 
175:     // ✅ Create composite index
176:     migrationBuilder.CreateIndex(
177:         name: "IX_{Entities}_{ParentEntity}Id_StartDate",
178:         table: "{Entities}",
179:         columns: new[] { "{ParentEntity}Id", "StartDate" });
180: 
181:     // ✅ Create unique index
182:     migrationBuilder.CreateIndex(
183:         name: "IX_Users_Email",
184:         table: "Users",
185:         column: "Email",
186:         unique: true);
187: }
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Add Column
191: 
192: ```csharp
193: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
194: {
195:     // ✅ Add nullable column (safe)
196:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<string>(
197:         name: "Subtitle",
198:         table: "{Entities}",
199:         type: "character varying(200)",
200:         maxLength: 200,
201:         nullable: true);
202: 
203:     // ⚠️ Add non-nullable column (requires default)
204:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<int>(
205:         name: "Priority",
206:         table: "{Entities}",
207:         type: "integer",
208:         nullable: false,
209:         defaultValue: 0);
210: }
211: ```
212: 
213: ### Modify Column
214: 
215: ```csharp
216: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
217: {
218:     // ✅ Change column type
219:     migrationBuilder.AlterColumn<string>(
220:         name: "Title",
221:         table: "{Entities}",
222:         type: "character varying(500)",  // Changed from 200
223:         maxLength: 500,
224:         nullable: false,
225:         oldClrType: typeof(string),
226:         oldType: "character varying(200)",
227:         oldMaxLength: 200);
228: }
229: ```
230: 
231: ### Rename Column/Table
232: 
233: ```csharp
234: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
235: {
236:     // ✅ Rename column
237:     migrationBuilder.RenameColumn(
238:         name: "OldName",
239:         table: "{Entities}",
240:         newName: "NewName");
241: 
242:     // ✅ Rename table
243:     migrationBuilder.RenameTable(
244:         name: "OldTableName",
245:         newName: "NewTableName");
246: }
247: ```
248: 
249: ---
250: 
251: ## Data Migrations
252: 
253: ### Seed Data
254: 
255: ```csharp
256: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
257: {
258:     // ✅ Insert seed data
259:     migrationBuilder.InsertData(
260:         table: "{LookupEntity}s",
261:         columns: new[] { "Id", "FullName", "Description" },
262:         values: new object[,]
263:         {
264:             { 1, "Type A", "Description for Type A" },
265:             { 2, "Type B", "Description for Type B" },
266:             { 3, "Type C", "Description for Type C" }
267:         });
268: }
269: 
270: protected override void Down(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
271: {
272:     // ✅ Remove seed data
273:     migrationBuilder.DeleteData(
274:         table: "{LookupEntity}s",
275:         keyColumn: "Id",
276:         keyValues: new object[] { 1, 2, 3 });
277: }
278: ```
279: 
280: ### Data Transformation
281: 
282: ```csharp
283: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
284: {
285:     // ✅ Transform existing data
286:     migrationBuilder.Sql(@"
287:         UPDATE ""{Entities}""
288:         SET ""Title"" = UPPER(""Title"")
289:         WHERE ""Title"" IS NOT NULL;
290:     ");
291: }
292: ```
293: 
294: ---
295: 
296: ## PostgreSQL-Specific Migrations
297: 
298: ### PostGIS Extension
299: 
300: ```csharp
301: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
302: {
303:     // ✅ Enable PostGIS extension
304:     migrationBuilder.Sql("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;");
305: 
306:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<NetTopologySuite.Geometries.Point>(
307:         name: "Location",
308:         table: "{Entities}",
309:         type: "geography(point)",
310:         nullable: true);
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: ### JSONB Column
315: 
316: ```csharp
317: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
318: {
319:     // ✅ Add JSONB column
320:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<string>(
321:         name: "Metadata",
322:         table: "{Entities}",
323:         type: "jsonb",
324:         nullable: true);
325: 
326:     // ✅ Create GIN index for JSONB
327:     migrationBuilder.Sql(@"
328:         CREATE INDEX IX_{Entities}_Metadata
329:         ON ""{Entities}"" USING GIN (""Metadata"");
330:     ");
331: }
332: ```
333: 
334: ### Array Column
335: 
336: ```csharp
337: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
338: {
339:     // ✅ Add array column
340:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<string[]>(
341:         name: "Tags",
342:         table: "{Entities}",
343:         type: "text[]",
344:         nullable: true);
345: }
346: ```
347: 
348: ---
349: 
350: ## Migration Management
351: 
352: ### List Migrations
353: 
354: ```bash
355: # List all migrations
356: dotnet ef migrations list --project {Project}.Persistence
357: ```
358: 
359: ### Remove Last Migration
360: 
361: ```bash
362: # ⚠️ ONLY if not applied to database
363: dotnet ef migrations remove --project {Project}.Persistence
364: 
365: # ❌ DON'T remove if already applied - create a new migration instead
366: ```
367: 
368: ### Check Pending Migrations
369: 
370: ```csharp
371: // In code
372: var pendingMigrations = await _dbContext.Database.GetPendingMigrationsAsync();
373: if (pendingMigrations.Any())
374: {
375:     // Migrations need to be applied
376:     Console.WriteLine($"Pending migrations: {string.Join(", ", pendingMigrations)}");
377: }
378: ```
379: 
380: ### Apply Migrations Programmatically
381: 
382: ```csharp
383: // Program.cs - Apply migrations on startup
384: using var scope = app.Services.CreateScope();
385: var dbContext = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<{DbContext}>();
386: 
387: // ✅ Apply pending migrations
388: await dbContext.Database.MigrateAsync();
389: ```
390: 
391: ---
392: 
393: ## Best Practices
394: 
395: | Practice | Reason |
396: |----------|--------|
397: | ✅ Review generated SQL before applying | Catch issues early |
398: | ✅ Use descriptive migration names | Easy to understand history |
399: | ✅ Add indexes for foreign keys | Query performance |
400: | ✅ Make nullable columns when adding to existing tables | Avoid data loss |
401: | ✅ Use transactions for data migrations | Data integrity |
402: | ✅ Test migrations on copy of production data | Validate before production |
403: | ✅ Keep migrations small and focused | Easier to review and rollback |
404: | ✅ Generate idempotent SQL scripts for production | Safe deployment |
405: | ❌ Don't remove migrations after applied | Breaks history |
406: | ❌ Don't modify migrations after applied | Use new migration |
407: | ❌ Don't include sensitive data in migrations | Security risk |
408: 
409: ---
410: 
411: ## Troubleshooting
412: 
413: ### Migration Already Applied
414: 
415: ```bash
416: # Error: "The migration '20240101120000_MigrationName' has already been applied to the database."
417: 
418: # ✅ Solution: Create a new migration for changes
419: dotnet ef migrations add UpdateMigration --project {Project}.Persistence
420: ```
421: 
422: ### Conflicting Migrations
423: 
424: ```bash
425: # Error: "Your migrations are out of sync"
426: 
427: # ✅ Solution 1: Pull latest and rebase
428: git pull origin main
429: dotnet ef migrations remove  # If not yet applied
430: 
431: # ✅ Solution 2: Create new migration
432: dotnet ef migrations add ResolveMergeConflict --project {Project}.Persistence
433: ```
434: 
435: ### Connection String Not Found
436: 
437: ```bash
438: # Error: "No connection string named 'DefaultConnection' was found"
439: 
440: # ✅ Solution: Specify connection string
441: dotnet ef database update \
442:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
443:   --connection "Host=localhost;Database={project}_db;Username=postgres;Password=password"
444: ```
445: 
446: ---
447: 
448: ## Production Deployment
449: 
450: ### Generate SQL Script for DBA
451: 
452: ```bash
453: # ✅ Generate idempotent SQL script
454: dotnet ef migrations script \
455:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
456:   --idempotent \
457:   --output migrations/release-1.0.0.sql
458: ```
459: 
460: ### Manual vs Automatic
461: 
462: **Manual (Recommended for Production)**:
463: ```bash
464: # 1. Generate SQL script
465: dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent --output release.sql
466: 
467: # 2. Review script with DBA
468: # 3. DBA applies script to production database
469: ```
470: 
471: **Automatic (Development Only)**:
472: ```csharp
473: // Program.cs
474: if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
475: {
476:     using var scope = app.Services.CreateScope();
477:     var dbContext = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<{DbContext}>();
478:     await dbContext.Database.MigrateAsync();  // ✅ Auto-apply in dev only
479: }
480: ```
481: 
482: ---
483: 
484: **Related Resources**:
485: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
486: - [entity-configuration.md](entity-configuration.md) - Entity configuration
487: - [repository-pattern.md](repository-pattern.md) - Repository implementations
````

## File: docs/FEDERATION.md
````markdown
  1: # Federation
  2: 
  3: ## Status
  4: 
  5: Federation (ATProto / ActivityPub) is a **roadmap feature** - currently in **Phase 1: Data Model Only**.
  6: 
  7: ### ✅ Implemented (Phase 1: Foundation)
  8: - **Domain Entities**: Federation data models exist in `Explore.Domain`:
  9:   - `Actor` - Federated identity representation
 10:   - `AtprotoRecord` - ATProto record storage
 11:   - `PdsSyncOutbox` - Sync queue for outbound records
 12:   - `IndexedDid` - DID resolution cache
 13:   - `ActorKeyStore` - Cryptographic key storage
 14:   - Supporting entities: `ActorType`, `DidCustodyType` enums
 15: 
 16: ### ⏳ Not Yet Implemented (Roadmap)
 17: - **HTTP Endpoints**: No federation endpoints exposed in `Explore.API`:
 18:   - ❌ WebFinger (`/.well-known/webfinger`)
 19:   - ❌ Actor endpoints (`/actors/{handle}`)
 20:   - ❌ Inbox/Outbox (ActivityPub)
 21:   - ❌ ATProto PDS server
 22:   - ❌ ATProto AppView indexing
 23: - **Protocol Implementation**: No active federation protocol logic
 24: - **Bridge/Gateway**: ActivityPub ↔ ATProto translation not implemented
 25: - **DID Resolution**: No PLC/DNS-based DID resolution
 26: - **HTTP Signatures**: Cryptographic message verification not implemented
 27: - **Collections**: Followers/Following/Liked collections not exposed
 28: 
 29: **Timeline**: Federation implementation planned for future release. Foundation (entities) is complete.
 30: 
 31: ## Protocol Overview (Planned)
 32: 
 33: > **Note**: This section describes the **intended** federation model for ISLAMU Event.
 34: > **Current Status**: Protocol implementation not yet started. Only domain entities exist.
 35: 
 36: - **Server-to-Server (S2S)** (planned): Instances exchange activities via inbox/outbox
 37: - **HTTP Signatures** (planned): Cryptographic verification of federated messages
 38: - **WebFinger** (planned): Actor discovery via `/.well-known/webfinger`
 39: - **Collections** (planned): Followers, Following, Liked as ordered collections
 40:

105: │                                                    │  • Session N...     │   │

108: │   March 15-17, Amsterdam                          │  • Participants     │   │

114: 
115: ## CID
116: ```
117: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
118: │                          How CID Works                                       │
119: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
120: │                                                                             │
121: │  1. User creates event record                                               │
122: │     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐                                     │
123: │     │ {                               │                                     │
124: │     │   "$type": "ngo.islamu.event...",│                                    │
125: │     │   "title": "Community Iftar",   │                                     │
126: │     │   "startsAt": "2025-03-15...",  │                                     │
127: │     │   ...                           │                                     │
128: │     │ }                               │                                     │
129: │     └─────────────────────────────────┘                                     │
130: │                    │                                                        │
131: │                    ▼                                                        │
132: │  2. PDS serializes to DAG-CBOR (deterministic binary format)               │
133: │                    │                                                        │
134: │                    ▼                                                        │
135: │  3. PDS computes SHA-256 hash → CID                                        │
136: │     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
137: │     │ bafyreigxyz123... (base32 encoded multihash)                │        │
138: │     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
139: │                    │                                                        │
140: │  4. CID is included in the repo commit (signed by user's key)              │
141: │                                                                             │
142: │  WHY THIS MATTERS:                                                          │
143: │  ─────────────────                                                          │
144: │  • Anyone can verify the record hasn't been tampered with                  │
145: │  • If content changes → CID changes → old references become invalid        │
146: │  • Enables "strong references" (URI + CID = exact version)                 │
147: │                                                                             │
148: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
149: ```
150:
