## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/repository-pattern.md
````markdown
  1: # Repository Pattern
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Repository Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## Why Repository Pattern?
 10: 
 11: ```
 12: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 13: │                    BENEFITS OF REPOSITORY PATTERN                   │
 14: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 15: │                                                                     │
 16: │  ✅ Abstraction: Application layer doesn't depend on EF Core        │
 17: │  ✅ Testability: Easy to mock repositories for unit tests          │
 18: │  ✅ Clean Architecture: Maintains dependency inversion              │
 19: │  ✅ Centralized Data Access: Common queries in one place            │
 20: │  ✅ Consistent API: Uniform data access across entities             │
 21: │                                                                     │
 22: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 23: ```
 24: 
 25: ---
 26: 
 27: ## Generic Repository
 28: 
 29: Base repository with common CRUD operations.
 30: 
 31: ### Interface (Application Layer)
 32: 
 33: ```csharp
 34: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/IGenericRepository.cs
 35: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 36: 
 37: public interface IGenericRepository<T, TKey> where T : class
 38: {
 39:     Task<T> Create(T entity);
 40:     Task<T?> GetById(TKey id);
 41:     Task<IReadOnlyList<T>> GetAll();
 42:     Task Update(T entity);
 43:     Task Delete(T entity);
 44:     Task<bool> Exists(TKey id);
 45: }
 46: ```
 47: 
 48: ### Implementation (Persistence Layer)
 49: 
 50: ```csharp
 51: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/GenericRepository.cs
 52: using System;
 53: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 54: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
 55: using Npgsql;
 56: 
 57: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
 58: 
 59: public class GenericRepository<T, TKey> : IGenericRepository<T, TKey> where T : class
 60: {
 61:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
 62: 
 63:     public GenericRepository({DbContext} dbContext)
 64:     {
 65:         _dbContext = dbContext;
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     public async Task<T> Create(T entity)
 69:     {
 70:         try
 71:         {
 72:             await _dbContext.AddAsync(entity);
 73:             await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 74:             return entity;
 75:         }
 76:         catch (DbUpdateException ex) when (ex.InnerException is PostgresException pgEx && pgEx.SqlState == "23505")
 77:         {
 78:             // Duplicate key violation - detach the entity and rethrow with more context
 79:             _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Detached;
 80:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
 81:                 $"A record with the same unique key already exists. Constraint: {pgEx.ConstraintName}. Detail: {pgEx.Detail}",
 82:                 ex);
 83:         }
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     public async Task<T?> GetById(TKey id)
 87:     {
 88:         return await _dbContext.Set<T>().FindAsync(id);
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<T>> GetAll()
 92:     {
 93:         return await _dbContext.Set<T>().ToListAsync();
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     public async Task Update(T entity)
 97:     {
 98:         _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Modified;
 99:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
100:     }
101: 
102:     public async Task Delete(T entity)
103:     {
104:         _dbContext.Set<T>().Remove(entity);
105:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
106:     }
107: 
108:     public async Task<bool> Exists(TKey id)
109:     {
110:         var entity = await GetById(id);
111:         return entity != null;
112:     }
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## Entity-Specific Repository
119: 
120: Inherit from GenericRepository and add custom methods.
121: 
122: ### Interface (Application Layer)
123: 
124: ```csharp
125: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs
126: using {Project}.Domain;
127: 
128: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
129: 
130: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
131: {
132:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();
133:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
134:     Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId);
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: ### Implementation (Persistence Layer)
139: 
140: ```csharp
141: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
142: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
143: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
144: using {Project}.Domain;
145: 
146: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
147: 
148: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
149: {
150:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
151: 
152:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext)
153:     {
154:         _dbContext = dbContext;
155:     }
156: 
157:     // ✅ REPOSITORIES RETURN ENTITIES, NOT DTOs
158:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
159:     {
160:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
161:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
162:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
163:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
164:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
165:             .Include(e => e.Status)
166:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
167:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
168:             .ToListAsync();
169:     }
170: 
171:     public async Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id)
172:     {
173:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
174:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
175:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
176:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
177:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
178:             .Include(e => e.Status)
179:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
180:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
181:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == id);
182:     }
183: 
184:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId)
185:     {
186:         {IdType} userIdParsed;
187:         var isValid = {IdType}.TryParse(userId, out userIdParsed);
188: 
189:         var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
190:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
191:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
192:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
193:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
194:             .Include(e => e.Status)
195:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
196:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
197:             .AsQueryable();
198: 
199:         if (isValid)
200:         {
201:             query = query.Where(e =>
202:                 _dbContext.Users.Any(u => u.Id == userIdParsed && u.{ParentEntity}Id == e.{ParentEntity}Id));
203:         }
204: 
205:         return await query.ToListAsync();
206:     }
207: 
208:     // NOTE: In the Application layer handler, entities are mapped to DTOs:
209:     //
210:     // public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
211:     // {
212:     //     // Repository returns ENTITIES
213:     //     var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();
214:     //
215:     //     // AutoMapper maps ENTITIES to DTOs
216:     //     return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});
217:     // }
218: }
219: ```
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## Repository Registration (DI)
224: 
225: ```csharp
226: // File: {Project}.Persistence/PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs
227: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
228: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
229: using {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
230: 
231: namespace {Project}.Persistence;
232: 
233: public static class PersistenceServicesRegistration
234: {
235:     public static IServiceCollection AddPersistenceServices(
236:         this IServiceCollection services)
237:     {
238:         // Register generic repository
239:         services.AddScoped(typeof(IGenericRepository<,>), typeof(GenericRepository<,>));
240: 
241:         // Register specific repositories
242:         services.AddScoped<I{Entity}Repository, {Entity}Repository>();
243:         services.AddScoped<I{ParentEntity}Repository, {ParentEntity}Repository>();
244:         services.AddScoped<IUserRepository, UserRepository>();
245:         services.AddScoped<I{LinkEntity}Repository, {LinkEntity}Repository>();
246: 
247:         return services;
248:     }
249: }
250: ```
251: 
252: **Usage in Program.cs**:
253: ```csharp
254: builder.Services.AddPersistenceServices();
255: ```
256: 
257: ---
258: 
259: ## Repository Method Patterns
260: 
261: ### Return Entities (Standard Pattern)
262: 
263: **CRITICAL**: Repositories return ENTITIES, not DTOs. DTO mapping happens in Application layer handlers via AutoMapper.
264: 
265: ```csharp
266: // ✅ CORRECT: Repository returns entities
267: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
268: {
269:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
270:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
271:         .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
272:         .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
273:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
274:         .ToListAsync();
275: }
276: 
277: // ✅ CORRECT: Handler maps entities to DTOs
278: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
279: {
280:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
281:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
282: 
283:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
284:     {
285:         // Repository returns ENTITIES
286:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();
287: 
288:         // AutoMapper maps ENTITIES to DTOs
289:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});
290:     }
291: }
292: ```
293: 
294: **Benefits**:
295: - ✅ Clean separation of concerns
296: - ✅ Repositories focus on data access only
297: - ✅ Handlers handle DTO mapping with AutoMapper
298: - ✅ Reusable repositories for different DTO shapes
299: 
300: ### AsNoTracking for Read-Only Queries
301: 
302: ```csharp
303: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}ReadOnly()
304: {
305:     // ✅ No change tracking (faster for read-only)
306:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
307:         .AsNoTracking()
308:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
309:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
310:         .ToListAsync();
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: ---
315: 
316: ## Advanced Repository Patterns
317: 
318: ### Specification Pattern
319: 
320: ```csharp
321: // File: Application/Specifications/ISpecification.cs
322: public interface ISpecification<T>
323: {
324:     Expression<Func<T, bool>> Criteria { get; }
325:     List<Expression<Func<T, object>>> Includes { get; }
326: }
327: 
328: // File: Application/Specifications/{Entity}Specification.cs
329: public class {Entities}By{ParentEntity}Spec : ISpecification<{Entity}>
330: {
331:     public {Entities}By{ParentEntity}Spec({IdType} {parentEntity}Id)
332:     {
333:         Criteria = e => e.{ParentEntity}Id == {parentEntity}Id;
334:         Includes = new List<Expression<Func<{Entity}, object>>>
335:         {
336:             e => e.{ParentEntity},
337:             e => e.{LookupEntity}
338:         };
339:     }
340: 
341:     public Expression<Func<{Entity}, bool>> Criteria { get; }
342:     public List<Expression<Func<{Entity}, object>>> Includes { get; }
343: }
344: 
345: // Repository method
346: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Find(ISpecification<{Entity}> spec)
347: {
348:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}.Where(spec.Criteria);
349: 
350:     query = spec.Includes
351:         .Aggregate(query, (current, include) => current.Include(include));
352: 
353:     return await query.ToListAsync();
354: }
355: ```
356: 
357: ### Pagination
358: 
359: ```csharp
360: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}Paginated(
361:     int page,
362:     int pageSize,
363:     string? searchTerm)
364: {
365:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
366:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
367:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
368:         .AsQueryable();
369: 
370:     if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(searchTerm))
371:     {
372:         query = query.Where(e =>
373:             e.Title.Contains(searchTerm) ||
374:             e.Description.Contains(searchTerm));
375:     }
376: 
377:     var totalCount = await query.CountAsync();
378: 
379:     var items = await query
380:         .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
381:         .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
382:         .Take(pageSize)
383:         .ToListAsync();
384: 
385:     return items;
386: }
387: ```
388: 
389: ---
390: 
391: ## Best Practices
392: 
393: | Practice | Reason |
394: |----------|--------|
395: | ✅ Interface in Application, implementation in Persistence | Clean Architecture |
396: | ✅ Inherit from GenericRepository | Code reuse |
397: | ✅ Return entities, not DTOs | Separation of concerns |
398: | ✅ Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only | No unnecessary tracking |
399: | ✅ Include related entities with `Include` | Avoid N+1 queries |
400: | ✅ Register repositories in DI | Dependency injection |
401: | ✅ Use async methods (`Async` suffix) | Non-blocking I/O |
402: | ❌ Don't return IQueryable from repository | Encapsulation |
403: | ❌ Don't inject DbContext in Application layer | Breaks abstraction |
404: | ❌ Don't track entities for read-only queries | Performance overhead |
405: 
406: ---
407: 
408: **Related Resources**:
409: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
410: - [querying-patterns.md](querying-patterns.md) - Query optimization
411: - [entity-configuration.md](entity-configuration.md) - Entity configuration
````

## File: docs/CONTRIBUTING.md
````markdown
  1: # Contribution Workflow
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Contribution Guidelines**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Placeholder Substitutions
  8: 
  9: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 10: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 11: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 12: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `{Project}.API` |
 13: | `{Project}.AppHost` | Aspire AppHost | `{Project}.AppHost` |
 14: | `{Project}ApiClient` | Generated API client | `{Project}ApiClient` |
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Branch Strategy
 19: 
 20: ```
 21: main                    # Default branch
 22: ├── feature/xxx         # New features
 23: ├── bugfix/xxx          # Bug fixes
 24: └── refactor/xxx        # Code improvements
 25: ```
 26: 
 27: ## Commit Convention
 28: 
 29: ```
 30: type(scope): subject
 31: 
 32: body (optional)
 33: 
 34: footer (optional)
 35: ```
 36: 
 37: **Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`
 38: 
 39: **Examples**:
 40: ```
 41: feat(events): add prayer-relative scheduling
 42: fix(federation): correct HTTP signature validation
 43: docs(api): update endpoint documentation
 44: ```
 45: 
 46: ## Pull Request Process
 47: 
 48: 1. Create a branch from `main`
 49: 2. Implement changes with tests
 50: 3. Ensure all tests pass: `dotnet test`
 51: 4. Ensure code formatting: `dotnet format`
 52: 5. Create PR with description and linked issue
 53: 6. Request review from maintainers
 54: 7. Address feedback
 55: 8. Squash and merge when approved
 56: 
 57: ## Issue Templates
 58: 
 59: - **Bug Report**: Describe bug, steps to reproduce, expected behavior
 60: - **Feature Request**: Describe need, proposed solution, alternatives
 61: - **Task**: Technical work without user-facing change
 62: 
 63: ---
 64: 
 65: ## DTO Change Workflow (API → Blazor Client)
 66: 
 67: When making changes to DTOs in the API project, follow this specific workflow to ensure the Blazor client is properly updated.
 68: 
 69: ### Why This Workflow Matters
 70: 
 71: The project uses **.NET Aspire** for orchestration, which:
 72: 1. Fetches secrets from Infisical and injects them as environment variables
 73: 2. Starts all projects in the correct order
 74: 3. **Triggers OpenAPI schema regeneration** in the API project on startup
 75: 4. **NSwag watches for schema changes** and automatically regenerates the Blazor API client
 76: 
 77: **Key Point**: You must run Aspire to regenerate the client. Building alone won't update the generated client code.
 78: 
 79: ### The Vicious Cycle Problem
 80: 
 81: Understanding **why** this workflow exists prevents frustrating debugging sessions.
 82: 
 83: #### The Problem: Build Errors Block Client Regeneration
 84: 
 85: When you change DTOs in the API and then try to build the **full solution**, you enter a vicious cycle:
 86: 
 87: ```
 88: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 89: │                    ❌ THE VICIOUS CYCLE                              │
 90: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 91: │                                                                     │
 92: │  1. You change a DTO in the API (add new property)                  │
 93: │     ↓                                                               │
 94: │  2. You try to build the FULL SOLUTION                              │
 95: │     ↓                                                               │
 96: │  3. ❌ BUILD FAILS - Blazor references the OLD generated client     │
 97: │     │   (The generated client doesn't have the new property yet)    │
 98: │     ↓                                                               │
 99: │  4. ❌ ASP.NET API won't run (solution didn't build)                │
100: │     ↓                                                               │
101: │  5. ❌ swagger.json can't regenerate (API isn't running)            │
102: │     ↓                                                               │
103: │  6. ❌ NSwag can't update the client (no new schema)                │
104: │     ↓                                                               │
105: │  7. ❌ Generated client stays outdated                              │
106: │     ↓                                                               │
107: │  8. ❌ Build errors persist → BACK TO STEP 3                        │
108: │                                                                     │
109: │  💀 YOU ARE STUCK IN AN INFINITE LOOP                               │
110: │                                                                     │
111: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
112: ```
113: 
114: #### The Solution: Build API Separately First
115: 
116: By building **only the API project** first, you break the cycle:
117: 
118: ```
119: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
120: │                    ✅ THE CORRECT WORKFLOW                           │
121: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
122: │                                                                     │
123: │  1. You change a DTO in the API (add new property)                  │
124: │     ↓                                                               │
125: │  2. Build ONLY the API project: `dotnet build {Project}.API`          │
126: │     ↓                                                               │
127: │  3. ✅ API builds successfully (no Blazor dependency issues)        │
128: │     ↓                                                               │
129: │  4. Run Aspire: `dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost`              │
130: │     ↓                                                               │
131: │  5. ✅ API starts and generates new swagger.json                    │
132: │     ↓                                                               │
133: │  6. ✅ NSwag detects changes, regenerates client                    │
134: │     ↓                                                               │
135: │  7. ✅ Generated client now has the new property                    │
136: │     ↓                                                               │
137: │  8. NOW update Blazor services/components                           │
138: │     ↓                                                               │
139: │  9. ✅ Build full solution: `dotnet build {Project}.sln`              │
140: │                                                                     │
141: │  🎉 SUCCESS - No build errors!                                      │
142: │                                                                     │
143: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
144: ```
145: 
146: #### Common Trap: Updating Blazor Services Too Early
147: 
148: A particularly frustrating mistake is updating **Blazor services that interact with the generated API client** before the client is regenerated:
149: 
150: ```
151: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
152: │              ❌ THE SERVICE UPDATE TRAP                              │
153: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
154: │                                                                     │
155: │  Scenario: You add `Description` property to `EventDto`             │
156: │                                                                     │
157: │  1. You update EventDto in API (✅ correct)                         │
158: │     ↓                                                               │
159: │  2. You update EventService in Blazor to use `.Description`         │
160: │     ↓                                                               │
161: │  3. ❌ ERROR: 'EventDto' does not contain 'Description'             │
162: │     │                                                               │
163: │     │   WHY? The generated client ({Project}ApiClient.cs) still       │
164: │     │   has the OLD EventDto without Description!                   │
165: │     │                                                               │
166: │     │   Your service references: Generated.EventDto (OLD)           │
167: │     │   You expect:              Generated.EventDto.Description     │
168: │     │   Reality:                 Property doesn't exist yet         │
169: │     ↓                                                               │
170: │  4. Build fails on BOTH sides:                                      │
171: │     • API side: Works fine (your DTO has the property)              │
172: │     • Blazor side: Fails (generated client is outdated)             │
173: │                                                                     │
174: │  💡 The generated client is OUT OF SYNC with the API!               │
175: │                                                                     │
176: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
177: ```
178: 
179: **Rule of Thumb**:
180: - **API-only changes** → Build API only, run Aspire, then update Blazor
181: - **UI-only changes** (no DTO changes) → Can work directly in Blazor
182: - **Both API + Blazor changes** → Follow the full checklist, API first
183: 
184: ### Standard Workflow
185: 
186: ```
187: API Changes → Build API → Run Aspire → Client Regenerates → Update Blazor UI
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Process Checklist for DTO Changes
191: 
192: Follow this checklist whenever you add/modify DTO properties:
193: 
194: ```markdown
195: ## DTO Change Checklist
196: 
197: ### 1. Application Layer Changes
198: - [ ] Add/update properties in `{Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/` files
199: - [ ] Update `{Entity}Dto.cs` (full details)
200: - [ ] Update `{Entity}ListDto.cs` (list view) if applicable
201: - [ ] Update `Create{Entity}Dto.cs` / `Update{Entity}Dto.cs` if applicable
202: 
203: ### 2. Mapping & Data Access
204: - [ ] Update `MappingProfile.cs` if new navigation properties
205: - [ ] Update Repository `.Include()` statements if loading related data
206: - [ ] Update Handler if new processing logic needed
207: 
208: ### 3. Build & Regenerate
209: - [ ] Build API project only: `dotnet build {Project}.API`
210: - [ ] Start Aspire: `dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost`
211: - [ ] Wait for swagger.json to regenerate (automatic on API startup)
212: - [ ] NSwag regenerates client automatically (watches schema file)
213: 
214: ### 4. Blazor UI Updates
215: - [ ] NOW update Blazor components to use new properties
216: - [ ] Build full solution: `dotnet build {Project}.sln`
217: - [ ] Test the changes in browser
218: ```
219: 
220: ### Quick Fix: If You Forgot the Workflow
221: 
222: If you already updated Blazor UI before running Aspire and the generated client is missing properties:
223: 
224: **Option 1: Proper Fix (Recommended)**
225: ```powershell
226: # Stop any running instances
227: # Run Aspire to regenerate everything
228: dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost
229: ```
230: 
231: **Option 2: Manual Fix (Quick Workaround)**
232: Manually add the missing properties to the generated client file as a temporary fix, then run Aspire later to properly regenerate.
233: 
234: ### Architecture Diagram
235: 
236: ```
237: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
238: │                         .NET Aspire Orchestration                    │
239: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
240: │                                                                     │
241: │  1. Aspire Starts                                                   │
242: │     └── Fetches secrets from Infisical                              │
243: │     └── Injects environment variables to all projects               │
244: │                                                                     │
245: │  2. API Project Starts                                              │
246: │     └── Generates swagger.json (OpenAPI schema)                     │
247: │     └── Schema reflects current DTO structure                       │
248: │                                                                     │
249: │  3. Blazor Project Watches                                          │
250: │     └── NSwag detects swagger.json changes                          │
251: │     └── Regenerates API client ({Project}ApiClient.cs)                │
252: │                                                                     │
253: │  4. Blazor Components                                               │
254: │     └── Use the regenerated client with new properties              │
255: │                                                                     │
256: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
257: ```
258: 
259: ### Common Mistakes
260: 
261: | Mistake | Why It Fails | Fix |
262: |---------|--------------|-----|
263: | Build solution without running Aspire | swagger.json not regenerated | Run Aspire first |
264: | Update Blazor before API | Generated client missing new properties | Follow the checklist order |
265: | Manually edit generated files | Changes overwritten on next regeneration | Add to source DTOs, regenerate |
266: | Skip the MappingProfile update | AutoMapper doesn't map new properties | Always update profile |
267: 
268: ### Related Documentation
269: 
270: - [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture
271: - [API.md](API.md) - API endpoint patterns
272: - [BLAZOR.md](BLAZOR.md) - Blazor client architecture
273: - [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md) - DTO patterns and conventions
````

## File: docs/SECURITY.md
````markdown
  1: # Security Architecture
  2: 
  3: This document provides a high-level overview of the security architecture for the ISLAMU Event platform.
  4: 
  5: For detailed implementation patterns, code examples, and specific conventions, refer to the **`auth-patterns` skill**.
  6: 
  7: ## 1. Authentication Strategy: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
  8: 
  9: The project employs a **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** security model to provide a high level of security by ensuring that no tokens are ever exposed to the end-user's browser.
 10: 
 11: **Protocol**: OpenID Connect (OIDC) / OAuth 2.0  
 12: **Provider**: Keycloak
 13: 
 14: ### Conceptual Flow
 15: 
 16: The authentication flow is designed to separate the concerns of browser session management from backend API authorization.
 17: 
 18: ```mermaid
 19: sequenceDiagram
 20:     participant Browser (Blazor WASM)
 21:     participant BFF (Blazor Server)
 22:     participant Keycloak
 23:     participant API (Backend)
 24: 
 25:     Browser->>+BFF: User clicks "Login"
 26:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Initiates OIDC Authorization Code Flow
 27:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Redirects with Authorization Code
 28:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Exchanges Code for Tokens (Access + Refresh)
 29:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Returns JWTs
 30:     BFF-->>-Browser: Stores tokens in a secure, HttpOnly cookie & redirects
 31: 
 32:     Browser->>+BFF: Makes API call
 33:     BFF->>+API: YARP proxy attaches JWT Bearer token
 34:     API->>API: Validates JWT
 35:     API-->>-BFF: Returns data
 36:     BFF-->>-Browser: Returns data
 37: ```
 38: 
 39: ### Key Architectural Principles
 40: 
 41: *   **`Explore.Blazor` (The BFF)** is the only component that communicates directly with Keycloak. It manages the user's session using a secure, server-side, `HttpOnly` cookie.
 42: *   **`Explore.Blazor.Client` (The Frontend)** is completely unaware of OIDC or JWTs. It operates like a traditional web application, automatically sending the session cookie with every request to its backend (the BFF).
 43: *   **`Explore.API` (The Backend Resource)** is a stateless service. It only accepts JWT Bearer tokens for authorization and has no knowledge of the user's session cookie. This allows the API to be used by other clients (e.g., mobile apps, other services) in the future.
 44: 
 45: ## 2. Authorization Strategy
 46: 
 47: ### Endpoint-Level Authorization
 48: 
 49: A simple and strict convention is followed for securing API endpoints:
 50: *   **Read operations (`GET`)** are generally public and decorated with `[AllowAnonymous]`.
 51: *   **Write operations (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`)** are protected and require a valid token, enforced with `[Authorize]`.
 52: 
 53: ### Resource-Level Authorization
 54: 
 55: Fine-grained, resource-level authorization (e.g., "can this user edit *this specific* event?") is the responsibility of the **Application Layer**, typically within the MediatR handlers. This logic is not handled at the controller level.
 56: 
 57: ### Policy-Based Authorization (Cerbos)
 58: 
 59: Cerbos is actively integrated as the policy decision point (PDP) for fine-grained authorization.
 60: 
 61: Current implementation overview:
 62: 
 63: *   **Application Layer** enforces resource/action checks via MediatR `AuthorizationBehavior` before command handlers execute.
 64: *   **Infrastructure Layer** delegates policy decisions to Cerbos via HTTP in `CerbosAuthorizationService` (implements `IAuthorizationProvider`).
 65: *   **Fallback Path** exists via `FallbackAuthorizationService` (also implements `IAuthorizationProvider`) when Cerbos is disabled by configuration. A `RuntimeAuthorizationProvider` wrapper selects the active provider based on the `AuthorizationProvider` system setting.
 66: *   **API HATEOAS Layer** filters links using Cerbos batch checks so clients only receive authorized actions.
 67: *   **Blazor UI** uses DB-backed admin claims for UX gating; server-side authorization remains the hard security boundary.
 68: 
 69: This keeps endpoint authorization simple (`[AllowAnonymous]` for public reads, `[Authorize]` for writes) while enforcing fine-grained resource policies centrally.
 70: 
 71: ## 3. Fine-Grained Authorization (Cerbos)
 72: 
 73: We use **Cerbos** as an external Policy Decision Point (PDP). This decouples authorization logic from application code.
 74: 
 75: ### 3.1. Implementation Pattern
 76: 
 77: 1.  **Define Policy**: Authorization rules are defined in YAML files in the `cerbos/policies` directory.
 78: 2.  **Decorate Command**: Use `[AuthorizeResource]` on MediatR commands (optionally with `ISecureRequest` for dynamic resource IDs).
 79: 
 80: ```csharp
 81: [AuthorizeResource("event", PermissionAction.Update)]
 82: public class UpdateEventCommand : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse>
 83: {
 84:     public Guid Id { get; set; }
 85: }
 86: ```
 87: 
 88: 3.  **Pipeline Enforcement**: The `AuthorizationBehavior` pipeline detects this attribute:
 89:     *   Extracts the User (Principal) from `IUserContext`.
 90:     *   Constructs the Resource (Kind: "event", ID: `command.Id`).
 91:     *   Calls Cerbos: `Check(principal, resource, "update")`.
 92:     *   If denied, throws `ForbiddenException`.
 93: 
 94: ### 3.2. Policy Structure
 95: 
 96: Cerbos policies follow a standard hierarchy:
 97: 
 98: *   **Resource Policy**: Rules for a specific resource type (e.g., `event.yaml`).
 99: *   **Principal Policy**: Rules for specific users/roles (rarely used, prefer roles in resource policies).
100: *   **Derived Roles**: Logic to map dynamic conditions to simple roles (e.g., `owner` if `request.auth.id == resource.attr.ownerId`).
101: 
102: ---
103: 
104: ## 4. Multi-Tenancy & Keycloak
105: 
106: ### 4.1. Tenant Isolation
107: 
108: *   **Data Layer**: Enforced via Global Query Filters (`TenantId`).
109: *   **Auth Layer**: Keycloak manages identity.
110: 
111: ### 4.2. Keycloak Configuration Models
112: 
113: The system supports two multi-tenancy models in Keycloak:
114: 
115: 1.  **Shared Realm (Default)**:
116:     *   All tenants live in one Keycloak Realm.
117:     *   `TenantId` is stored as a custom attribute on the User or Group.
118:     *   Pros: Simpler management, Single Sign-On (SSO) across tenants.
119:     *   Cons: Less isolation between tenant user directories.
120: 
121: 2.  **Realm-per-Tenant**:
122:     *   Each tenant has its own Keycloak Realm.
123:     *   Pros: Total isolation, tenant-specific login pages/policies.
124:     *   Cons: No SSO, higher management overhead.
125: 
126: *Current Implementation assumes **Shared Realm** with Group-based tenancy.*
127: 
128: ---
129: 
130: ## 5. Secret Management (Infisical)
131: 
132: We use **Infisical** to manage secrets (DB connection strings, API keys, Client Secrets) at runtime.
133: 
134: *   **No Hardcoded Secrets**: `appsettings.json` contains only placeholders or non-sensitive config.
135: *   **Runtime Injection**: `AddInfisicalBlazorCompatibility()` loads secrets into the `.NET Configuration` provider at startup.
136: *   **Rotation**: Secrets can be rotated in Infisical without code changes (requires app restart).
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 6. Client-Side Authorization (UX-Only)
141: 
142: Blazor WASM receives user claims via the BFF pattern — the server serializes admin authority claims into the authentication cookie, and `AddAuthenticationStateSerialization` makes them available to the client.
143: 
144: ### What Client-Side Auth Does
145: 
146: - **Route guards** (`AdminRouteGuard`): Redirect unauthorized users away from admin pages
147: - **UI visibility**: Hide buttons, menu items, and actions the user cannot perform
148: - **Form validation**: Disable fields the user shouldn't edit
149: 
150: ### What Client-Side Auth Does NOT Do
151: 
152: Client-side authorization checks are **UX conveniences only**. They:
153: 
154: - **Cannot prevent unauthorized access** — a user can bypass Blazor WASM checks trivially
155: - **Cannot enforce security policies** — all enforcement happens server-side
156: - **Cannot be trusted** for any security decision
157: 
158: ### The Hard Security Boundary
159: 
160: ```
161: Blazor WASM (client)          →  UX gating only (hide/show)
162:      │
163:      ▼
164: Blazor Server BFF (server)    →  Cookie auth, YARP proxy
165:      │
166:      ▼
167: API Controller (server)       →  [Authorize] + JWT validation
168:      │
169:      ▼
170: AuthorizationBehavior (server) →  THE ENFORCEMENT POINT
171:      │                            Calls IAuthorizationProvider
172:      │                            Throws ForbiddenException if denied
173:      ▼
174: Handler (server)              →  Business logic (only runs if authorized)
175: ```
176: 
177: `AuthorizationBehavior` in the MediatR pipeline is the **only** authorization enforcement point. Every write operation passes through it before reaching the handler.
178: 
179: For pattern details, see [AUTHORIZATION_PATTERNS.md](AUTHORIZATION_PATTERNS.md).
180: 
181: ---
182: For implementation details, see the `auth-patterns` skill.
````

````csharp
  1: using Explore.Blazor.Client.Models;
  2: using Explore.Blazor.Client.Pages.Event;

 74:     private static PaginatedResult<EventListDto> CreateResult(int pageNumber, int pageSize, List<EventListDto> items)

 82:         };

 85:     private void SetupPagedResult(Task<PaginatedResult<EventListDto>> resultTask)
 86:     {

 88:             Arg.Any<int>(),
 89:             Arg.Any<int>(),
 90:             Arg.Any<string?>(),
 91:             Arg.Any<Guid?>(),
 92:             Arg.Any<Guid?>(),
 93:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
 94:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
 95:             Arg.Any<Guid?>(),
 96:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
 97:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
 98:             Arg.Any<DateTimeOffset?>(),
 99:             Arg.Any<DateTimeOffset?>(),
100:             Arg.Any<string?>(),
101:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
102:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
103:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
104:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
105:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
106:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
107:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
108:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
109:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
110:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
111:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
112:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
113:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
114:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
115:             Arg.Any<string?>(),
116:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
117:             Arg.Any<CancellationToken>())
118:             .Returns(resultTask);
119:     }
120: 
121:     private static async Task InvokeLoadEventsAsync(IRenderedComponent<EventList> cut)
122:     {
123:         var loadEventsMethod = typeof(EventList).GetMethod("LoadEventsAsync", System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Instance | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic);
124:         if (loadEventsMethod is null)
125:         {
126:             throw new InvalidOperationException("LoadEventsAsync method was not found on EventList.");
127:         }
128: 
129:         var request = new ItemsProviderRequest(startIndex: 0, count: 20, cancellationToken: CancellationToken.None);
130:         await cut.InvokeAsync(async () =>
131:         {
132:             var valueTask = (ValueTask<ItemsProviderResult<EventListDto>>)loadEventsMethod.Invoke(cut.Instance, [request])!;
133:             await valueTask;
134:         });
135:     }
136: 
137:     [Test]
138:     public async Task EventList_DoesNotShowEmptyState_BeforeFirstEventsLoadCompletes()
139:     {
140: 
141:         var pendingResult = new TaskCompletionSource<PaginatedResult<EventListDto>>();
142:         SetupPagedResult(pendingResult.Task);
143: 
144: 
145:         var cut = _ctx.RenderMudComponent<EventList>();
146: 
147: 
148:         if (cut.Markup.Contains("No events found"))
149:         {
150:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Empty state should not be displayed before first events load completes.");
151:         }
152: 
153: 
154:         pendingResult.TrySetResult(CreateResult(1, 20, []));
155:         await Task.CompletedTask;
156:     }
157: 
158:     [Test]
159:     public async Task EventList_ShowsNoEventsState_OnlyAfterInitialLoadCompletesWithEmptyResult()
160:     {
161: 
162:         var pendingResult = new TaskCompletionSource<PaginatedResult<EventListDto>>();
163:         SetupPagedResult(pendingResult.Task);
164: 
165: 
166:         var cut = _ctx.RenderMudComponent<EventList>();
167: 
168: 
169:         cut.WaitForAssertion(() =>
170:         {
171:             if (cut.Markup.Contains("No events found"))
172:             {
173:                 throw new InvalidOperationException("Empty state should not be visible before first event load completes.");
174:             }
175:         });
176: 
177: 
178:         pendingResult.SetResult(CreateResult(1, 20, []));
179:         await InvokeLoadEventsAsync(cut);
180: 
181:         if (!cut.Markup.Contains("No events found"))
182:         {
183:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Expected empty-state message after completed empty load.");
184:         }
185: 
186:         await Task.CompletedTask;
187:     }
188: 
189:     [Test]
190:     public async Task EventList_HidesNoEventsState_WhenResultsExist()
191:     {
192: 
193:         var events = new List<EventListDto>
194:         {
195:             new() { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), Title = "Blazor Summit", Description = "Event description" }
196:         };
197:         SetupPagedResult(Task.FromResult(CreateResult(1, 20, events)));
198: 
199: 
200:         var cut = _ctx.RenderMudComponent<EventList>();
201: 
202: 
203:         await InvokeLoadEventsAsync(cut);
204: 
205:         if (!cut.Markup.Contains("Blazor Summit"))
206:         {
207:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Expected event title in rendered markup.");
208:         }
209: 
210:         if (cut.Markup.Contains("No events found"))
211:         {
212:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Empty-state message should not be visible when events exist.");
213:         }
214: 
215:         if (!cut.Markup.Contains("1 events found"))
216:         {
217:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Expected total count text for non-empty result.");
218:         }
219: 
220:         await Task.CompletedTask;
221:     }
222: }

  1: using Blazouter.Services;

 10: 
 11: public partial class OrganizationMembers
 12: {
 13:     [Inject] protected IOrganizationMemberService MemberService { get; set; } = null!;
 14:     [Inject] protected IOrganizationService OrganizationService { get; set; } = null!;
 15:     [Inject] protected IDialogService DialogService { get; set; } = null!;
 16:     [Inject] protected NavigationManager Navigation { get; set; } = null!;
 17:     [Inject] protected AuthenticationStateProvider AuthenticationStateProvider { get; set; } = null!;
 18:     [Inject] protected RouterStateService RouterState { get; set; } = null!;
 19: 
 20:     private Guid Id { get; set; }
 21:     private List<OrganizationMemberDto> Members = new();
 22:     private bool _loading = true;
 23:     private string? currentUserId;
 24:     private int? currentUserRole;
 25:     private string? _errorMessage;
 26: 
 27:     private string _searchString = "";
 28:     private int? _roleFilter;
 29: 
 30:     private IEnumerable<OrganizationMemberDto> FilteredMembers =>
 31:         Members
 32:             .Where(x => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_searchString) ||
 33:                         (x.UserFullName?.Contains(_searchString, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ?? false) ||
 34:                         (x.UserEmail?.Contains(_searchString, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ?? false))
 35:             .Where(x => _roleFilter == null || x.OrganizationRoleId == _roleFilter);
 36: 
 37:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 38:     {
 39:         var idStr = RouterState.GetParam("id");
 40:         if (Guid.TryParse(idStr, out var id))
 41:         {
 42:             Id = id;
 43:         }
 44: 
 45:         var authState = await AuthenticationStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();
 46:         var user = authState.User;
 47:         currentUserId = user.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
 48:             ?? user.FindFirst("http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier")?.Value
 49:             ?? user.FindFirst("oid")?.Value;
 50: 
 51:         await LoadMembers();
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     private void DetermineCurrentUserRole()
 55:     {
 56:         if (currentUserId != null)
 57:         {
 58:             var me = Members.FirstOrDefault(m => m.UserId.ToString().Equals(currentUserId, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
 59:             if (me != null)
 60:             {
 61:                 currentUserRole = me.OrganizationRoleId;
 62:             }
 63:         }
 64:     }
 65: 
 66:     private async Task LoadMembers()
 67:     {
 68:         _loading = true;
 69:         _errorMessage = null;
 70:         try
 71:         {
 72:             Members = (await MemberService.GetMembersAsync(Id))?.ToList() ?? new List<OrganizationMemberDto>();
 73:             DetermineCurrentUserRole();
 74:         }
 75:         catch (Exception ex)
 76:         {
 77:             _errorMessage = $"Error loading members: {ex.Message}";
 78:         }
 79:         finally
 80:         {
 81:             _loading = false;
 82:         }
 83:     }
 84: 
 85:     private Color GetRoleColor(int role)
 86:     {
 87:         return RoleHelper.GetRoleColor(role);
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     private string GetRoleName(int role)
 91:     {
 92:         return RoleHelper.GetRoleName(role);
 93:     }
 94: 
 95:     private async Task OpenInviteDialog()
 96:     {
 97:         var parameters = new DialogParameters { ["OrganizationId"] = Id };
 98:         var dialog = await DialogService.ShowAsync<InviteMemberDialog>("Invite Member", parameters);
 99:         var result = await dialog.Result;
100: 
101:         if (!result.Canceled)
102:         {
103:             await LoadMembers();
104:         }
105:     }
106: 
107:     private async Task OpenEditRoleDialog(OrganizationMemberDto member)
108:     {
109:         var parameters = new DialogParameters { ["Member"] = member, ["OrganizationId"] = Id };
110:         var dialog = await DialogService.ShowAsync<EditMemberRoleDialog>("Edit Role", parameters);
111:         var result = await dialog.Result;
112: 
113:         if (!result.Canceled)
114:         {
115:             await LoadMembers();
116:         }
117:     }
118: 
119:     private async Task RemoveMember(OrganizationMemberDto member)
120:     {
121:         bool? result = await DialogService.ShowMessageBox(
122:             "Remove Member",
123:             $"Are you sure you want to remove {member.UserEmail} from the organization?",
124:             yesText: "Remove", cancelText: "Cancel");
125: 
126:         if (result == true)
127:         {
128:             try
129:             {
130:                 if (!member.Id.HasValue)
131:                 {
132:                     _errorMessage = "Member ID is missing";
133:                     return;
134:                 }
135:                 await MemberService.DeleteMemberAsync(member.Id.Value);
136:                 await LoadMembers();
137:             }
138:             catch (Exception ex)
139:             {
140:                 _errorMessage = $"Error removing member: {ex.Message}";
141:             }
142:         }
143:     }
144: }

 10: public interface IUserService

 12: 
 13: 
 14: 
 15:     Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> SyncUserAsync();
 16: 
 17: 
 18:

 20:     Task<UserDto?> GetCurrentUserAsync();
 21:

 35: 
 36: public class UserService : IUserService
 37: {
 38:     private readonly IEventApiClient _apiClient;
 39:     private readonly ILogger<UserService> _logger;
 40: 
 41:     public UserService(IEventApiClient apiClient, ILogger<UserService> logger)
 42:     {
 43:         _apiClient = apiClient ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(apiClient));
 44:         _logger = logger ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(logger));
 45:     }
 46: 
 47: 
 48:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> SyncUserAsync()
 49:     {
 50:         try
 51:         {
 52:             _logger.LogInformation("Syncing user");
 53:             var response = await _apiClient.SyncAsync();
 54:             _logger.LogInformation("Sync result: Success={Success}, Id={Id}", response?.Success, response?.Id);
 55:             return response;
 56:         }
 57:         catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == 200)
 58:         {
 59: 
 60: 
 61:             _logger.LogWarning(ex, "Sync completed with status 200 but response parsing issue");
 62:             return new BaseCommandResponseOfGuid
 63:             {
 64:                 Success = true,
 65:                 Message = "User synced successfully"
 66:             };
 67:         }
 68:         catch (ApiException ex)
 69:         {
 70:             _logger.LogError(ex, "API error syncing user: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
 71:             return new BaseCommandResponseOfGuid
 72:             {
 73:                 Success = false,
 74:                 Message = $"API error: {ex.Message}",
 75:                 Errors = new List<string> { ex.Response ?? ex.Message }
 76:             };
 77:         }
 78:         catch (Exception ex)
 79:         {
 80:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Error syncing user");
 81:             return new BaseCommandResponseOfGuid
 82:             {
 83:                 Success = false,
 84:                 Message = $"Error: {ex.Message}",
 85:                 Errors = new List<string> { ex.Message }
 86:             };
 87:         }
 88:     }
 89: 
 90: 
 91:     public async Task<UserDto?> GetCurrentUserAsync()
 92:     {
 93:         try
 94:         {
 95:             _logger.LogInformation("Fetching current user");
 96:             var user = await _apiClient.UserGETAsync();
 97:             _logger.LogInformation("User found: {Email}", user?.Email);
 98:             return user;
 99:         }
100:         catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == 404)
101:         {
102:             _logger.LogWarning("User not found (404) - attempting auto-sync");
103: 
104: 
105:             try
106:             {
107:                 var syncResult = await SyncUserAsync();
108:                 if (syncResult?.Success == true)
109:                 {
110:                     _logger.LogInformation("Auto-sync successful, retrying GetCurrentUser");
111:                     await Task.Delay(100);
112:                     return await _apiClient.UserGETAsync();
113:                 }
114:                 else
115:                 {
116:                     _logger.LogWarning("Auto-sync failed: {Message}", syncResult?.Message);
117:                 }
118:             }
119:             catch (Exception syncEx)
120:             {
121:                 _logger.LogError(syncEx, "Auto-sync exception");
122:             }
123: 
124:             return null;
125:         }
126:         catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == 401)
127:         {
128:             _logger.LogWarning("User not authenticated (401)");
129:             return null;
130:         }
131:         catch (ApiException ex)
132:         {
133:             _logger.LogError(ex, "API error: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
134:             return null;
135:         }
136:         catch (Exception ex)
137:         {
138:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Error getting user");
139:             return null;
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143: 
144:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> UpdateUserAsync(UpdateUserDto userDto)
145:     {
146:         try
147:         {
148:             _logger.LogInformation("Updating user");
149:             return await _apiClient.UserPUTAsync(userDto);
150:         }
151:         catch (ApiException ex)
152:         {
153:             _logger.LogError(ex, "API error updating user: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
154:             return null;
155:         }
156:         catch (Exception ex)
157:         {
158:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Error updating user");
159:             return null;
160:         }
161:     }
162: 
163: 
164:     public async Task<bool> DeleteUserAsync()
165:     {
166:         try
167:         {
168:             _logger.LogInformation("Deleting user");
169:             await _apiClient.UserDELETEAsync();
170:             return true;
171:         }
172:         catch (ApiException ex)
173:         {
174:             _logger.LogError(ex, "API error deleting user: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
175:             return false;
176:         }
177:         catch (Exception ex)
178:         {

181:         }
