## File: .claude/agents/README.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: Agents Documentation
  3: description: Documentation file - not an executable agent
  4: disabled: true
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: # Project Agents
  8: 
  9: > **Project-Agnostic Autonomous Agents for Complex Tasks**
 10: >
 11: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 12: 
 13: Specialized autonomous agents for complex, multi-step tasks in Clean Architecture .NET projects.
 14: 
 15: ---
 16: 
 17: ## Overview
 18: 
 19: Agents are autonomous Claude instances that handle specific complex tasks. Unlike skills (which provide inline guidance), agents:
 20: 
 21: - Run as separate sub-tasks with focused objectives
 22: - Work autonomously with minimal supervision
 23: - Have specialized tool access for their domain
 24: - Return comprehensive reports upon completion
 25: 
 26: **Key Advantage**: Agents are standalone—just reference the agent name and Claude Code handles the rest.
 27: 
 28: ---
 29: 
 30: ## Available Agents
 31: 
 32: | Agent | Purpose | When to Use |
 33: |-------|---------|-------------|
 34: | [blazor-component-architect](#blazor-component-architect) | Design and review Blazor components | Component architecture, MudBlazor patterns, BFF compliance |
 35: | [code-architecture-reviewer](#code-architecture-reviewer) | Review code for architectural consistency | After implementing features, before merging changes |
 36: | [code-refactor-master](#code-refactor-master) | Enforce Clean Architecture with CQRS | Architecture violations, pattern compliance |
 37: | [documentation-architect](#documentation-architect) | Create comprehensive documentation | API docs, developer guides, architectural overviews |
 38: | [frontend-error-fixer](#frontend-error-fixer) | Debug Blazor frontend errors | Compilation errors, MudBlazor issues, render mode problems |
 39: | [plan-reviewer](#plan-reviewer) | Review development plans | Before starting complex features, validating approaches |
 40: | [refactor-planner](#refactor-planner) | Create refactoring strategies | Code reorganization, modernizing legacy code |
 41: | [web-research-specialist](#web-research-specialist) | Research technical issues | Debugging obscure errors, finding best practices |
 42: | [auth-route-tester](#auth-route-tester) | Test authenticated API endpoints | Validating endpoint functionality, debugging auth |
 43: | [auth-route-debugger](#auth-route-debugger) | Debug authentication issues | Token issues, cookie problems, permission errors |
 44: | [auto-error-resolver](#auto-error-resolver) | Automatically fix C#/.NET errors | Build failures, systematic error resolution |
 45: 
 46: ---
 47: 
 48: ## Agent Details
 49: 
 50: ### blazor-component-architect
 51: 
 52: **Purpose**: Design and review Blazor Server + WASM components for {Project}.
 53: 
 54: **Capabilities**:
 55: - Blazor hybrid rendering patterns (Server + WASM)
 56: - MudBlazor component best practices
 57: - BFF architecture validation
 58: - Service layer patterns
 59: - Authentication state management
 60: 
 61: **Example Usage**:
 62: ```
 63: Use the blazor-component-architect agent to review the {Entity}List.razor component
 64: ```
 65: 
 66: ---
 67: 
 68: ### code-architecture-reviewer
 69: 
 70: **Purpose**: Review code for architectural consistency and best practices.
 71: 
 72: **Capabilities**:
 73: - Clean Architecture layer validation
 74: - CQRS pattern compliance
 75: - Repository pattern enforcement
 76: - Controller pattern review
 77: 
 78: **Example Usage**:
 79: ```
 80: Use the code-architecture-reviewer agent to review the new {Entity} feature
 81: ```
 82: 
 83: ---
 84: 
 85: ### code-refactor-master
 86: 
 87: **Purpose**: Enforce Clean Architecture with CQRS patterns for {Project}.
 88: 
 89: **Capabilities**:
 90: - Repository pattern enforcement (entities only, no DTOs)
 91: - CQRS validation (BaseCommandResponse<Guid> for commands)
 92: - Validation pattern checks (manual validation in handlers)
 93: - Controller pattern review (AllowAnonymous vs Authorize)
 94: 
 95: **Example Usage**:
 96: ```
 97: Use the code-refactor-master agent to check the {Entity} handlers
 98: ```
 99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ### documentation-architect
103: 
104: **Purpose**: Create comprehensive documentation following project standards.
105: 
106: **Capabilities**:
107: - C# XML documentation generation
108: - Swagger/Scalar API annotations
109: - Architecture documentation
110: - Developer guides
111: 
112: **Example Usage**:
113: ```
114: Use the documentation-architect agent to document the {Entity}Session endpoints
115: ```
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ### frontend-error-fixer
120: 
121: **Purpose**: Debug and fix Blazor frontend errors.
122: 
123: **Capabilities**:
124: - Blazor compilation error resolution
125: - MudBlazor component debugging
126: - Render mode issue diagnosis
127: - Razor syntax fixes
128: 
129: **Example Usage**:
130: ```
131: Use the frontend-error-fixer agent to fix the error in Create{Entity}.razor
132: ```
133: 
134: ---
135: 
136: ### plan-reviewer
137: 
138: **Purpose**: Review development plans before implementation.
139: 
140: **Capabilities**:
141: - .NET best practices validation
142: - EF Core performance review
143: - Security assessment
144: - Clean Architecture compliance
145: 
146: **Example Usage**:
147: ```
148: Use the plan-reviewer agent to review my implementation plan for user authentication
149: ```
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ### refactor-planner
154: 
155: **Purpose**: Create comprehensive refactoring strategies.
156: 
157: **Capabilities**:
158: - Legacy code modernization plans
159: - Technical debt cleanup strategies
160: - Clean Architecture enforcement
161: - Step-by-step refactoring guides
162: 
163: **Example Usage**:
164: ```
165: Use the refactor-planner agent to plan refactoring the {Entity} module
166: ```
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: ### web-research-specialist
171: 
172: **Purpose**: Research technical issues and best practices.
173: 
174: **Capabilities**:
175: - .NET backend library research
176: - PostGIS solutions investigation
177: - Ecosystem best practices
178: - Solution comparison
179: 
180: **Example Usage**:
181: ```
182: Use the web-research-specialist agent to research pagination strategies for EF Core
183: ```
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ### auth-route-tester
188: 
189: **Purpose**: Test authenticated API endpoints for {Project}.
190: 
191: **Requirements**: Requires active authentication session.
192: 
193: **Capabilities**:
194: - Authentication endpoint testing
195: - Authorization validation
196: - Security regression testing
197: 
198: **Example Usage**:
199: ```
200: Use the auth-route-tester agent to test the {Entity} controller endpoints
201: ```
202: 
203: ---
204: 
205: ### auth-route-debugger
206: 
207: **Purpose**: Debug ASP.NET Core authentication issues with OIDC/JWT.
208: 
209: **Requirements**: Requires JWT/cookie-based authentication setup.
210: 
211: **Capabilities**:
212: - OIDC flow debugging
213: - Token validation issues
214: - Cookie configuration problems
215: - Claim extraction troubleshooting
216: 
217: **Example Usage**:
218: ```
219: Use the auth-route-debugger agent to debug why users can't access protected endpoints
220: ```
221: 
222: ---
223: 
224: ### auto-error-resolver
225: 
226: **Purpose**: Automatically resolve C#/.NET compilation and runtime errors.
227: 
228: **Capabilities**:
229: - Build error resolution
230: - Type error fixes
231: - Missing reference detection
232: - DI registration issues
233: 
234: **Example Usage**:
235: ```
236: Use the auto-error-resolver agent to fix the current build errors
237: ```
238: 
239: ---
240: 
241: ## When to Use Agents vs Skills
242: 
243: | Use Agents When... | Use Skills When... |
244: |-------------------|-------------------|
245: | Task requires multiple autonomous steps | Need inline guidance while coding |
246: | Complex analysis is needed | Checking best practices |
247: | Clear end goal exists | Ongoing development work |
248: | Want comprehensive report | Want to maintain control |
249: | **Example**: "Review all controllers" | **Example**: "Creating a new route" |
250: 
251: **Complementary Usage**:
252: - Use a **skill** for patterns during development
253: - Use an **agent** to review the result when complete
254: 
255: ---
256: 
257: ## Creating Custom Agents
258: 
259: Agents are markdown files with YAML frontmatter:
260: 
261: ```markdown
262: ---
263: name: my-custom-agent
264: description: Brief description of the agent's purpose
265: tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
266: ---
267: 
268: # Agent Name
269: 
270: ## Purpose
271: What this agent accomplishes
272: 
273: ## Instructions
274: Step-by-step instructions for autonomous execution
275: 
276: ## Tools Available
277: - Read: For reading files
278: - Edit: For modifying files
279: - Bash: For running commands
280: 
281: ## Expected Output
282: What format to return results in
283: ```
284: 
285: **Best Practices**:
286: - Be specific in instructions
287: - Break complex tasks into numbered steps
288: - Specify exactly what to return
289: - Include examples of good output
290: - List available tools explicitly
291: 
292: ---
293: 
294: ## Troubleshooting
295: 
296: ### Agent Not Found
297: 
298: Verify the agent file exists:
299: ```powershell
300: Get-ChildItem .claude\agents\agent-name.md
301: ```
302: 
303: ### Agent Fails with Path Errors
304: 
305: Check for hardcoded paths:
306: ```powershell
307: Select-String -Path ".claude\agents\agent-name.md" -Pattern "~/|/root/|/Users/"
308: ```
309: 
310: Fix by replacing with relative paths or `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`.
311: 
312: ### Agent Returns Incomplete Results
313: 
314: - Ensure the task is well-defined
315: - Break complex tasks into smaller sub-tasks
316: - Provide more context in the initial prompt
317: 
318: ---
319: 
320: ## Related Documentation
321: 
322: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - System architecture overview
323: - [`docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md`](../../docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md) - Critical rules and patterns
324: - [`.claude/skills/`](../skills/) - Inline guidance skills
````

## File: .claude/skills/clean-architecture-rules/resources/dependency-rules.md
````markdown
  1: # Dependency Rules - Complete Reference
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Dependency Rules**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Dependency Matrix
  8: 
  9: | Layer | Can Reference | Cannot Reference | Framework Dependencies Allowed |
 10: |-------|---------------|------------------|-------------------------------|
 11: | **{Project}.Domain** | Nothing | Everything | None (pure C#) |
 12: | **{Project}.Application** | Domain | Infrastructure, Persistence, API, Blazor | MediatR, FluentValidation, AutoMapper |
 13: | **{Project}.Persistence** | Application, Domain | API, Blazor | EF Core, Database Provider, PostGIS |
 14: | **{Project}.Infrastructure** | Application, Domain | API, Blazor | Any (email, file storage, external APIs) |
 15: | **{Project}.API** | All | None (top layer) | ASP.NET Core, Swashbuckle, Serilog |
 16: | **{Project}.Blazor** | All | None (top layer) | Blazor, MudBlazor, SignalR |
 17: | **{Project}.Blazor.Client** | Shared DTOs | Server components | Blazor WebAssembly, MudBlazor |
 18: 
 19: ## Visual Dependency Flow
 20: 
 21: ```mermaid
 22: graph TD
 23:     subgraph Presentation Layer
 24:         A[{Project}.API]
 25:         B[{Project}.Blazor]
 26:     end
 27: 
 28:     subgraph Infrastructure Layer
 29:         C[{Project}.Persistence]
 30:         D[{Project}.Infrastructure]
 31:     end
 32: 
 33:     subgraph Application Layer
 34:         E[{Project}.Application]
 35:     end
 36: 
 37:     subgraph Domain Layer
 38:         F[{Project}.Domain]
 39:     end
 40: 
 41:     A --> E
 42:     A --> C
 43:     A --> D
 44: 
 45:     B --> E
 46:     B --> C
 47:     B --> D
 48: 
 49:     C --> E
 50:     C --> F
 51: 
 52:     D --> E
 53:     D --> F
 54: 
 55:     E --> F
 56: 
 57:     style A fill:#fbe5c5,stroke:#333
 58:     style B fill:#fbe5c5,stroke:#333
 59:     style C fill:#c5fbe5,stroke:#333
 60:     style D fill:#c5fbe5,stroke:#333
 61:     style E fill:#e5c5fb,stroke:#333
 62:     style F fill:#c5fbc5,stroke:#333
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: ## The Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
 66: 
 67: **Core Idea**: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions.
 68: 
 69: ### Example: Application needs Database Access
 70: 
 71: **❌ WITHOUT Dependency Inversion** (Violation):
 72: ```
 73: Application ──────> Infrastructure
 74: (high-level)        (low-level, concrete)
 75: 
 76: Create{Entity}CommandHandler → {DbContext}
 77: ```
 78: *Problem*: Application layer depends on concrete Infrastructure implementation.
 79: 
 80: **✅ WITH Dependency Inversion** (Correct):
 81: ```
 82: Application ──────> I{Entity}Repository (Interface)
 83:                            ▲
 84:                            │ implements
 85: Infrastructure ────────────┘
 86: {Entity}Repository (implements I{Entity}Repository)
 87: ```
 88: *Solution*: Both depend on abstraction (interface) defined in Application.
 89: 
 90: ## Allowed `using` Statements by Layer
 91: 
 92: ### {Project}.Domain
 93: 
 94: ```csharp
 95: // File: {Project}.Domain/{Entity}.cs
 96: namespace {Project}.Domain;
 97: 
 98: // ✅ ALLOWED - Pure C# only
 99: using System;
100: using System.Collections.Generic;
101: using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.Schema;
102: 
103: public class {Entity}
104: {
105:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
106: 
107:     [ForeignKey("{LookupEntity}")]
108:     public {LookupIdType} {LookupEntity}Id { get; set; }
109:     public {LookupEntity} {LookupEntity} { get; set; }
110: 
111:     [ForeignKey("{RelatedEntity}")]
112:     public {IdType} {RelatedEntity}Id { get; set; }
113:     public {RelatedEntity} {RelatedEntity} { get; set; }
114: 
115:     // ... more navigation properties
116: }
117: 
118: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED in Domain
119: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;           // Infrastructure concern
120: using {Project}.Application;                   // Layer above
121: using {Project}.Infrastructure;                // Layer above
122: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
123: using MediatR;                                 // Application concern
124: ```
125: 
126: ### {Project}.Application
127: 
128: ```csharp
129: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
130: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
131: 
132: // ✅ ALLOWED
133: using System;
134: using System.Collections.Generic;
135: using System.Linq;
136: using System.Threading;
137: using System.Threading.Tasks;
138: using AutoMapper;                                       // Application framework
139: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;     // Same layer
140: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};             // Same layer
141: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;  // Same layer
142: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;  // Same layer
143: using {Project}.Application.Responses;                 // Same layer
144: using {Project}.Domain;                                // Domain entities
145: using MediatR;                                         // CQRS framework
146: 
147: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
148: using {Project}.Persistence;                   // Infrastructure layer
149: using {Project}.Infrastructure;                // Infrastructure layer
150: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
151: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;           // Infrastructure concern
152: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
153: ```
154: 
155: ### {Project}.Persistence
156: 
157: ```csharp
158: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
159: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
160: 
161: // ✅ ALLOWED
162: using System;
163: using System.Collections.Generic;
164: using System.Linq;
165: using System.Threading.Tasks;
166: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;     // Application interfaces
167: using {Project}.Domain;                                // Domain entities
168: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;                   // ORM framework
169: 
170: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
171: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
172: using {Project}.Blazor;                        // Presentation layer
173: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
174: ```
175: 
176: ### {Project}.Infrastructure
177: 
178: ```csharp
179: // File: {Project}.Infrastructure/Email/EmailService.cs
180: namespace {Project}.Infrastructure.Email;
181: 
182: // ✅ ALLOWED
183: using {Project}.Domain;                                   // Domain entities
184: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;     // Application interfaces
185: using SendGrid;                                           // External service
186: using Azure.Storage.Blobs;                                // External service
187: 
188: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
189: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
190: using {Project}.Blazor;                        // Presentation layer
191: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
192: ```
193: 
194: ### {Project}.API
195: 
196: ```csharp
197: // File: {Project}.API/Controllers/{Entity}Controller.cs
198: namespace {Project}.API.Controllers;
199: 
200: // ✅ ALLOWED (Everything)
201: using System;
202: using System.Collections.Generic;
203: using System.Linq;
204: using System.Security.Claims;
205: using System.Threading.Tasks;
206: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};                          // DTOs
207: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
208: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
209: using {Project}.Application.Responses;                              // Response wrappers
210: using MediatR;                                                      // CQRS
211: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;                           // Auth
212: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;                                    // HTTP context
213: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                                     // Controllers
214: // ... any other dependencies
215: ```
216: 
217: ## Project Reference Rules (.csproj)
218: 
219: ### {Project}.Domain.csproj
220: ```xml
221: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
222:   <PropertyGroup>
223:     <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
224:   </PropertyGroup>
225: 
226:   <!-- ✅ NO PROJECT REFERENCES -->
227:   <ItemGroup>
228:     <!-- Only System.ComponentModel.Annotations for [ForeignKey] -->
229:     <PackageReference Include="System.ComponentModel.Annotations" Version="10.0.0" />
230:   </ItemGroup>
231: </Project>
232: ```
233: 
234: ### {Project}.Application.csproj
235: ```xml
236: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
237:   <ItemGroup>
238:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: Reference to Domain -->
239:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Domain\{Project}.Domain.csproj" />
240:   </ItemGroup>
241: 
242:   <ItemGroup>
243:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: Framework packages -->
244:     <PackageReference Include="MediatR" Version="12.4.0" />
245:     <PackageReference Include="FluentValidation" Version="11.9.0" />
246:     <PackageReference Include="AutoMapper" Version="13.0.1" />
247:   </ItemGroup>
248: 
249:   <!-- ❌ NOT ALLOWED: References to Infrastructure, Persistence, API, Blazor -->
250: </Project>
251: ```
252: 
253: ### {Project}.Persistence.csproj
254: ```xml
255: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
256:   <ItemGroup>
257:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: References to Domain and Application -->
258:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Domain\{Project}.Domain.csproj" />
259:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Application\{Project}.Application.csproj" />
260:   </ItemGroup>
261: 
262:   <ItemGroup>
263:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: EF Core and database packages -->
264:     <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore" Version="10.0.0" />
265:     <PackageReference Include="Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL" Version="10.0.0" />
266:   </ItemGroup>
267: </Project>
268: ```
269: 
270: ### {Project}.API.csproj
271: ```xml
272: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
273:   <ItemGroup>
274:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: References to ALL -->
275:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Application\{Project}.Application.csproj" />
276:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Infrastructure\{Project}.Infrastructure.csproj" />
277:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Persistence\{Project}.Persistence.csproj" />
278:   </ItemGroup>
279: </Project>
280: ```
281: 
282: ## Verification Commands
283: 
284: ### Check Project References
285: ```bash
286: # Domain should have NO project references
287: dotnet list {Project}.Domain/{Project}.Domain.csproj reference
288: 
289: # Application should ONLY reference Domain
290: dotnet list {Project}.Application/{Project}.Application.csproj reference
291: 
292: # Persistence should reference Domain + Application
293: dotnet list {Project}.Persistence/{Project}.Persistence.csproj reference
294: ```
295: 
296: ### Search for Violations
297: ```bash
298: # Find prohibited using statements in Domain
299: rg "using (Microsoft\.(EntityFrameworkCore|AspNetCore)|{Project}\.(Application|Infrastructure|API|Blazor))" {Project}.Domain/
300: 
301: # Find validation annotations in Domain (except [ForeignKey])
302: rg "\[Required\]|\[MaxLength\]|\[Range\]|\[StringLength\]" {Project}.Domain/
303: ```
304: 
305: ## Common Questions
306: 
307: ### Q: Can Domain use System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations?
308: **A**: LIMITED USE. Only `[ForeignKey]` is acceptable for EF Core relationships. Avoid `[Required]`, `[MaxLength]`, `[Range]` etc.
309: 
310: ```csharp
311: // File: {Project}.Domain/{Entity}.cs
312: public class {Entity}
313: {
314:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
315: 
316:     // ✅ OK - Specifies foreign key relationship
317:     [ForeignKey("{LookupEntity}")]
318:     public {LookupIdType} {LookupEntity}Id { get; set; }
319:     public {LookupEntity} {LookupEntity} { get; set; }
320: 
321:     // ❌ NOT OK - Validation annotations
322:     // [Required]
323:     // [MaxLength(200)]
324:     public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
325: }
326: ```
327: 
328: **Why**: `[ForeignKey]` is metadata for EF Core navigation, not validation. Use FluentValidation in Application layer for validation rules.
329: 
330: ### Q: Can Application use AutoMapper?
331: **A**: ✅ YES. AutoMapper is an Application-layer concern for mapping Domain entities to DTOs.
332: 
333: ```csharp
334: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs
335: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
336: {
337:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
338:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
339: 
340:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
341:     {
342:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // Returns List<{Entity}>
343:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});  // ✅ Maps to DTOs
344:     }
345: }
346: ```
347: 
348: ### Q: Can Application reference EF Core for IQueryable?
349: **A**: ❌ NO. Define repository interfaces that return `Task<List<T>>` instead. Let Infrastructure handle IQueryable.
350: 
351: **Correct Pattern**:
352: ```csharp
353: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs
354: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
355: 
356: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
357: {
358:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
359:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // ✅ Returns List<{Entity}>, not IQueryable
360: }
361: 
362: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
363: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
364: {
365:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
366:     {
367:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}  // ✅ EF Core IQueryable handled here
368:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
369:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity})
370:             .ToListAsync();  // ✅ Materializes to List
371:     }
372: }
373: ```
374: 
375: ### Q: Where do I put Email sending logic?
376: **A**:
377: - **Interface**: `{Project}.Application/Contracts/Infrastructure/IEmailService.cs`
378: - **Implementation**: `{Project}.Infrastructure/Services/EmailService.cs`
379: - **Usage**: Application layer uses `IEmailService`, Infrastructure provides concrete implementation
380: 
381: ### Q: Can Blazor.Client reference Persistence?
382: **A**: ❌ NO. Blazor.Client runs in the browser (WebAssembly) and cannot access databases directly. Use shared DTOs and API calls.
383: 
384: **Correct Pattern**:
385: ```csharp
386: // Shared DTO in {Project}.Application
387: public record {Entity}ListDto
388: {
389:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
390:     public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
391:     public string {LookupEntity}Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
392: }
393: 
394: // API endpoint in {Project}.API
395: [HttpGet]
396: [AllowAnonymous]
397: public async Task<ActionResult<List<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll()
398: {
399:     var {entities} = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}ListRequest());
400:     return Ok({entities});
401: }
402: 
403: // Blazor.Client calls API
404: @inject HttpClient Http
405: 
406: var {entities} = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<{Entity}ListDto>>("/api/v1/{entity}");
407: ```
408: 
409: ---
410: 
411: **Next**: See [violation-examples.md](violation-examples.md) for common mistakes and [fix-patterns.md](fix-patterns.md) for comprehensive fix strategies.
````

## File: .claude/skills/clean-architecture-rules/resources/fix-patterns.md
````markdown
  1: # Fix Patterns - How to Resolve Violations
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Fix Patterns Reference**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Pattern #1: Move Logic to Correct Layer
  8: 
  9: ### Scenario: Business Logic in Controller
 10: 
 11: **❌ Before** (Logic in wrong layer):
 12: ```csharp
 13: // File: {Project}.API/Controllers/{Entity}Controller.cs
 14: [HttpPost]
 15: public async Task<ActionResult> Create(Create{Entity}Dto dto)
 16: {
 17:     // ❌ Business logic in controller
 18:     if (dto.Title == null || dto.Title.Length > 500)
 19:         return BadRequest("Title must be between 1 and 500 characters");
 20: 
 21:     if (dto.{LookupEntity}Id <= 0)
 22:         return BadRequest("{LookupEntity} is required");
 23: 
 24:     var {entity} = new {Entity}
 25:     {
 26:         Id = Guid.NewGuid(),
 27:         Title = dto.Title,
 28:         {LookupEntity}Id = dto.{LookupEntity}Id,
 29:         ViewCount = 0
 30:     };
 31: 
 32:     _dbContext.{Entities}.Add({entity});
 33:     await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 34: 
 35:     return Ok({entity}.Id);
 36: }
 37: ```
 38: 
 39: **✅ After** (Logic in correct layers):
 40: ```csharp
 41: // Step 1: Create Command in Application layer
 42: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Commands/Create{Entity}Command.cs
 43: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
 44: 
 45: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
 46: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
 47: using MediatR;
 48: 
 49: public class Create{Entity}Command : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
 50: {
 51:     public Create{Entity}Dto {Entity}Dto { get; set; } = null!;
 52: }
 53: 
 54: // Step 2: Create Validator in Application layer
 55: // File: {Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/Validators/Create{Entity}DtoValidator.cs
 56: namespace {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
 57: 
 58: using FluentValidation;
 59: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 60: 
 61: public class Create{Entity}DtoValidator : AbstractValidator<Create{Entity}Dto>
 62: {
 63:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity1}Repository _{relatedEntity1}Repository;
 64:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity2}Repository _{relatedEntity2}Repository;
 65:     private readonly I{LookupEntity}Repository _{lookupEntity}Repository;
 66:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity3}Repository _{relatedEntity3}Repository;
 67:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity4}Repository _{relatedEntity4}Repository;
 68: 
 69:     public Create{Entity}DtoValidator(
 70:         I{RelatedEntity1}Repository {relatedEntity1}Repository,
 71:         I{RelatedEntity2}Repository {relatedEntity2}Repository,
 72:         I{LookupEntity}Repository {lookupEntity}Repository,
 73:         I{RelatedEntity3}Repository {relatedEntity3}Repository,
 74:         I{RelatedEntity4}Repository {relatedEntity4}Repository)
 75:     {
 76:         _{relatedEntity1}Repository = {relatedEntity1}Repository;
 77:         _{relatedEntity2}Repository = {relatedEntity2}Repository;
 78:         _{lookupEntity}Repository = {lookupEntity}Repository;
 79:         _{relatedEntity3}Repository = {relatedEntity3}Repository;
 80:         _{relatedEntity4}Repository = {relatedEntity4}Repository;
 81: 
 82:         RuleFor(x => x.Title)
 83:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("Title is required")
 84:             .MaximumLength(200);
 85: 
 86:         RuleFor(x => x.Description)
 87:             .MaximumLength(5000)
 88:             .When(x => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(x.Description));
 89: 
 90:         RuleFor(x => x.{LookupEntity}Id)
 91:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("{LookupEntity} is required")
 92:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
 93:             {
 94:                 var exists = await _{lookupEntity}Repository.Exists(id);
 95:                 return exists;
 96:             })
 97:             .WithMessage("{LookupEntity} not found");
 98: 
 99:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity2}Id)
100:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("{RelatedEntity2} is required")
101:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
102:             {
103:                 var exists = await _{relatedEntity2}Repository.Exists(id);
104:                 return exists;
105:             })
106:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity2} not found");
107: 
108:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity1}Id)
109:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("{RelatedEntity1} is required")
110:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
111:             {
112:                 var exists = await _{relatedEntity1}Repository.Exists(id);
113:                 return exists;
114:             })
115:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity1} not found");
116: 
117:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity3}Id)
118:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
119:             {
120:                 if (!id.HasValue) return true;
121:                 return await _{relatedEntity3}Repository.Exists(id.Value);
122:             })
123:             .When(x => x.{RelatedEntity3}Id.HasValue)
124:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity3} does not exist.");
125: 
126:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity4}Id)
127:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
128:             {
129:                 if (!id.HasValue) return true;
130:                 return await _{relatedEntity4}Repository.Exists(id.Value);
131:             })
132:             .When(x => x.{RelatedEntity4}Id.HasValue)
133:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity4} does not exist.");
134:     }
135: }
136: 
137: // Step 3: Create Handler in Application layer
138: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
139: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
140: 
141: using System;
142: using System.Linq;
143: using System.Threading;
144: using System.Threading.Tasks;
145: using AutoMapper;
146: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
147: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
148: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
149: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
150: using {Project}.Domain;
151: using MediatR;
152: 
153: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
154: {
155:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
156:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity1}Repository _{relatedEntity1}Repository;
157:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity2}Repository _{relatedEntity2}Repository;
158:     private readonly I{LookupEntity}Repository _{lookupEntity}Repository;
159:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity3}Repository _{relatedEntity3}Repository;
160:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity4}Repository _{relatedEntity4}Repository;
161:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
162: 
163:     public Create{Entity}CommandHandler(
164:         I{Entity}Repository {entity}Repository,
165:         I{RelatedEntity1}Repository {relatedEntity1}Repository,
166:         I{RelatedEntity2}Repository {relatedEntity2}Repository,
167:         I{LookupEntity}Repository {lookupEntity}Repository,
168:         I{RelatedEntity3}Repository {relatedEntity3}Repository,
169:         I{RelatedEntity4}Repository {relatedEntity4}Repository,
170:         IMapper mapper)
171:     {
172:         _{entity}Repository = {entity}Repository;
173:         _{relatedEntity1}Repository = {relatedEntity1}Repository;
174:         _{relatedEntity2}Repository = {relatedEntity2}Repository;
175:         _{lookupEntity}Repository = {lookupEntity}Repository;
176:         _{relatedEntity3}Repository = {relatedEntity3}Repository;
177:         _{relatedEntity4}Repository = {relatedEntity4}Repository;
178:         _mapper = mapper;
179:     }
180: 
181:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(Create{Entity}Command request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
182:     {
183:         var response = new BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>();
184: 
185:         // ✅ Validate using FluentValidation - instantiated manually with dependencies
186:         var validator = new Create{Entity}DtoValidator(
187:             _{relatedEntity1}Repository,
188:             _{relatedEntity2}Repository,
189:             _{lookupEntity}Repository,
190:             _{relatedEntity3}Repository,
191:             _{relatedEntity4}Repository);
192: 
193:         var validationResult = await validator.ValidateAsync(request.{Entity}Dto, cancellationToken);
194: 
195:         if (!validationResult.IsValid)
196:         {
197:             response.Success = false;
198:             response.Message = "{Entity} creation failed.";
199:             response.Errors = validationResult.Errors.Select(e => e.ErrorMessage).ToList();
200:             return response;
201:         }
202: 
203:         // ✅ Map DTO to Entity
204:         var {entity} = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
205:         {entity}.ViewCount = 0;
206: 
207:         // ✅ Save through repository
208:         {entity} = await _{entity}Repository.Create({entity});
209: 
210:         response.Success = true;
211:         response.Id = {entity}.Id;
212:         response.Message = "{Entity} created successfully.";
213: 
214:         return response;
215:     }
216: }
217: 
218: // Step 4: Thin Controller in API layer
219: // File: {Project}.API/Controllers/{Entity}Controller.cs
220: namespace {Project}.API.Controllers;
221: 
222: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
223: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
224: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
225: using MediatR;
226: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
227: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
228: 
229: [Route("api/v1/[controller]")]
230: [ApiController]
231: public class {Entity}Controller : ControllerBase
232: {
233:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
234: 
235:     public {Entity}Controller(IMediator mediator) => _mediator = mediator;
236: 
237:     [HttpPost]
238:     [Authorize]
239:     public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto dto)
240:     {
241:         var command = new Create{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = dto };
242:         var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
243:         return Ok(response);
244:     }
245: }
246: ```
247: 
248: **Benefits**:
249: - ✅ Business logic is testable without HTTP
250: - ✅ Validation runs automatically via FluentValidation
251: - ✅ Controller is thin (5 lines)
252: - ✅ Logic can be reused from Blazor, CLI, etc.
253:

256: ## Pattern #2: Use Interfaces for Infrastructure Dependencies
257: 
258: ### Scenario: Application Needs Email Sending
259: 
260: **❌ Before** (Direct dependency):
261: ```csharp
262: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
263: using {Project}.Infrastructure.Email;  // ❌ VIOLATION!
264: using SendGrid;  // ❌ Infrastructure concern
265: 
266: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
267: {
268:     private readonly SendGridEmailService _emailService;  // ❌ Concrete class
269: 
270:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(Create{Entity}Command request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
271:     {
272:         // ... create {entity}
273: 
274:         await _emailService.SendAsync(email);  // ❌ Tightly coupled
275: 
276:         return response;
277:     }
278: }
279: ```
280: 
281: **✅ After** (Dependency Inversion):
282: ```csharp
283: // Step 1: Define interface in Application layer
284: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Infrastructure/IEmailService.cs
285: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;
286: 
287: using System;
288: using System.Threading;
289: using System.Threading.Tasks;
290: 
291: public interface IEmailService
292: {
293:     Task Send{Entity}CreatedNotificationAsync(
294:         {IdType} {entity}Id,
295:         string {entity}Title,
296:         string ownerEmail,
297:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
298: }
299: 
300: // Step 2: Use interface in Application layer
301: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
302: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
303: 
304: using System;
305: using System.Linq;
306: using System.Threading;
307: using System.Threading.Tasks;
308: using AutoMapper;
309: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;  // ✅ Same layer interface
310: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
311: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
312: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
313: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
314: using {Project}.Domain;
315: using MediatR;
316: 
317: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
318: {
319:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
320:     private readonly IEmailService _emailService;  // ✅ Interface
321:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
322:     // ... other dependencies
323: 
324:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(Create{Entity}Command request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
325:     {
326:         var response = new BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>();
327: 
328:         // Validation...
329:         var {entity} = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
330:         {entity}.ViewCount = 0;
331:         {entity} = await _{entity}Repository.Create({entity});
332: 
333:         // ✅ Calls interface, doesn't know about SendGrid
334:         await _emailService.Send{Entity}CreatedNotificationAsync(
335:             {entity}.Id,
336:             {entity}.Title,
337:             request.{Entity}Dto.OwnerEmail,
338:             cancellationToken);
339: 
340:         return response;
341:     }
342: }
343: 
344: // Step 3: Implement in Infrastructure layer
345: // File: {Project}.Infrastructure/Email/SendGridEmailService.cs
346: namespace {Project}.Infrastructure.Email;
347: 
348: using System;
349: using System.Threading;
350: using System.Threading.Tasks;
351: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;  // ✅ Implements interface
352: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
353: using SendGrid;
354: using SendGrid.Helpers.Mail;
355: 
356: public class SendGridEmailService : IEmailService
357: {
358:     private readonly ISendGridClient _client;
359:     private readonly ILogger<SendGridEmailService> _logger;
360: 
361:     public SendGridEmailService(ISendGridClient client, ILogger<SendGridEmailService> logger)
362:     {
363:         _client = client;
364:         _logger = logger;
365:     }
366: 
367:     public async Task Send{Entity}CreatedNotificationAsync(
368:         {IdType} {entity}Id,
369:         string {entity}Title,
370:         string ownerEmail,
371:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
372:     {
373:         var from = new EmailAddress("noreply@example.com", "Application Name");
374:         var to = new EmailAddress(ownerEmail);
375:         var subject = $"{Entity} Created: {{entity}Title}";
376:         var htmlContent = $"<p>Your {entity} <strong>{{entity}Title}</strong> has been created successfully.</p>";
377: 
378:         var msg = MailHelper.CreateSingleEmail(from, to, subject, null, htmlContent);
379: 
380:         try
381:         {
382:             var response = await _client.SendEmailAsync(msg, cancellationToken);
383:             _logger.LogInformation("Email sent to {Email} for {Entity} {{EntityId}}", ownerEmail, {entity}Id);
384:         }
385:         catch (Exception ex)
386:         {
387:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to send email for {Entity} {{EntityId}}", {entity}Id);
388:             throw;
389:         }
390:     }
391: }
392: 
393: // Step 4: Register in API (Composition Root)
394: // File: {Project}.API/Program.cs
395: builder.Services.AddScoped<IEmailService, SendGridEmailService>();
396: ```
397: 
398: **Benefits**:
399: - ✅ Application doesn't know about SendGrid
400: - ✅ Can easily swap SendGrid for Mailgun, SMTP, or mock for testing
401: - ✅ No breaking changes to Application when Infrastructure changes
402:

405: ## Pattern #3: Repository Pattern for Data Access
406: 
407: ### Scenario: Application Needs Database Queries
408: 
409: **❌ Before** (Direct DbContext access):
410: ```csharp
411: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs
412: using {Project}.Persistence;  // ❌ VIOLATION!
413: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;  // ❌ VIOLATION!
414: 
415: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
416: {
417:     private readonly {DbContext} _context;  // ❌ Concrete class
418: 
419:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
420:     {
421:         return await _context.{Entities}  // ❌ Direct DbSet access
422:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
423:             .Where(e => e.StatusId == 2)
424:             .ToListAsync(cancellationToken);
425:     }
426: }
427: ```
428: 
429: **✅ After** (Repository pattern):
430: ```csharp
431: // Step 1: Define repository interface in Application layer
432: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs
433: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
434: 
435: using System;
436: using System.Collections.Generic;
437: using System.Threading.Tasks;
438: using {Project}.Domain;
439: 
440: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
441: {
442:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
443:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();
444:     Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId);
445: }
446: 
447: // Step 2: Use interface in Application layer
448: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs
449: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Queries;
450: 
451: using System.Collections.Generic;
452: using System.Threading;
453: using System.Threading.Tasks;
454: using AutoMapper;
455: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;  // ✅ Same layer
456: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
457: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
458: using MediatR;
459: 
460: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
461: {
462:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;  // ✅ Abstraction
463:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
464: 
465:     public Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler(I{Entity}Repository {entity}Repository, IMapper mapper)
466:     {
467:         _{entity}Repository = {entity}Repository;
468:         _mapper = mapper;
469:     }
470: 
471:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
472:     {
473:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // ✅ Returns List<{Entity}>
474:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});  // ✅ Maps to DTOs
475:     }
476: }
477: 
478: // Step 3: Implement repository in Persistence layer
479: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
480: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
481: 
482: using System;
483: using System.Collections.Generic;
484: using System.Linq;
485: using System.Threading.Tasks;
486: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;  // ✅ Implements interface
487: using {Project}.Domain;
488: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
489: 
490: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
491: {
492:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
493: 
494:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext)
495:     {
496:         _dbContext = dbContext;
497:     }
498: 
499:     public async Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id)
500:     {
501:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
502:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
503:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
504:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
505:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity3})
506:                 .ThenInclude(r => r.{NestedEntity})
507:             .Include(e => e.Status)
508:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity4})
509:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity5})
510:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity6})
511:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity7})
512:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity8})
513:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == id);
514:     }
515: 
516:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
517:     {
518:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
519:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
520:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
521:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
522:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity3})
523:                 .ThenInclude(r => r.{NestedEntity})
524:             .Include(e => e.Status)
525:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity4})
526:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity5})
527:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity6})
528:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity7})
529:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity8})
530:             .ToListAsync();
531:     }
532: 
533:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId)
534:     {
535:         {IdType} userGuid;
536:         var isGuid = {IdType}.TryParse(userId, out userGuid);
537: 
538:         var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
539:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
540:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
541:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
542:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity3})
543:                 .ThenInclude(r => r.{NestedEntity})
544:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity7})
545:             .Include(e => e.Status)
546:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity4})
547:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity5})
548:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity6})
549:             .AsQueryable();
550: 
551:         if (isGuid)
552:         {
553:             query = query.Where(e =>
554:                 _dbContext.Users.Any(u => u.Id == userGuid && u.{RelatedEntity3}Id == e.{RelatedEntity3}Id) ||
555:                 _dbContext.{ParentEntity}Members.Any(pm =>
556:                     pm.UserId == userGuid &&
557:                     _dbContext.{ParentEntities}.Any(p => p.Id == pm.{ParentEntity}Id && p.{RelatedEntity3}Id == e.{RelatedEntity3}Id)));
558:         }
559: 
560:         return await query.ToListAsync();
561:     }
562: }
563: 
564: // Step 4: Register in API (Composition Root)
565: // File: {Project}.API/Program.cs
566: builder.Services.AddScoped<I{Entity}Repository, {Entity}Repository>();
567: ```
568: 
569: **Benefits**:
570: - ✅ Application doesn't know about EF Core
571: - ✅ Can mock repository for unit tests
572: - ✅ Complex queries are encapsulated in Persistence
573: - ✅ Can optimize queries without changing Application
574:
