## File: .claude/skills/cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: cqrs-mediatr-guidelines
  3: description: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) patterns with MediatR for .NET Clean Architecture projects. Covers commands, queries, handlers, validation, and pipeline behaviors.
  4: type: domain
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # CQRS + MediatR Guidelines
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic CQRS Guidelines**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: Provides best practices for implementing **CQRS** (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) using **MediatR** in .NET Clean Architecture projects. Ensures consistent, testable, and maintainable application logic.
 18: 
 19: ## When This Skill Activates
 20: 
 21: **Triggered by**:
 22: - Keywords: "command", "query", "handler", "mediatr", "cqrs", "validation", "validator"
 23: - Intent patterns: "create feature", "add endpoint", "implement use case"
 24: - File patterns: `**/*Command.cs`, `**/*Query.cs`, `**/*Handler.cs`, `**/*Validator.cs`
 25: - Content patterns: `IRequest`, `IRequestHandler`, `AbstractValidator`
 26: 
 27: ## CQRS Pattern Overview
 28: 
 29: ```mermaid
 30: graph TD
 31:     subgraph Presentation Layer
 32:         Controller -- "Sends IRequest" --> MediatR[MediatR]
 33:     end
 34: 
 35:     subgraph Application Layer
 36:         MediatR --> Handler[Handler]
 37:         Handler --> Validator[Validator]
 38:         Handler --> Mapper[AutoMapper]
 39:         Handler --> Repository[Repository]
 40:         Repository --> Domain[Domain Entities]
 41:     end
 42: 
 43:     subgraph Infrastructure Layer
 44:         Repository --> DB[Database]
 45:     end
 46: 
 47:     style MediatR fill:#fbe5c5,stroke:#333
 48:     style Handler fill:#e5c5fb,stroke:#333
 49:     style Validator fill:#e5fbe5,stroke:#333
 50:     style Mapper fill:#fbe5e5,stroke:#333
 51:     style Repository fill:#c5fbe5,stroke:#333
 52:     style Domain fill:#c5fbc5,stroke:#333
 53:     style DB fill:#c5c5fb,stroke:#333
 54: ```
 55: 
 56: ## Key Principles
 57: 
 58: 1.  **Separation**: Commands (write operations) and Queries (read operations) are distinct.
 59: 2.  **Single Responsibility**: Each handler processes one specific request (command or query).
 60: 3.  **Class Requests**: Commands and Queries are defined as classes.
 61: 4.  **Validation**: FluentValidation is used at the Application boundary for input validation.
 62: 5.  **Thin Controllers**: Controllers should be minimal, primarily responsible for receiving HTTP requests, sending them to MediatR, and returning HTTP responses.
 63: 6.  **CancellationToken**: Always pass `CancellationToken` to all asynchronous methods to enable cancellation.
 64: 7.  **Repository Returns Entities**: Repositories must return domain entities, and handlers are responsible for mapping these entities to DTOs.
 65: 8.  **Validators Use Manual Instantiation**: Validators are instantiated manually within handlers, **NOT** injected via Dependency Injection.
 66: 
 67: ## Resources
 68: 
 69: *For more detailed examples, refer to the `resources/` folder within this skill.*
 70: 
 71: | Resource | Description |
 72: |----------|-------------|
 73: | [command-patterns.md](resources/command-patterns.md) | Command structure, naming, handlers |
 74: | [query-patterns.md](resources/query-patterns.md) | Query structure, pagination, projections |
 75: | [handler-patterns.md](resources/handler-patterns.md) | Handler implementation, DI, error handling |
 76: | [validation-integration.md](resources/validation-integration.md) | FluentValidation patterns and manual integration |
 77: | [complete-examples.md](resources/complete-examples.md) | End-to-end feature examples for CQRS |
 78: 
 79: ## Quick Reference
 80: 
 81: ### 1. Command (Write Operation)
 82: 
 83: Commands represent actions that modify the application's state.
 84: 
 85: ```csharp
 86: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Commands/Create{Entity}Command.cs
 87: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
 88: 
 89: using MediatR;
 90: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
 91: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
 92: 
 93: public class Create{Entity}Command : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
 94: {
 95:     public Create{Entity}Dto {Entity}Dto { get; set; } = null!; // Command wraps a DTO
 96: }
 97: ```
 98: *For more details, see [command-patterns.md](resources/command-patterns.md).*
 99: 
100: ### 2. Query (Read Operation)
101: 
102: Queries represent requests for data and should not alter the application's state.
103: 
104: ```csharp
105: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequest.cs
106: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
107: 
108: using System.Collections.Generic;
109: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
110: using MediatR;
111: 
112: public class Get{Entity}ListRequest : IRequest<List<{Entity}ListDto>>
113: {
114:     // Can include filter properties if needed
115: }
116: ```
117: *For more details, see [query-patterns.md](resources/query-patterns.md).*
118: 
119: ### 3. Handler (Processing Logic)
120: 
121: Handlers contain the business logic to execute a command or query.
122: 
123: ```csharp
124: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
125: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
126: 
127: using System.Linq;
128: using System.Threading;
129: using System.Threading.Tasks;
130: using AutoMapper;
131: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
132: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
133: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
134: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
135: using MediatR;
136: 
137: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
138: {
139:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
140:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
141:     // ... other dependencies needed for validation or business logic
142: 
143:     public Create{Entity}CommandHandler(I{Entity}Repository {entity}Repository, IMapper mapper /* ... */)
144:     {
145:         _{entity}Repository = {entity}Repository;
146:         _mapper = mapper;
147:     }
148: 
149:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(Create{Entity}Command request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
150:     {
151:         var response = new BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>();
152: 
153:         // ✅ CRITICAL: Manual validator instantiation with dependencies
154:         var validator = new Create{Entity}DtoValidator(/* repositories */);
155:         var validationResult = await validator.ValidateAsync(request.{Entity}Dto, cancellationToken);
156: 
157:         if (!validationResult.IsValid)
158:         {
159:             response.Success = false;
160:             response.Message = "{Entity} creation failed.";
161:             response.Errors = validationResult.Errors.Select(e => e.ErrorMessage).ToList();
162:             return response;
163:         }
164: 
165:         var {entity} = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
166:         {entity}.ViewCount = 0; // Set properties not coming from DTO
167:         {entity} = await _{entity}Repository.Create({entity});
168: 
169:         response.Success = true;
170:         response.Id = {entity}.Id;
171:         response.Message = "{Entity} created successfully.";
172:         return response;
173:     }
174: }
175: ```
176: *For more details, see [handler-patterns.md](resources/handler-patterns.md).*
177: 
178: ### 4. Validation (Manual Integration)
179: 
180: FluentValidation is used for input validation, with validators instantiated manually within handlers.
181: 
182: ```csharp
183: // File: {Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/Validators/Create{Entity}DtoValidator.cs
184: namespace {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
185: 
186: using FluentValidation;
187: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
188: 
189: public class Create{Entity}DtoValidator : AbstractValidator<Create{Entity}Dto>
190: {
191:     public Create{Entity}DtoValidator(I{RelatedEntity1}Repository {relatedEntity1}Repository /* ... */)
192:     {
193:         // ... inject repositories needed for FK validation
194: 
195:         RuleFor(x => x.Title)
196:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("Title is required")
197:             .MaximumLength(200);
198: 
199:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity1}Id)
200:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("{RelatedEntity1} is required")
201:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) => await {relatedEntity1}Repository.Exists(id))
202:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity1} not found");
203:     }
204: }
205: ```
206: *For more details, see [validation-integration.md](resources/validation-integration.md).*
207: 
208: ## Do's
209: 
210: -   ✅ **DO** separate Commands (write) and Queries (read).
211: -   ✅ **DO** use classes for Commands/Queries (not records).
212: -   ✅ **DO** pass `CancellationToken` to all asynchronous methods.
213: -   ✅ **DO** use repositories that return domain entities (not DTOs).
214: -   ✅ **DO** perform DTO mapping in handlers using AutoMapper.
215: -   ✅ **DO** instantiate validators manually within handlers.
216: -   ✅ **DO** keep controllers thin, delegating to MediatR.
217: -   ✅ **DO** use `BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>` for command responses (except `bool` for Delete).
218: 
219: ## Don'ts
220: 
221: -   ❌ **DON'T** return entities directly from query handlers.
222: -   ❌ **DON'T** put business logic in controllers.
223: -   ❌ **DON'T** use `IRequest` without a response type.
224: -   ❌ **DON'T** use `.Result` or `.Wait()` in asynchronous code.
225: -   ❌ **DON'T** mutate state in query handlers.
226: -   ❌ **DON'T** throw exceptions for business validation failures; return them in the `BaseCommandResponse`.
227: -   ❌ **DON'T** inject validators via Dependency Injection.
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: **Related Documentation**:
232: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture.
233: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - Dependency enforcement.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: error-tracking
  3: description: Implement error tracking and observability using Prometheus (metrics) and Loki (logs). Covers centralized exception handling, structured logging, and performance monitoring for .NET services.
  4: type: guardrail
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Error Tracking & Observability Guidelines
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic Observability Patterns for .NET**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: Guidelines for implementing **robust error tracking** and **performance monitoring** across .NET services using:
 18: - **Prometheus** - Metrics collection and monitoring
 19: - **Loki** - Centralized log aggregation
 20: - **Structured Logging** - Consistent log formatting via Serilog
 21: - **OpenTelemetry** - Distributed tracing and telemetry
 22: 
 23: ## When This Skill Activates
 24: 
 25: **Triggered by**:
 26: - Keywords: "error handling", "logging", "prometheus", "loki", "observability", "metrics", "tracing"
 27: - Intent patterns: "add error logging", "monitor performance", "track exceptions", "implement telemetry"
 28: - File patterns: `**/Program.cs`, `**/*Controller.cs`, `**/*Handler.cs`, `**/*Repository.cs`, `**/*.razor`
 29: 
 30: ## CRITICAL RULE: Do Not Swallow Exceptions!
 31: 
 32: All errors **MUST** be handled gracefully with structured logging and centralized exception handling.
 33: 
 34: ## Resources
 35: 
 36: *Detailed patterns are available in `resources/` (to be created) and [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](../../../docs/CONFIGURATION.md).*
 37: 
 38: | Resource | Description |
 39: |----------|-------------|
 40: | [api-exception-handling.md](resources/api-exception-handling.md) | Centralized API exception handling with RFC 7807 ProblemDetails |
 41: | [mediatr-logging-behavior.md](resources/mediatr-logging-behavior.md) | MediatR pipeline behavior for request/response logging |
 42: | [prometheus-metrics.md](resources/prometheus-metrics.md) | Exposing custom metrics via `/metrics` endpoint |
 43: | [loki-logging.md](resources/loki-logging.md) | Structured logging to Loki via Serilog |
 44: | [blazor-error-boundary.md](resources/blazor-error-boundary.md) | Graceful UI error handling with ErrorBoundary component |
 45: | [opentelemetry-tracing.md](resources/opentelemetry-tracing.md) | Distributed tracing with ActivitySource |
 46: 
 47: ## Quick Reference
 48: 
 49: ### 1. Centralized API Exception Handling
 50: - Use `app.UseExceptionHandler()` to catch unhandled API exceptions
 51: - Transform exceptions into RFC 7807 `ProblemDetails` format
 52: - Log exceptions with structured logging before returning response
 53: - Return appropriate HTTP status codes (400, 404, 500)
 54: 
 55: *Details: [api-exception-handling.md](resources/api-exception-handling.md)*
 56: 
 57: ### 2. MediatR Pipeline Logging
 58: - Implement `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` for centralized logging
 59: - Log request start/completion with structured data (request name, duration)
 60: - Capture and log exceptions from handlers
 61: - Attach correlation IDs and tenant context to logs
 62: 
 63: *Details: [mediatr-logging-behavior.md](resources/mediatr-logging-behavior.md)*
 64: 
 65: ### 3. Prometheus Metrics
 66: - Expose `/metrics` endpoint using `app.MapPrometheusScrapingEndpoint()`
 67: - Configure OpenTelemetry with `AddPrometheusExporter()`
 68: - Track: HTTP request durations, database query times, command/query execution
 69: - Use histograms for latency metrics (P50, P95, P99)
 70: 
 71: *Configuration: [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](../../../docs/CONFIGURATION.md) Prometheus section*
 72: 
 73: ### 4. Loki Centralized Logging
 74: - Configure Serilog with `GrafanaLoki` sink
 75: - Add structured labels: `app`, `environment`, `tenant`
 76: - Include correlation IDs for request tracing
 77: - Ship logs asynchronously to avoid performance impact
 78: 
 79: *Configuration: [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](../../../docs/CONFIGURATION.md) Loki section*
 80: 
 81: ### 5. Blazor Error Boundary
 82: - Wrap components in `<ErrorBoundary>` to catch UI exceptions
 83: - Provide `<ErrorContent>` fallback UI for graceful degradation
 84: - Log caught exceptions with component context
 85: - Display user-friendly error messages
 86: 
 87: *Implementation: [blazor-error-boundary.md](resources/blazor-error-boundary.md)*
 88: 
 89: ### 6. OpenTelemetry Tracing
 90: - Use `ActivitySource` for distributed tracing
 91: - Create spans for database operations, external API calls, long-running processes
 92: - Attach custom tags (entity ID, operation type)
 93: - Integrate with Prometheus for performance monitoring
 94: 
 95: *Details: [opentelemetry-tracing.md](resources/opentelemetry-tracing.md)*
 96: 
 97: ## Key Principles
 98: 
 99: *   **No Uncaught Exceptions**: All exceptions must be caught and logged with structured context
100: *   **Structured Logging**: Use Serilog with `ILogger<T>` for consistent log formatting
101: *   **Contextual Information**: Include user ID, tenant ID, correlation IDs, and request data in logs
102: *   **Metrics Over Logs**: Use Prometheus metrics for performance tracking; logs for debugging
103: *   **RFC 7807 Compliance**: API error responses must use `ProblemDetails` format
104: *   **Label-Based Filtering**: Add labels to Loki logs for efficient querying (app, env, tenant)
105: *   **Performance Monitoring**: Track P50/P95/P99 latencies for critical operations
106: 
107: ---
108: 
109: **Related Skills**:
110: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - For proper error handling layer placement.
111: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - For error handling patterns within MediatR handlers.
112: - [`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`](../dotnet-efcore-guidelines/SKILL.md) - For database error handling and performance considerations.
113: - [`blazor-ui-conventions`](../blazor-ui-conventions/SKILL.md) - For UI error handling patterns.
````

````markdown
   1: # API Architecture
   2: 
   3: > **Project-Agnostic REST API Design Patterns**
   4: >
   5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
   6: 
   7: **Last Updated**: January 2026
   8: 
   9: ---
  10: 
  11: ## Placeholder Substitutions
  12: 
  13: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
  14: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
  15: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
  16: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `Explore.API` |
  17: | `{Project}.Blazor` | Blazor Server project | `Explore.Blazor` |
  18: | `{DbContext}` | EF Core DbContext class | `ExploreDbContext` |
  19: | `{Entity}` | Your main entity (singular) | `Event` |
  20: | `{Entities}` | Your main entity (plural) | `Events` |
  21: | `{entity}` | camelCase entity | `event` |
  22: | `{IdType}` | Primary key type | `Guid` |
  23: 
  24: ---
  25: 
  26: ## Table of Contents
  27: 
  28: 1. [Overview](#1-overview)
  29: 2. [Base URL & Versioning](#2-base-url--versioning)
  30: 3. [Controller Conventions](#3-controller-conventions)
  31: 4. [Authentication & Authorization](#4-authentication--authorization)
  32: 5. [Request/Response Patterns](#5-requestresponse-patterns)
  33: 6. [Pagination](#6-pagination)
  34: 7. [Error Handling](#7-error-handling)
  35: 8. [OpenAPI Documentation](#8-openapi-documentation)
  36: 9. [Endpoint Reference](#9-endpoint-reference)
  37: 10. [Multi-Tenancy](#10-multi-tenancy)
  38: 
  39: ---
  40: 
  41: ## 1. Overview
  42: 
  43: The `{Project}.API` is a stateless REST API built on ASP.NET Core, following Clean Architecture and CQRS patterns.
  44: 
  45: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
  46: 
  47: - **API Project**: `Explore.API`
  48: - **Technology**: ASP.NET Core 10.0
  49: - **Architecture**: Clean Architecture + CQRS + MediatR
  50: 
  51: ### Key Characteristics
  52: 
  53: | Aspect | Implementation |
  54: |--------|----------------|
  55: | Framework | ASP.NET Core 10.0 |
  56: | Architecture | Clean Architecture + CQRS |
  57: | Authentication | JWT Bearer (Keycloak) |
  58: | Documentation | OpenAPI 3.0 (Scalar + Swagger) |
  59: | Versioning | URL path (`/api/v1/`) |
  60: | Serialization | System.Text.Json |
  61: 
  62: ### Request Flow
  63: 
  64: ```
  65: HTTP Request → Controller → MediatR → Handler → Repository → Entity → DTO → Response
  66: ```
  67: 
  68: ---
  69: 
  70: ## 2. Base URL & Versioning
  71: 
  72: ### Development URLs
  73: 
  74: | Service | URL |
  75: |---------|-----|
  76: | API | `https://localhost:7001` |
  77: | Scalar Docs | `https://localhost:7001/scalar/v1` |
  78: | Swagger UI | `https://localhost:7001/swagger` |
  79: | OpenAPI JSON | `https://localhost:7001/openapi/v1.json` |
  80: 
  81: ### URL Structure
  82: 
  83: **Generic Pattern:**
  84: ```
  85: /api/v1/{resource}
  86: /api/v1/{resource}/{id}
  87: /api/v1/{resource}/{id}/{subresource}
  88: ```
  89: 
  90: **Generic Examples:**
  91: - `GET /api/v1/{entity}` - List entities
  92: - `GET /api/v1/{entity}/{id}` - Get entity details
  93: - `GET /api/v1/{childEntity}/by-{parentEntity}/{parentId}` - Get children
  94: - `POST /api/v1/{entity}` - Create entity
  95: 
  96: ### Implementation Examples: ISLAMU Event
  97: - `GET /api/v1/event` - List events
  98: - `GET /api/v1/event/{id}` - Get event details
  99: - `GET /api/v1/eventsession/by-event/{eventId}` - Get sessions for event
 100: - `POST /api/v1/organization` - Create organization
 101: 
 102: ---
 103: 
 104: ## 3. Controller Conventions
 105: 
 106: ### Standard Controller Structure
 107: 
 108: **Generic Template:**
 109: 
 110: ```csharp
 111: [Route("api/v1/[controller]")]
 112: [ApiController]
 113: public class {Entity}Controller : ControllerBase
 114: {
 115:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
 116:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
 117:     private readonly ILogger<{Entity}Controller> _logger;
 118: 
 119:     public {Entity}Controller(
 120:         IMediator mediator,
 121:         IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor,
 122:         ILogger<{Entity}Controller> logger)
 123:     {
 124:         _mediator = mediator;
 125:         _httpContextAccessor = httpContextAccessor;
 126:         _logger = logger;
 127:     }
 128: }
 129: ```
 130: 
 131: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 132: 
 133: ```csharp
 134: [Route("api/v1/[controller]")]
 135: [ApiController]
 136: public class EventController : ControllerBase
 137: {
 138:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
 139:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
 140:     private readonly ILogger<EventController> _logger;
 141: 
 142:     public EventController(
 143:         IMediator mediator,
 144:         IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor,
 145:         ILogger<EventController> logger)
 146:     {
 147:         _mediator = mediator;
 148:         _httpContextAccessor = httpContextAccessor;
 149:         _logger = logger;
 150:     }
 151: }
 152: ```
 153: 
 154: ### CRUD Operations
 155: 
 156: | Operation | HTTP Method | Route | Auth | Returns |
 157: |-----------|-------------|-------|------|---------|
 158: | List | `GET` | `/` | `[AllowAnonymous]` | `PaginatedResult<{Entity}ListDto>` |
 159: | Get | `GET` | `/{id}` | `[AllowAnonymous]` | `{Entity}Dto` |
 160: | Create | `POST` | `/` | `[Authorize]` | `BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>` |
 161: | Update | `PUT` | `/{id}` | `[Authorize]` | `BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>` |
 162: | Delete | `DELETE` | `/{id}` | `[Authorize]` | `NoContent` or `NotFound` |
 163: 
 164: ### Thin Controllers
 165: 
 166: Controllers should be thin - they only:
 167: 1. Extract data from HTTP request
 168: 2. Send command/query to MediatR
 169: 3. Return appropriate HTTP response
 170: 
 171: **Generic Template:**
 172: 
 173: ```csharp
 174: [HttpPost]
 175: [Authorize]
 176: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto dto)
 177: {
 178:     var command = new Create{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = dto };
 179:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
 180: 
 181:     if (!response.Success)
 182:     {
 183:         return BadRequest(response);
 184:     }
 185: 
 186:     return Ok(response);
 187: }
 188: ```
 189: 
 190: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 191: 
 192: ```csharp
 193: [HttpPost]
 194: [Authorize]
 195: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create([FromBody] CreateEventDto dto)
 196: {
 197:     var command = new CreateEventCommand { EventDto = dto };
 198:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
 199: 
 200:     if (!response.Success)
 201:     {
 202:         return BadRequest(response);
 203:     }
 204: 
 205:     return Ok(response);
 206: }
 207: ```
 208: 
 209: ---
 210: 
 211: ## 4. Authentication & Authorization
 212: 
 213: ### JWT Bearer Authentication
 214: 
 215: The API uses JWT Bearer tokens issued by Keycloak:
 216: 
 217: ```csharp
 218: // In Program.cs
 219: builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
 220:     .AddJwtBearer(options =>
 221:     {
 222:         options.Authority = builder.Configuration["Keycloak:Authority"];
 223:         options.Audience = builder.Configuration["Keycloak:Audience"];
 224:         options.RequireHttpsMetadata = false; // Dev only
 225:     });
 226: ```
 227: 
 228: ### Authorization Patterns
 229: 
 230: **Read Operations** - Public access:
 231: ```csharp
 232: [HttpGet]
 233: [AllowAnonymous]
 234: [EndpointSummary("Get all {Entities}")]
 235: public async Task<ActionResult<PaginatedResult<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll(...)
 236: ```
 237: 
 238: **Write Operations** - Authenticated users:
 239: ```csharp
 240: [HttpPost]
 241: [Authorize]
 242: [EndpointSummary("Create a new {Entity}")]
 243: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create(...)
 244: ```
 245: 
 246: ### User ID Extraction
 247: 
 248: Use the fallback pattern for extracting user ID from JWT claims:
 249: 
 250: ```csharp
 251: var userId = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
 252:     ?? _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier")?.Value
 253:     ?? _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sid")?.Value;
 254: 
 255: if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
 256: {
 257:     return Unauthorized(new { error = "User ID not found in token" });
 258: }
 259: ```
 260: 
 261: ---
 262: 
 263: ## 5. Request/Response Patterns
 264: 
 265: ### HATEOAS / HAL+JSON Implementation
 266: 
 267: The API implements **HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State)** using the HAL+JSON format. This allows clients to discover available actions dynamically based on their permissions and the resource state.
 268: 
 269: #### Core Components
 270: 
 271: 1.  **`IResourceAssembler<TDto, TListDto>`**:
 272:     The central service that converts DTOs into `HalResource<T>` or `HalCollectionResource<T>`.
 273:     - Automatically handles `Prefer: return=minimal` header to strip links.
 274:     - Evaluates authorization policies before adding links.
 275:     - Uses `ResourceAssemblerBase` for shared logic.
 276: 
 277: 2.  **`ILinkPolicy<T>`**:
 278:     Defines *which* links apply to a specific resource.
 279:     - `GetLinks(dto, user)`: Returns links for a single resource.
 280:     - `GetCollectionLinks(user)`: Returns links for the collection root (e.g., "create").
 281: 
 282: 3.  **`IHateoasAuthorizationEvaluator`**:
 283:     Integrates with **Cerbos** to filter links. If a user lacks permission for an action (e.g., `update`), the corresponding link is automatically omitted from the response.
 284: 
 285: #### Defining Links
 286: 
 287: Links are defined using a fluent API in Policy classes:
 288: 
 289: ```csharp
 290: public class EventLinkPolicy : ILinkPolicy<EventDto>
 291: {
 292:     public IEnumerable<LinkDefinition> GetLinks(EventDto dto, ClaimsPrincipal user)
 293:     {
 294:         // Self link (always visible)
 295:         yield return new LinkDefinition(
 296:             rel: LinkRelations.Self,
 297:             routeName: RouteNames.GetEvent,
 298:             routeValues: new { id = dto.Id });
 299: 
 300:         // Update link (only if user has permission)
 301:         yield return new LinkDefinition(
 302:             rel: LinkRelations.Update,
 303:             routeName: RouteNames.UpdateEvent,
 304:             routeValues: new { id = dto.Id })
 305:             .RequirePermission(CerbosPermissionAction.Update, dto); // Checks Cerbos policy
 306:     }
 307: }
 308: ```
 309: 
 310: #### Response Wrapper Types
 311: 
 312: **For Single Resources:**
 313: ```csharp
 314: public class HalResource<T>
 315: {
 316:     public T Data { get; set; }  // The actual DTO payload
 317:     public Dictionary<string, HalLink> _links { get; set; }  // Hypermedia links
 318: }
 319: ```
 320: 
 321: **For Collections:**
 322: ```csharp
 323: public class HalCollectionResource<T>
 324: {
 325:     public Dictionary<string, object> _embedded { get; set; }  // Contains "items" array
 326:     public Dictionary<string, HalLink> _links { get; set; }   // Collection navigation links
 327:     public int TotalCount { get; set; }
 328:     public int PageNumber { get; set; }
 329:     public int PageSize { get; set; }
 330:     public int TotalPages { get; set; }
 331: }
 332: ```
 333: 
 334: #### Example Response
 335: 
 336: **Request:**
 337: ```http
 338: GET /api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
 339: Accept: application/hal+json
 340: ```
 341: 
 342: **Response:**
 343: ```json
 344: {
 345:   "data": {
 346:     "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 347:     "title": "Community Iftar 2026",
 348:     "status": "Published"
 349:   },
 350:   "_links": {
 351:     "self": {
 352:       "href": "/api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 353:       "method": "GET"
 354:     },
 355:     "update": {
 356:       "href": "/api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 357:       "method": "PUT"
 358:     }
 359:   }
 360: }
 361: ```
 362: 
 363: #### Optimization: Minimal Response
 364: 
 365: Clients can request payloads without hypermedia overhead using the standard `Prefer` header. This is useful for mobile apps or internal services that don't need discovery.
 366: 
 367: **Request:**
 368: ```http
 369: GET /api/v1/events/123...
 370: Prefer: return=minimal
 371: ```
 372: 
 373: **Response (Pure JSON):**
 374: ```json
 375: {
 376:   "data": {
 377:     "id": "123...",
 378:     "title": "Community Iftar 2026"
 379:   }
 380: }
 381: ```
 382: 
 383: ### Command Response
 384: 
 385: 
 386: All write operations return `BaseCommandResponse<T>`:
 387: 
 388: ```csharp
 389: public class BaseCommandResponse<T>
 390: {
 391:     public bool Success { get; set; }
 392:     public string Message { get; set; } = string.Empty;
 393:     public T? Id { get; set; }
 394:     public List<string> Errors { get; set; } = new();
 395: }
 396: ```
 397: 
 398: **Success Response**:
 399: ```json
 400: {
 401:     "success": true,
 402:     "message": "{Entity} created successfully.",
 403:     "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
 404:     "errors": []
 405: }
 406: ```
 407: 
 408: **Failure Response**:
 409: ```json
 410: {
 411:     "success": false,
 412:     "message": "{Entity} creation failed.",
 413:     "id": null,
 414:     "errors": [
 415:         "Title is required",
 416:         "{RelatedEntity}Id not found"
 417:     ]
 418: }
 419: ```
 420: 
 421: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 422: 
 423: **Success Response**:
 424: ```json
 425: {
 426:     "success": true,
 427:     "message": "Event created successfully.",
 428:     "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
 429:     "errors": []
 430: }
 431: ```
 432: 
 433: **Failure Response**:
 434: ```json
 435: {
 436:     "success": false,
 437:     "message": "Event creation failed.",
 438:     "id": null,
 439:     "errors": [
 440:         "Title is required",
 441:         "EventTypeId not found"
 442:     ]
 443: }
 444: ```
 445: 
 446: ### Query Response
 447: 
 448: Read operations return DTOs directly or wrapped in `PaginatedResult<T>`:
 449: 
 450: **Generic Pattern:**
 451: 
 452: ```csharp
 453: // Single entity
 454: public async Task<ActionResult<{Entity}Dto>> GetById({IdType} id)
 455: 
 456: // List with pagination
 457: public async Task<ActionResult<PaginatedResult<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll(...)
 458: ```
 459: 
 460: ### HATEOAS / HAL+JSON Response Format
 461: 
 462: All API responses are wrapped in **HAL (Hypertext Application Language)** format, providing hypermedia links for discoverability and navigation.
 463: 
 464: #### Response Wrapper Types
 465: 
 466: **For Single Resources:**
 467: ```csharp
 468: public class HalResource<T>
 469: {
 470:     public T Data { get; set; }  // The actual DTO payload
 471:     public Dictionary<string, HalLink> _links { get; set; }  // Hypermedia links
 472: }
 473: 
 474: public class HalLink
 475: {
 476:     public string Href { get; set; }       // URL
 477:     public string? Method { get; set; }    // HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
 478:     public string? Rel { get; set; }       // Link relation type
 479: }
 480: ```
 481: 
 482: **For Collections:**
 483: ```csharp
 484: public class HalCollectionResource<T>
 485: {
 486:     public Dictionary<string, object> _embedded { get; set; }  // Contains "items" array
 487:     public Dictionary<string, HalLink> _links { get; set; }   // Collection navigation links
 488:     public int TotalCount { get; set; }
 489:     public int PageNumber { get; set; }
 490:     public int PageSize { get; set; }
 491:     public int TotalPages { get; set; }
 492: }
 493: ```
 494: 
 495: #### Example Single Resource Response
 496: 
 497: **Request:**
 498: ```http
 499: GET /api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
 500: Accept: application/hal+json
 501: ```
 502: 
 503: **Response:**
 504: ```json
 505: {
 506:   "data": {
 507:     "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 508:     "title": "Community Iftar 2026",
 509:     "startDate": "2026-03-15T18:00:00Z",
 510:     "location": "Amsterdam Mosque",
 511:     "status": "Published"
 512:   },
 513:   "_links": {
 514:     "self": {
 515:       "href": "/api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 516:       "method": "GET"
 517:     },
 518:     "update": {
 519:       "href": "/api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 520:       "method": "PUT"
 521:     },
 522:     "delete": {
 523:       "href": "/api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 524:       "method": "DELETE"
 525:     },
 526:     "sessions": {
 527:       "href": "/api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000/sessions",
 528:       "method": "GET"
 529:     }
 530:   }
 531: }
 532: ```
 533: 
 534: #### Example Collection Response
 535: 
 536: **Request:**
 537: ```http
 538: GET /api/v1/events?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10
 539: Accept: application/hal+json
 540: ```
 541: 
 542: **Response:**
 543: ```json
 544: {
 545:   "_embedded": {
 546:     "items": [
 547:       {
 548:         "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 549:         "title": "Community Iftar 2026",
 550:         "startDate": "2026-03-15T18:00:00Z"
 551:       },
 552:       {
 553:         "id": "987e6543-e21c-45d6-b789-123456789abc",
 554:         "title": "Tech Workshop: Clean Architecture",
 555:         "startDate": "2026-04-01T14:00:00Z"
 556:       }
 557:     ]
 558:   },
 559:   "_links": {
 560:     "self": {
 561:       "href": "/api/v1/events?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10",
 562:       "method": "GET"
 563:     },
 564:     "first": {
 565:       "href": "/api/v1/events?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10",
 566:       "method": "GET"
 567:     },
 568:     "next": {
 569:       "href": "/api/v1/events?pageNumber=2&pageSize=10",
 570:       "method": "GET"
 571:     },
 572:     "last": {
 573:       "href": "/api/v1/events?pageNumber=5&pageSize=10",
 574:       "method": "GET"
 575:     }
 576:   },
 577:   "totalCount": 47,
 578:   "pageNumber": 1,
 579:   "pageSize": 10,
 580:   "totalPages": 5
 581: }
 582: ```
 583: 
 584: #### Prefer Header Support
 585: 
 586: Clients can request minimal responses without hypermedia links using the `Prefer` header:
 587: 
 588: **Request:**
 589: ```http
 590: GET /api/v1/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
 591: Prefer: return=minimal
 592: ```
 593: 
 594: **Response (without _links):**
 595: ```json
 596: {
 597:   "data": {
 598:     "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 599:     "title": "Community Iftar 2026",
 600:     "startDate": "2026-03-15T18:00:00Z",
 601:     "location": "Amsterdam Mosque",
 602:     "status": "Published"
 603:   }
 604: }
 605: ```
 606: 
 607: #### Resource Assembler Pattern
 608: 
 609: Controllers use `IResourceAssembler<TDto, TListDto>` to build HAL responses:
 610: 
 611: **Generic Pattern:**
 612: ```csharp
 613: public class {Entity}Controller : ControllerBase
 614: {
 615:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
 616:     private readonly IResourceAssembler<{Entity}Dto, {Entity}ListDto> _resourceAssembler;
 617: 
 618:     [HttpGet("{id}")]
 619:     public async Task<ActionResult<HalResource<{Entity}Dto>>> GetById({IdType} id)
 620:     {
 621:         var dto = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}DetailsRequest { Id = id });
 622:         if (dto == null) return NotFound();
 623: 
 624:         var resource = _resourceAssembler.ToResource(dto, RouteNames.Get{Entity});
 625:         return Ok(resource);
 626:     }
 627: 
 628:     [HttpGet]
 629:     public async Task<ActionResult<HalCollectionResource<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll(...)
 630:     {
 631:         var dtos = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}ListRequest { ... });
 632:         var resource = _resourceAssembler.ToCollectionResource(
 633:             dtos,
 634:             RouteNames.Get{Entities},
 635:             totalCount,
 636:             pageNumber,
 637:             pageSize);
 638:         return Ok(resource);
 639:     }
 640: }
 641: ```
 642: 
 643: **RouteNames Constants:**
 644: Route names are defined in `RouteNames.cs` for consistency:
 645: ```csharp
 646: public static class RouteNames
 647: {
 648:     public const string GetEvent = "GetEvent";
 649:     public const string GetEvents = "GetEvents";
 650:     public const string UpdateEvent = "UpdateEvent";
 651:     public const string DeleteEvent = "DeleteEvent";
 652:     // ...
 653: }
 654: ```
 655: 
 656: #### Benefits
 657: 
 658: - **Discoverability**: Clients can navigate the API without hardcoding URLs
 659: - **Evolvability**: Server can change URLs without breaking clients
 660: - **Self-Documenting**: Links show available actions based on current state
 661: - **Bandwidth Control**: Use `Prefer: return=minimal` to reduce payload size
 662: 
 663: **See Also**: [CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md](CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md) Section 14 for HATEOAS implementation details
 664: 
 665: ---

 667: ## 6. Pagination
 668: 
 669: ### Paginated Response Structure
 670: 
 671: ```csharp
 672: public class PaginatedResult<T>
 673: {
 674:     public ICollection<T> Items { get; set; } = new List<T>();
 675:     public int TotalCount { get; set; }
 676:     public int PageNumber { get; set; }
 677:     public int PageSize { get; set; }
 678:     public int TotalPages => (int)Math.Ceiling((double)TotalCount / PageSize);
 679:     public bool HasPreviousPage => PageNumber > 1;
 680:     public bool HasNextPage => PageNumber < TotalPages;
 681: }
 682: ```
 683: 
 684: ### Query Parameters
 685: 
 686: **Generic Pattern:**
 687: ```
 688: GET /api/v1/{entity}?pageNumber=1&pageSize=20
 689: ```
 690: 
 691: **Example (ISLAMU Event):**
 692: ```
 693: GET /api/v1/event?pageNumber=1&pageSize=20
 694: ```
 695: 
 696: | Parameter | Type | Default | Max | Description |
 697: |-----------|------|---------|-----|-------------|
 698: | `pageNumber` | int | 1 | - | Page number (1-indexed) |
 699: | `pageSize` | int | 20 | 100 | Items per page |
 700: 
 701: ### Example Response
 702: 
 703: ```json
 704: {
 705:     "items": [
 706:         { "id": "...", "title": "Event 1", ... },
 707:         { "id": "...", "title": "Event 2", ... }
 708:     ],
 709:     "totalCount": 150,
 710:     "pageNumber": 1,
 711:     "pageSize": 20,
 712:     "totalPages": 8,
 713:     "hasPreviousPage": false,
 714:     "hasNextPage": true
 715: }
 716: ```
 717:

 719: 
 720: ## 7. Error Handling
 721: 
 722: ### Standardization
 723: 
 724: The API follows **RFC 7807 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs)** for all unhandled exceptions, while using structured `BaseCommandResponse` for domain logic failures.
 725: 
 726: ### 7.1. Global Exception Handler
 727: 
 728: Any unhandled exception (System.Exception) is caught by the global `ExceptionHandler` middleware and converted into a standardized JSON response.
 729: 
 730: **Response Format (ProblemDetails):**
 731: ```json
 732: {
 733:   "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc9110#section-15.6.1",
 734:   "title": "An error occurred while processing your request.",
 735:   "status": 500,
 736:   "detail": "Database connection timeout",
 737:   "instance": "/api/v1/events"
 738: }
 739: ```
 740: 
 741: ### 7.2. Domain Logic Errors (Command Response)
 742: 
 743: For expected business rule violations (e.g., validation failures, logic conflicts), endpoints return a `200 OK` or `400 Bad Request` with a structured `BaseCommandResponse`.
 744: 
 745: **Response Format:**
 746: ```json
 747: {
 748:     "success": false,
 749:     "message": "Validation failed",
 750:     "id": null,
 751:     "errors": [
 752:         "Event date cannot be in the past.",
 753:         "Title is required."
 754:     ]
 755: }
 756: ```
 757: 
 758: ### 7.3. HTTP Status Codes
 759: 
 760: | Code | Meaning | When Used |
 761: |------|---------|-----------|
 762: | `200 OK` | Success | GET, PUT, POST success |
 763: | `201 Created` | Resource created | POST (alternative) |
 764: | `204 No Content` | Success, no body | DELETE success |
 765: | `400 Bad Request` | Validation failed | Business rule violation |
 766: | `401 Unauthorized` | Not authenticated | Missing/invalid token |
 767: | `403 Forbidden` | Not authorized | Insufficient permissions (Cerbos denial) |
 768: | `404 Not Found` | Resource not found | Invalid ID |
 769: | `500 Internal Error` | Server error | Unexpected exception (Unhandled) |
 770: 
 771: ### 7.4. Exception Handling Pattern in Controllers
 772: 
 773: Controllers should use `try-catch` blocks only when specific recovery or logging context is needed. Otherwise, let the global handler manage 500s.
 774: 
 775: **Recommended Pattern:**
 776: 
 777: ```csharp
 778: [HttpDelete("{id}")]
 779: [Authorize]
 780: public async Task<ActionResult> Delete(Guid id)
 781: {
 782:     try
 783:     {
 784:         // ... logic ...
 785:     }
 786:     catch (Exception ex)
 787:     {
 788:         // Only catch if you need to add context before re-throwing
 789:         // or if you want to return a specific status code manually
 790:         _logger.LogError(ex, "Error deleting event {EventId}", id);
 791:         return StatusCode(500, new { error = "An unexpected error occurred." });
 792:     }
 793: }
 794: ```
 795:

 798: ## 8. OpenAPI Documentation
 799: 
 800: ### Required Attributes
 801: 
 802: All controller actions must include:
 803: 
 804: **Generic Template:**
 805: 
 806: ```csharp
 807: [HttpGet("{id}")]
 808: [EndpointSummary("Get {Entity} Details")]
 809: [EndpointDescription("Returns detailed information about a specific {entity} including related data.")]
 810: [AllowAnonymous]
 811: [ProducesResponseType(typeof({Entity}Dto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 812: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
 813: public async Task<ActionResult<{Entity}Dto>> GetById({IdType} id)
 814: ```
 815: 
 816: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 817: 
 818: ```csharp
 819: [HttpGet("{id}")]
 820: [EndpointSummary("Get Event Details")]
 821: [EndpointDescription("Returns detailed information about a specific event including sessions.")]
 822: [AllowAnonymous]
 823: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(EventDto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 824: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
 825: public async Task<ActionResult<EventDto>> GetById(Guid id)
 826: ```
 827: 
 828: ### Attribute Guidelines
 829: 
 830: | Attribute | Required | Purpose |
 831: |-----------|----------|---------|
 832: | `[EndpointSummary]` | Yes | Short title in API docs |
 833: | `[EndpointDescription]` | Yes | Detailed description |
 834: | `[ProducesResponseType]` | Yes | Document response types |
 835: | `[Consumes]` | For POST/PUT | Request content type |
 836: 
 837: ### Example with Full Documentation
 838: 
 839: **Generic Template:**
 840: 
 841: ```csharp
 842: [HttpPost]
 843: [EndpointSummary("Create a new {Entity}")]
 844: [EndpointDescription("Creates a new {entity} under the specified {relatedEntity}. User must have appropriate permissions.")]
 845: [Authorize]
 846: [Consumes("application/json")]
 847: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 848: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>), StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
 849: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status401Unauthorized)]
 850: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto dto)
 851: ```
 852: 
 853: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 854: 
 855: ```csharp
 856: [HttpPost]
 857: [EndpointSummary("Create a new Event")]
 858: [EndpointDescription("Creates a new event under the specified organization. User must be an admin of the organization.")]
 859: [Authorize]
 860: [Consumes("application/json")]
 861: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 862: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
 863: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status401Unauthorized)]
 864: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create([FromBody] CreateEventDto dto)
 865: ```

 869: ## 9. Caching Strategy
 870: 
 871: The API implements a **Dual-Layer Caching Strategy** to maximize performance while ensuring data consistency.
 872: 
 873: ### 9.1. Layer 1: Output Caching (HTTP Level)
 874: 
 875: **Purpose**: Caches the entire HTTP response body.
 876: **Use Case**: Public, read-only endpoints (lists, details) that don't vary per user.
 877: **Mechanism**: ASP.NET Core Output Caching Middleware.
 878: 
 879: **Configuration**:
 880: Policies are defined in `Program.cs`:
 881: - `ListData`: Expire 5m, Vary by Query keys (page, size, search).
 882: - `DetailData`: Expire 10m, Vary by Route Value (id).
 883: 
 884: **Usage in Controllers**:
 885: ```csharp
 886: [HttpGet("{id}")]
 887: [AllowAnonymous]
 888: [OutputCache(PolicyName = "DetailData")]
 889: public async Task<ActionResult> GetById(Guid id) { ... }
 890: ```
 891: 
 892: ### 9.2. Layer 2: Hybrid Caching (Application Level)
 893: 
 894: **Purpose**: Caches domain entities or calculation results within the application logic.
 895: **Use Case**:
 896: - Data needed by multiple handlers.
 897: - Data that is expensive to compute/fetch but used in authenticated endpoints (where OutputCache isn't suitable).
 898: - Scenarios requiring **stampede protection**.
 899: **Mechanism**: .NET 9+ `HybridCache` (L1 In-Memory + L2 Redis).
 900: 
 901: **Usage in Handlers (Query Side)**:
 902: Use `GetOrCreateAsync` to fetch-or-cache:
 903: 
 904: ```csharp
 905: public async Task<EventDto> Handle(GetEventDetailsRequest request, CancellationToken ct)
 906: {
 907:     var cacheKey = $"event:{request.Id}";
 908:     
 909:     return await _hybridCache.GetOrCreateAsync(
 910:         cacheKey,
 911:         async cancel => await _repository.GetByIdAsync(request.Id, cancel),
 912:         options: new HybridCacheEntryOptions { Expiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) },
 913:         cancellationToken: ct
 914:     );
 915: }
 916: ```
 917: 
 918: **Usage in Handlers (Command Side)**:
 919: Explicitly invalidate cache after updates:
 920: 
 921: ```csharp
 922: public async Task<BaseCommandResponse> Handle(UpdateEventCommand request, CancellationToken ct)
 923: {
 924:     // ... update logic ...
 925:     
 926:     // Invalidate the specific entity cache
 927:     await _hybridCache.RemoveAsync($"event:{request.Id}", ct);
 928:     
 929:     return response;
 930: }
 931: ```
 932: 
 933: ### 9.3. Caching Guidelines
 934: 
 935: | Feature | Use **Output Cache** | Use **Hybrid Cache** |
 936: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
 937: | **Public Public Data** (e.g., Event List) | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
 938: | **Authenticated Data** (e.g., "My Events") | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
 939: | **Lookup Tables** (e.g., Categories) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (if reused internally) |
 940: | **User-Specific Content** | ❌ No | ✅ Yes (Keyed by UserID) |
 941: | **Write Operations** | ❌ Never | ❌ Use to Invalidate |
 942: 
 943: ---

 975: |----------|----------|-------------|
 976: | Users | `/api/v1/user` | User management |
 977: | Actors | `/api/v1/actor` | Identity (user/org) actors |
 978: | Organization Members | `/api/v1/organizationmember` | Org membership |
 979: 
 980: ### Storage
 981: 
 982: | Resource | Endpoint | Description |
 983: |----------|----------|-------------|
 984: | Storage Objects | `/api/v1/storageobject` | File/image storage |
 985: 
 986: ---
 987: 
 988: ## 11. Multi-Tenancy
 989: 
 990: ### Tenant Header
 991: 
 992: All requests must include the tenant ID header:
 993: 
 994: ```
 995: X-Tenant-Id: 018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001
 996: ```
 997: 
 998: ### Default Tenant
 999: 
1000: For single-instance deployments, use the default tenant:
1001: 
1002: ```
1003: 018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001
1004: ```
1005: 
1006: This MUST match across:
1007: - `{Project}.API/Services/TenantContext.cs`
1008: - `{Project}.Blazor/Program.cs` (YARP transform)
1009: - `{Project}.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs`
1010: - `{Project}.Persistence/SeedIds.cs`
1011: 
1012: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
1013: - `Explore.API/Services/TenantContext.cs`
1014: - `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs` (YARP transform)
1015: - `Explore.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs`
1016: - `Explore.Persistence/SeedIds.cs`
1017: 
1018: ### Tenant Context Service
1019: 
1020: ```csharp
1021: public interface ITenantContext
1022: {
1023:     Guid TenantId { get; }
1024: }
1025: 
1026: public class TenantContext : ITenantContext
1027: {
1028:     public const string DefaultTenantIdString = "018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001";
1029:     public static readonly Guid DefaultTenantId = Guid.Parse(DefaultTenantIdString);
1030: 
1031:     public Guid TenantId { get; }
1032: 
1033:     public TenantContext(IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor)
1034:     {
1035:         var header = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Headers["X-Tenant-Id"].FirstOrDefault();
1036:         TenantId = Guid.TryParse(header, out var tenantId) ? tenantId : DefaultTenantId;
1037:     }
1038: }
1039: ```
1040: 
1041: ### Global Query Filters
1042: 
1043: EF Core automatically filters all queries by tenant:
1044: 
1045: **Generic Template:**
1046: 
1047: ```csharp
1048: // In {DbContext}
1049: protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
1050: {
1051:     // Apply tenant filter to all entities with TenantId
1052:     modelBuilder.Entity<{Entity}>().HasQueryFilter(e => e.TenantId == _tenantContext.TenantId);
1053:     // ... etc for all tenant-scoped entities
1054: }
1055: ```
1056: 
1057: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
1058: 
1059: ```csharp
1060: // In ExploreDbContext
1061: protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
1062: {
1063:     // Apply tenant filter to all entities with TenantId
1064:     modelBuilder.Entity<Event>().HasQueryFilter(e => e.TenantId == _tenantContext.TenantId);
1065:     // ... etc for all tenant-scoped entities
1066: }
1067: ```
1068:
